P02CA.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Overboost Condition
P02CA.description: Boost pressure on the secondary turbocharger/supercharger (B) on a sequential or twin-charged setup is above the upper threshold. Wastegate stuck closed, VGT vanes stuck, or boost pressure sensor reads high.
symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P02CB.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Underboost Condition
P02CB.description: Boost pressure on the secondary turbocharger/supercharger (B) is below the lower threshold. Wastegate stuck open, charge-air leak, or VGT vanes stuck open.
symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P02CC.title: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Min Limit
P02CC.description: The PCM applies a per-cylinder injector offset (Mengenausgleich) to compensate for production-tolerance differences in injector flow rate. On cylinder 1 the learned correction has reached its minimum value — the injector is delivering significantly more fuel than the calibrated reference and the controller cannot trim it any further.

causes.cause: Injector over-delivering — worn nozzle or stuck-open seat
Calibration code not programmed after replacement

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P02CD.title: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Max Limit
P02CD.description: The per-cylinder injector offset on cylinder 1 has reached its maximum value — the injector is delivering significantly less fuel than the calibrated reference, and the controller cannot trim it any further.

causes.cause: Injector under-delivering — clogged nozzle or worn coil
Calibration code not programmed after replacement

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P02E0.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit/Open
P02E0.description: The drive circuit for the diesel intake air-flow control valve A is open. This valve (also called intake throttle, swirl flap actuator, or anti-shudder valve) closes the diesel intake to control airflow during regeneration and shutdown.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P02E1.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Performance
P02E1.description: Diesel intake air-flow control A is electrically OK but does not move the throttle plate as commanded — typically carbon buildup or seized actuator.

P02E2.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit Low
P02E2.description: Diesel intake air-flow control A drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P02E3.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit High
P02E3.description: Diesel intake air-flow control A drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P02E4.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Open
P02E4.description: Diesel intake throttle A is mechanically stuck open — anti-shudder function on shutdown will not work and DPF regen airflow control is lost.

causes.cause: Carbon buildup or broken return spring
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P02E5.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Closed
P02E5.description: Diesel intake throttle A is mechanically stuck closed — engine starves of intake air.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P02E6.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit
P02E6.description: A general electrical fault is reported on diesel intake throttle A position sensor — open, shorted, or out of plausibility.

P02E7.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P02E7.description: Position sensor reads in range but plausibility check fails — does not match commanded throttle position.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P02E8.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Low
P02E8.description: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P02E9.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit High
P02E9.description: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P02EA.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P02EA.description: Position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P02EB.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P02EB.description: Motor current draw of the diesel intake throttle A actuator does not match the calibrated map for the commanded position — high friction, partial short, or stiction from carbon.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P02EC.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control System - High Air Flow Detected
P02EC.description: Air flow through diesel intake throttle A is higher than the commanded set point — flap leaking past the seat or stuck partly open.

P02ED.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control System - Low Air Flow Detected
P02ED.description: Air flow through diesel intake throttle A is lower than the commanded set point — flap stuck partly closed.

P02EE.title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Range/Performance
P02EE.description: The cylinder 1 injector drive circuit is electrically OK but the response (current ramp, dwell time, or peak voltage) does not match the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or wiring corrosion.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P02EF.title: Cylinder 2 Injector Circuit Range/Performance
P02EF.description: The cylinder 2 injector drive circuit is electrically OK but the response (current ramp, dwell time, or peak voltage) does not match the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or wiring corrosion.

P02FA.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow Position Sensor Minimum/Maximum Stop Performance
P02FA.description: The diesel intake throttle position sensor does not reach the calibrated minimum or maximum stop value during a self-test sweep — typically sensor wear, mechanical stop misalignment, or a sticky throttle plate.

P02FB.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit/Open
P02FB.description: The drive circuit for the cold-start auxiliary fuel injector or the cold-start ECU output is open. Some diesels use an extra cold-start injector to inject fuel into the intake manifold during very cold starts.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P02FC.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit Low
P02FC.description: Cold-start injector drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P02FD.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit High
P02FD.description: Cold-start injector drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

P02FE.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit Range/Performance
P02FE.description: Cold-start injector drive is electrically OK but does not deliver the calibrated injection quantity — partial blockage or weak coil.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P02FF.title: Propulsion System Inactive Timer Performance
P02FF.description: The timer that monitors how long the propulsion system has been inactive (used by hybrid and stop-start strategies to schedule rebalancing tasks) is not behaving plausibly — typically a clock or PCM-state fault.

P0300.title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
P0300.description: The ECU has detected misfires that are not concentrated on a single cylinder. The misfire monitor measures crankshaft acceleration after each combustion event; missing acceleration on multiple cylinders, or randomly across cylinders, triggers this code.
symptoms: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

P0301.title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
P0301.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 1. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression.

causes.cause: Spark plug for cylinder 1 worn or fouled

symptoms: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

P0302.title: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
P0302.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 2. Diagnostic approach is identical to P0301 — swap the suspect coil or plug with a known-good cylinder and see if the misfire follows.

causes.cause: Spark plug for cylinder 2 worn or fouled

symptoms: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

P0303.title: Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected
P0303.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 3. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression. Verify by swapping the suspected coil/plug to a different cylinder; if the code follows, the part is bad.

causes.cause: Spark plug for cylinder 3 worn or fouled

symptoms: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

P0304.title: Cylinder 4 Misfire Detected
P0304.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 4. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression. causes.cause: Spark plug for cylinder 4 worn or fouled

symptoms: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

P0305.title: Cylinder 5 Misfire Detected
P0305.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 5 (only present on engines with 5+ cylinders). Same diagnostic approach as P0301 — swap the suspect coil/plug with another cylinder.
symptoms: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

P030A.title: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit/Open
P030A.description: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit/Open: the circuit is open. This line drives an ignition coil group; a fault causes misfire on those cylinders.

causes.cause: Open wire between PCM and coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P030B.title: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit Low
P030B.description: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. This line drives an ignition coil group; a fault causes misfire on those cylinders.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P030C.title: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit High
P030C.description: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. This line drives an ignition coil group; a fault causes misfire on those cylinders.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P030D.title: Ignition B Control Signal Circuit/Open
P030D.description: The ignition B control signal circuit is open — typically the PCM drive line for the first ignition coil group has lost continuity.

causes.cause: Open wire between PCM and coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P030E.description: Ignition B control signal stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

symptoms: Check engine light on or flashing

P0313.title: Misfire Detected with Low Fuel
P0313.description: Misfires are detected while the fuel level is low. The ECM disables further misfire reporting under this condition because intermittent fuel starvation can cause false positives in catalyst-damaging logic.
symptoms: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

P0314.title: Single Cylinder Misfire — Cylinder Not Specified
P0314.description: A persistent misfire is detected on one cylinder, but the engine controller cannot identify which cylinder is affected. Often seen on engines without per-cylinder feedback or when crank position correlation fails.

causes.cause: Weak ignition component on one cylinder

symptoms: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

P0315.title: Crankshaft Position System Variation Not Learned
P0315.description: The PCM has not yet learned the crankshaft position variation table required for accurate misfire detection. After flywheel/sensor replacement or PCM relearn, a procedure must be performed (typically deceleration from a defined RPM with closed throttle).

P0316.title: Engine Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)
P0316.description: The misfire monitor detected misfires during the first 1000 revolutions after startup but the engine then settled. Often caused by fouled spark plugs that warm up clean, weak ignition coils, or a borderline cold-start fuel mixture.

causes.cause: Ignition coil weak below operating temperature
Cold-start mixture too lean (fuel pressure, leaking injectors at rest)

symptoms: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

P0317.title: Rough Road Hardware Not Present
P0317.description: The PCM has been configured to use rough-road sensor input for misfire detection (to mask false positives on bumpy surfaces) but the expected hardware is not detected on the network. Typically a configuration mismatch after replacement.

causes.cause: PCM configuration does not match installed hardware

P0318.title: Rough Road Sensor A Signal Circuit
P0318.description: A general electrical fault is reported on rough-road sensor A — used to gate misfire detection so that engine vibration from rough roads is not misclassified as misfire.

P0319.title: Rough Road Sensor B Signal Circuit
P0319.description: A general electrical fault is reported on rough-road sensor B — used to gate misfire detection so that engine vibration from rough roads is not misclassified as misfire.

P031A.title: Ignition C Control Signal Circuit/Open
P031A.description: The ignition C control signal circuit is open — typically the PCM drive line for the first ignition coil group has lost continuity.

causes.cause: Open wire between PCM and coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P031B.title: Ignition C Control Signal Circuit Low
P031B.description: Ignition C control signal stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P031C.title: Ignition C Control Signal Circuit High
P031C.description: Ignition C control signal stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P031D.title: Ignition D Control Signal Circuit/Open
P031D.description: The ignition D control signal circuit is open — typically the PCM drive line for the first ignition coil group has lost continuity.

causes.cause: Open wire between PCM and coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P031E.title: Ignition D Control Signal Circuit Low
P031E.description: Ignition D control signal stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P031F.title: Ignition D Control Signal Circuit High
P031F.description: Ignition D control signal stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0320.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit
P0320.description: A general electrical fault is reported on the engine speed input from the ignition/distributor — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. On older systems this is the distributor pickup; on newer ones it is the crank/cam-derived speed signal feeding the ignition driver.

P0321.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit Range/Performance
P0321.description: Engine speed input from the ignition/distributor is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — slow response, drift, or noise.

causes.cause: Sensor drift or pickup gap wrong
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0322.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit No Signal
P0322.description: No engine speed signal from the ignition/distributor — open circuit, dead pickup, or sensor air gap too wide.

causes.cause: Pickup dead or air gap excessive

P0323.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit Intermittent
P0323.description: Engine speed input signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or wiring issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0324.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Control System Error
P0324.description: The knock-control subsystem reports an internal error — typically a self-test fault or a noise floor that cannot be calibrated. The system protects against detonation by retarding ignition; with this fault knock control is disabled.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P0325.title: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1)
P0325.description: A general fault has been detected in the bank 1 knock sensor circuit. The ECU uses the knock sensor to detect pre-ignition and retards ignition timing when knock occurs; with no signal, the ECU runs conservative timing and loses power.

causes.cause: Sensor mounting bolt loose (sensor must be torqued correctly)

symptoms: Power loss from defensive spark retard

P0326.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0326.description: Knock sensor A signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

P0327.title: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit Low Input (Bank 1)
P0327.description: The knock sensor signal voltage is below the expected range. Usually points to a piezoelectric sensor that has lost its output, or a short to ground in the signal line.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss from defensive spark retard

P0328.title: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit High Input (Bank 1)
P0328.description: The knock sensor signal voltage is above the expected range. Often caused by a sensor producing excess output due to mechanical noise (loose mounting, accessory drive vibration) rather than a sensor fault.

causes.cause: Mechanical noise picked up by sensor (loose accessory)
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage

symptoms: Power loss from defensive spark retard

P0329.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0329.description: Knock sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P032A.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit
P032A.description: A general electrical fault on knock sensor C — used on engines with multiple knock sensors (one per bank or per cylinder pair).

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P032B.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P032B.description: Knock sensor C signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P032C.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit Low
P032C.description: Knock sensor C signal below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P032D.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit High
P032D.description: Knock sensor C signal above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P032E.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit Intermittent
P032E.description: Knock sensor C signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P032F.title: Combustion Engine Producing Insufficient Torque
P032F.description: The engine torque measured (or modelled from intake/exhaust signals) is below the calibrated set point for the commanded throttle position. Causes range from low compression, intake leak, fuel pressure issue, ignition fault, to high mechanical drag.

causes.cause: Low compression on one or more cylinders

P0330.title: Knock Sensor 2 Circuit (Bank 2)
P0330.description: A general electrical fault in the bank 2 knock sensor circuit. The ECU monitors a piezoelectric sensor for engine vibration patterns associated with detonation; an open, shorted, or out-of-range circuit triggers this code.
symptoms: Power loss from defensive spark retard

P0331.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0331.description: Knock sensor B signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P0332.title: Knock Sensor 2 Circuit Low Input (Bank 2)
P0332.description: Knock sensor 2 (bank 2) reports a signal level below the diagnostic threshold. The sensor is a piezo element bolted to the engine block; output should be a small AC voltage on each combustion event. A cold or open sensor reads 0 V; a loose mounting bolt damps the signal. Without knock detection, the ECM retards spark globally as a safety measure — fuel economy and power suffer.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss from defensive spark retard

P0333.title: Knock Sensor 2 Circuit High Input (Bank 2)
P0333.description: The bank 2 knock sensor signal is above the expected voltage range. Typically caused by a short to supply voltage or an internal sensor fault.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss from defensive spark retard

P0334.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P0334.description: Knock sensor B signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P0335.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Malfunction
P0335.description: The crankshaft position (CKP) sensor signal is missing or implausible. The CKP is essential — without it the ECU cannot synchronise injection or ignition, and the engine will not start or will stall.

causes.cause: Reluctor ring damaged or contaminated with metal debris

P0336.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance
P0336.description: The CKP signal is present but inconsistent with engine RPM, or pulse counts deviate from the reluctor's expected pattern. Often points to a damaged tooth on the reluctor or an air gap that has changed.

P0337.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Low Input
P0337.description: The CKP signal voltage is below the lower threshold. Usually a sensor whose internal coil has degraded, or a wiring short to ground.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0338.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit High Input
P0338.description: The CKP signal voltage is above the upper threshold. Either a sensor producing excess output or a short to supply voltage.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0339.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0339.description: The crankshaft position sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector, sensor air gap, or damaged tone wheel. The PCM may detect a "false" stall or misfire spike when the signal drops.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P033A.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit
P033A.description: A general electrical fault on knock sensor D — used on engines with multiple knock sensors (one per bank or per cylinder pair).

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P033B.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance
P033B.description: Knock sensor D signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P033C.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Low
P033C.description: Knock sensor D signal below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P033D.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit High
P033D.description: Knock sensor D signal above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P033E.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Intermittent
P033E.description: Knock sensor D signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P033F.title: Crankshaft/Camshaft Loss Of Synchronization
P033F.description: The PCM has lost crank-to-cam synchronization — the relative phase between crankshaft and camshaft no longer matches the calibrated reference. Causes include a stretched or jumped timing chain, broken cam timing tooth, or sensor signal corruption.

causes.cause: Crank or cam sensor signal corrupted

P0340.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)
P0340.description: The camshaft position (CMP) sensor signal is missing or implausible. The ECU uses CMP together with CKP to identify cylinder phase for sequential injection and coil-on-plug ignition; without CMP the engine may run on group injection or fail to start.

causes.cause: Timing chain stretched, throwing off sensor timing

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P0341.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P0341.description: The CMP signal is present but its phase relative to the crankshaft is outside tolerance. On engines with variable valve timing, this code often appears together with VVT solenoid faults.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P0342.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Low Input (Bank 1)
P0342.description: The CMP signal voltage is below the lower threshold. Most often a sensor with degraded internal output or a short to ground.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P0343.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit High Input (Bank 1)
P0343.description: The CMP signal voltage is above the upper threshold. Either excessive sensor output or a short to supply voltage.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P0344.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)
P0344.description: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 or Single Sensor): the signal is intermittent or erratic. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P0345.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit (Bank 2)
P0345.description: General electrical fault in the bank 2 camshaft position sensor circuit. The ECU uses this signal together with the crank sensor for sequential injection and ignition timing.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P0346.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P0346.description: The bank 2 camshaft position sensor signal is present but does not match the crank reference correctly, or its pulse pattern is implausible.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P0347.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P0347.description: Camshaft position sensor A on bank 2 reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P0348.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit High (Bank 2)
P0348.description: Camshaft position sensor A on bank 2 reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P0349.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
P0349.description: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2): the signal is intermittent or erratic. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P034A.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor - Crankshaft Start Position Incorrect
P034A.description: At engine start the crankshaft position reported by the sensor does not match the calibrated start window — typically a wrong tone-wheel installation, sensor air gap, or PCM not synchronised after a relearn.

causes.cause: Tone wheel misindexed or relearn pending

P034B.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor - Crankshaft Direction Incorrect
P034B.description: The crankshaft is rotating in the wrong direction relative to the expected reference — typically only seen on stop-start systems where the engine briefly counter-rotates after shutdown.

P034C.title: Ion Sense System Performance
P034C.description: Some engines (notably Saab and some Mazda direct-injection units) use the spark plug as an ion-current sensor after spark to detect knock and misfire. This code reports a performance issue with the ion-sense input — typically a worn plug, loose secondary connection, or aged ion-sense module.

P0350.title: Ignition Coil Primary/Secondary Circuit/Open
P0350.description: A general open-circuit fault has been detected on an ignition coil's primary or secondary winding (no specific cylinder identified). This code is set when the PCM cannot localise the fault to a single coil.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0351.title: Ignition Coil "A" Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 1)
P0351.description: An electrical fault is detected in both the primary and the secondary circuit of ignition coil A (cylinder 1). The ECU cannot drive the coil correctly, so the cylinder served by coil A misfires or does not fire at all. Causes: an open or shorted primary control wire, an internal coil winding fault, a failed igniter/driver, or wiring or connector damage at the coil.

causes.cause: Coil primary winding open or shorted

P0352.title: Ignition Coil "B" Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 2)
P0352.description: An electrical fault has been detected in the ignition coil circuit for cylinder 2 — open primary winding, short to ground, or short to supply. The ECU disables the coil to protect its driver and the cylinder misfires.

causes.cause: Coil primary winding open or shorted

P0353.title: Ignition Coil "C" Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 3)
P0353.description: An electrical fault has been detected in the ignition coil circuit for cylinder 3 — open primary winding, short to ground, or short to supply. The ECU disables the coil to protect its driver and the cylinder misfires.

causes.cause: Coil primary winding open or shorted

P0354.title: Ignition Coil "D" Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 4)
P0354.description: An electrical fault has been detected in the ignition coil circuit for cylinder 4 — open primary winding, short to ground, or short to supply. The ECU disables the coil to protect its driver and the cylinder misfires.

Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0363.title: Misfire Detected - Fueling Disabled
P0363.description: Severe misfire detected — the PCM has disabled fuel injection on the affected cylinder(s) to protect the catalyst from raw fuel. Common protective response on heavy or sustained misfire conditions.

causes.cause: Severe misfire — read companion P030x codes

symptoms: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

P0364.title: DC/AC Converter Control Module Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0364.description: The control circuit for the DC/AC converter (used in plug-in hybrid and EV traction systems to convert DC battery voltage to 3-phase AC for the motor) reports a performance issue. This is part of the high-voltage drivetrain.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0365.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit (Bank 1)
P0365.description: A general electrical fault on camshaft position sensor B (typically the exhaust cam) on bank 1 — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. Required for variable valve timing on the exhaust cam.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P0366.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P0366.description: Cam sensor B on bank 1 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response, drift, or signal does not match expected cam profile.

P03E5.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit (Bank 1)
P03E5.description: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit (Bank 1): an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P03E6.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P03E6.description: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Range/Performance (Bank 1): the signal is implausible or outside the valid range. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P03E7.description: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit Low (Bank 1): the signal voltage is below the expected range. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P03E9.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator Position Sensor A Exceeded Learning Limit
P03E9.description: The adaptive learning offset for camshaft profile actuator A position sensor A has reached its learning limit. Long-term mechanical wear of the cam profile lock pin or oil control valve.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P03EA.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator Position Sensor B Exceeded Learning Limit
P03EA.description: The adaptive learning offset for camshaft profile actuator A position sensor B has reached its learning limit. Long-term mechanical wear of the cam profile lock pin or oil control valve.

P03EB.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator Position Sensor C Exceeded Learning Limit
P03EB.description: The adaptive learning offset for camshaft profile actuator A position sensor C has reached its learning limit. Long-term mechanical wear of the cam profile lock pin or oil control valve.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P03EC.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1)
P03EC.description: The drive circuit for cam profile actuator A in position C on bank 1 is open. Three-stage cam profile systems use a separate control valve per profile position.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P03ED.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P03ED.description: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Circuit Low (Bank 1): the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P03EE.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Circuit High (Bank 1)

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P03EF.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Performance/Stuck Off (Bank 1)
P03EF.description: Cam profile actuator A position C is electrically OK but does not engage when commanded. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.

causes.cause: Lock pin or oil supply restricted
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P03F0.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Stuck On (Bank 1)
P03F0.description: Cam profile actuator A position C is stuck engaged when commanded off — typically a stuck oil control valve.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P0400.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Malfunction
P0400.description: A general fault has been detected in the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system. EGR routes a portion of exhaust back into the intake to reduce combustion temperature and NOx emissions. Most EGR codes today are caused by carbon buildup blocking the valve.

P0401.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Insufficient Detected
P0401.description: When the ECU commands EGR open, the actual flow measured by the DPFE sensor or the resulting MAP/MAF change is below threshold. By far the most common cause is a carboned-up EGR valve or blocked intake passages.

causes.cause: EGR valve clogged or stuck closed
Intake EGR passages blocked with carbon
Vacuum line to EGR (vacuum-actuated valves) cracked

P0402.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Excessive Detected
P0402.description: EGR flow is higher than expected when the valve should be closed, or higher than commanded when partially open. Typically a valve that has stuck open due to carbon, causing rough idle and stalling.

causes.cause: Valve seat eroded — does not seal

P0403.title: EGR Control Circuit
P0403.description: The control circuit for the EGR valve solenoid is open or shorted. The ECM cannot drive the valve to the commanded position.

P0404.title: EGR Range/Performance
P0404.description: The EGR valve does not move through its expected range or its position feedback does not track command. The valve may be sticking, the position sensor may be drifting or carbon buildup is preventing full travel.

P0405.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit Low
P0405.description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0406.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit High
P0406.description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0407.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit Low
P0407.description: The signal from EGR position or pressure sensor B is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Indicates a short to ground, open signal wire or sensor fault.

P0408.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit Low
P0408.description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

P0409.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit High

P040A.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P040A.description: A general electrical fault on EGR temperature sensor A — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. The sensor monitors recirculated exhaust gas temperature for EGR cooler protection and dosing.

P040B.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P040B.description: EGR temperature sensor A reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P040C.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P040C.description: EGR temperature sensor A below lower plausibility — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P040D.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P040D.description: EGR temperature sensor A above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P040E.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P040E.description: EGR temperature sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P040F.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A/B Correlation
P040F.description: EGR temperature sensors A and B disagree by more than the allowed tolerance over a drive cycle. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P0410.title: Secondary Air Injection System Malfunction
P0410.description: A general fault in the secondary air injection system. The system pumps fresh air into the exhaust during cold start to accelerate catalyst light-off; common faults are a seized pump, blocked passages or a stuck valve.

causes.cause: Air pump seized (water ingress is a common cause)

P0411.title: Secondary Air Injection System Incorrect Flow
P0411.description: When the ECU commands secondary air injection, the actual flow measured by the front oxygen sensor (or a dedicated mass flow meter) does not match the expected value. Usually a partially blocked passage or a leaking combi valve.

causes.cause: Air passages in cylinder head clogged with carbon

P0412.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit
P0412.description: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0413.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit Open
P0413.description: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit Open: the circuit is open. Likely a broken wire, disconnected connector, or failed component.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0414.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve "A" Circuit Shorted
P0414.description: The ECU detected a short circuit in the secondary air injection switching valve A control circuit. With the valve unable to switch correctly, the cold-start emissions strategy fails and the catalyst takes longer to reach light-off.

P0415.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit
P0415.description: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0416.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit Open
P0416.description: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit Open: the circuit is open. Likely a broken wire, disconnected connector, or failed component.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0417.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit Shorted
P0417.description: AIR switching valve B drive circuit shorted to ground or B+.

P0418.title: Secondary Air Injection System Relay "A" Circuit Malfunction
P0418.description: General electrical fault in the secondary air injection pump relay A circuit. Without the relay, the air pump cannot be commanded and the system cannot complete its cold-start function.

P0419.title: Secondary Air Injection System Control B Circuit
P0419.description: A general electrical fault on AIR system control circuit B (typically the AIR pump driver line on the second pump or relay).

P041A.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit
P041A.description: A general electrical fault on EGR temperature sensor B — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. The sensor monitors recirculated exhaust gas temperature for EGR cooler protection and dosing.

P041B.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P041B.description: EGR temperature sensor B reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P041C.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
P041C.description: EGR temperature sensor B below lower plausibility — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P041D.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
P041D.description: EGR temperature sensor B above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P041E.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P041E.description: EGR temperature sensor B signal jumps or drops out intermittently. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P041F.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit Low
P041F.description: AIR switching valve A drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0420.title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P0420.description: The oxygen storage capacity of the main catalytic converter on bank 1 has degraded below the OBD threshold. The downstream oxygen sensor signal increasingly mirrors the upstream sensor, indicating reduced conversion efficiency.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0421.title: Warm Up Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P0421.description: The pre-cat (warm-up) catalyst on bank 1 has lost too much oxygen storage capacity. Its primary purpose — quickly reaching light-off after a cold start — is no longer met within the OBD limits.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0422.title: Main Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P0422.description: Generic main catalyst efficiency code on bank 1 — used by some manufacturers in addition to or instead of P0420. Indicates the same root cause — degraded oxygen storage in the main catalyst.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0423.title: Heated Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P0423.description: Heated (electrically warmed) catalyst on bank 1 fails efficiency monitoring. In addition to standard catalyst aging, faults in the catalyst heater control or supply can cause this code.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0424.title: Heated Catalyst Temperature Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P0424.description: The heated catalyst on bank 1 does not reach its target temperature within the expected time. Common causes are a defective heater element, supply fault, or a damaged temperature sensor.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0425.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P0425.description: General electrical fault detected in the catalyst temperature sensor on bank 1 sensor position 1. The ECU uses this signal to manage heater control and protect the catalyst from overtemperature.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0426.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0426.description: Catalyst temperature sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0427.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0427.description: Catalyst temperature sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0428.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0428.description: Catalyst temperature sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0429.title: Catalyst Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1)
P0429.description: The drive circuit for the heated catalyst on bank 1 is open. Heated catalysts use an electrical heating element to reach light-off temperature within seconds of cold start.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P042A.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P042A.description: A general electrical fault on the catalyst temperature sensor at bank 1 sensor 2.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P042B.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P042B.description: Catalyst temperature sensor at bank 1 sensor 2 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P042F.title: EGR A Control Stuck Closed
P042F.description: EGR A Control Stuck Closed: the control module has detected this fault condition. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P0430.title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P0430.description: Same condition as P0420 but on bank 2. On engines with one shared catalyst per bank, P0420 and P0430 appearing together usually point to age rather than damage.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0431.title: Warm Up Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P0431.description: The pre-cat (warm-up) catalyst on bank 2 has lost too much oxygen storage capacity. Its primary purpose — quickly reaching light-off after a cold start — is no longer met within the OBD limits.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0432.title: Main Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P0432.description: Generic main catalyst efficiency code on bank 2 — used by some manufacturers in addition to or instead of P0420. Indicates the same root cause — degraded oxygen storage in the main catalyst.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0433.title: Heated Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P0433.description: Heated (electrically warmed) catalyst on bank 2 fails efficiency monitoring. In addition to standard catalyst aging, faults in the catalyst heater control or supply can cause this code.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0434.title: Heated Catalyst Temperature Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P0434.description: The heated catalyst on bank 2 has not reached its calibrated light-off temperature within the expected time after engine start. Heater element weak or insufficient supply.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0435.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0435.description: A general electrical fault on the catalyst temperature sensor at bank 2 sensor 1.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0436.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0436.description: Catalyst temperature sensor at bank 2 sensor 1 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P043A.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P043A.description: A general electrical fault on the catalyst temperature sensor at bank 2 sensor 2.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P043E.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Reference Orifice Low Flow
P043E.description: During the EVAP leak-detection self-test, the calibration airflow through the reference orifice is below the expected rate. The orifice may be partially blocked.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P043F.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Reference Orifice High Flow
P043F.description: During the leak-detection self-test, airflow through the reference orifice is above the expected rate — typically a leak around the orifice or a damaged seal.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0440.title: Evaporative Emission Control System Malfunction
P0440.description: A general fault in the evaporative emission (EVAP) system has been detected. The system seals the fuel tank and captures fuel vapour in a charcoal canister; this code indicates a failed leak test or sensor without identifying the specific failure.

causes.cause: Fuel filler cap loose or worn
Purge valve stuck open or closed

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0441.title: Evaporative Emission System Incorrect Purge Flow
P0441.description: The actual purge flow does not match the commanded value. Usually a purge valve stuck closed (no flow) or stuck open (too much flow at idle). Distinct from a leak code.

causes.cause: Purge valve stuck open or closed

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0442.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Small Leak)
P0442.description: A small leak (typically equivalent to a 0.040 inch / 1.0 mm orifice) has been detected in the EVAP system. By far the most common cause is a fuel cap that is loose, missing, or has a worn seal.

causes.cause: Fuel cap loose, missing, or worn seal

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0443.title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit
P0443.description: Electrical fault in the EVAP purge solenoid circuit. The ECU detects an open, shorted, or out-of-range condition on the purge valve driver.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0444.title: Evaporative Emission Purge Control Valve Circuit Open
P0444.description: The ECU has detected an open circuit in the purge solenoid control line — usually a broken wire, unplugged connector, or open coil winding.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0445.title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Shorted
P0445.description: The ECU detected a short in the EVAP purge solenoid control circuit. With the valve permanently energized or shorted, the system can either over-purge causing rich running, or stay closed.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0446.title: Evaporative Emission Vent Control Circuit Malfunction
P0446.description: A fault in the EVAP vent valve circuit. The vent valve seals the canister against atmosphere during the leak test; without it, the test cannot pull a vacuum and may set false leak codes alongside.

causes.cause: Vent valve seized or contaminated by water/dirt

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0447.title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit Open
P0447.description: The ECU detected an open circuit on the EVAP vent valve control. The vent valve is needed to seal the system for leak diagnostics; with the circuit open the leak test cannot complete.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0448.title: EVAP System Vent Control Circuit Shorted
P0448.description: EVAP vent valve drive circuit shorted to ground or B+. The vent valve seals the canister during pressure-test diagnostics.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0449.title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve/Solenoid Circuit Malfunction
P0449.description: A general electrical fault was detected in the EVAP vent valve/solenoid control circuit. Without a working vent valve the EVAP leak test cannot complete and the system may remain not-ready.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P044A.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit
P044A.description: EGR Sensor C Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

P044B.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P044B.description: EGR Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance: the signal is implausible or outside the valid range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P044C.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit Low
P044C.description: EGR sensor C below lower plausibility — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P044D.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit High
P044D.description: EGR sensor C above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P044E.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P044E.description: EGR sensor C signal jumps or drops out intermittently. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P044F.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit High
P044F.description: AIR switching valve A drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0450.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0450.description: A general electrical fault on EVAP pressure sensor/switch A — used to monitor canister pressure during leak-detection diagnostics.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0451.title: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0451.description: The fuel tank pressure sensor reading is implausible — for example, fluctuating signal, noise, or values that do not respond to known pressure events such as a key-on tank refill.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0452.title: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor Low Input
P0452.description: The fuel tank pressure sensor signal is below the expected minimum voltage. Often caused by a failed sensor or a short to ground in the signal line.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0453.title: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor High Input
P0453.description: The fuel tank pressure sensor signal is above the expected maximum voltage, typical of a short to supply or a sensor that has failed high.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0454.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent
P0454.description: EVAP pressure sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0455.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
P0455.description: A large leak has been detected during the EVAP system pressure or vacuum test — large enough that the system cannot hold pressure for the diagnostic interval. Typically a missing fuel cap, disconnected hose, or split canister.

causes.cause: Fuel cap missing or not seated

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0456.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Very Small Leak)
P0456.description: A very small leak (typically equivalent to a 0.020 inch / 0.5 mm orifice) has been detected. Smaller threshold than P0442; intermittent and often weather-dependent. Modern OBD-II requires this monitor on most vehicles since model year 2000.

causes.cause: Fuel cap seal hardened or worn
Purge or vent valve leaking slightly

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0457.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Fuel Cap Loose/Off)
P0457.description: The EVAP system detected a large leak that strongly correlates with a missing or improperly closed fuel filler cap. After re-tightening the cap, the code clears once the readiness monitor completes.

causes.cause: Fuel cap loose, missing, or worn seal

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0458.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Low
P0458.description: EVAP purge control valve A drive line stuck low — short to ground. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0459.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit High
P0459.description: EVAP purge control valve A drive line stuck high — short to B+. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P045A.title: EGR B Control Circuit
P045A.description: A general electrical fault on EGR control circuit B — second EGR valve on engines with high-pressure and low-pressure EGR loops.

P045B.title: EGR B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P045B.description: EGR valve B is electrically OK but does not respond as commanded — typically carbon buildup or sticking actuator.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P045C.title: EGR B Control Circuit Low

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0460.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit
P0460.description: A general electrical fault on the primary fuel-level sensor (A) — open, shorted, or out of plausibility.

P0461.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0461.description: Fuel-level sensor A reads in range but plausibility check fails — value sticks, jumps, or does not match consumption.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0462.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Low

P0465.title: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit

P046A.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 1)
P046A.description: Catalyst temperature sensors 1 and 2 on bank 1 disagree by more than the allowed tolerance over a drive cycle.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P046B.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 2)
P046B.description: Catalyst temperature sensors 1 and 2 on bank 2 disagree by more than the allowed tolerance over a drive cycle.

P0470.description: A general electrical fault on exhaust pressure sensor A — used to monitor backpressure across the DPF or to control variable-geometry turbo.

P0471.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance

P0475.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A
P0475.description: A general fault on exhaust pressure control valve A — used as a backpressure brake on heavy-duty diesels and to assist DPF regeneration by raising exhaust temperature.

P0476.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Range/Performance
P0476.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A is electrically OK but does not move as commanded.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0477.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Low
P0477.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A drive line stuck low — short to ground.

P0478.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A High
P0478.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A drive line stuck high — short to B+.

P0479.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Intermittent
P0479.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A drive signal is unstable.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P047A.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P047A.description: A general electrical fault on exhaust pressure sensor B — used to monitor backpressure across the DPF or to control variable-geometry turbo.

P047B.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P047B.description: Exhaust pressure sensor B reads in range but plausibility check fails. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

P047F.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Stuck Open
P047F.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A is mechanically stuck open — backpressure cannot be raised, exhaust brake and DPF regen support fail.

causes.cause: Carbon buildup or broken return spring
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P0480.title: Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit
P0480.description: Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault. Reduced cooling-fan control can let the engine or A/C condenser overheat.

P0481.title: Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit
P0481.description: Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault. Reduced cooling-fan control can let the engine or A/C condenser overheat.

P0482.title: Cooling Fan 3 Control Circuit Malfunction
P0482.description: Electrical fault detected in the third cooling fan control circuit. With one stage of cooling lost, engine and A/C condenser cooling capacity is reduced, particularly at low vehicle speeds.

P0483.title: Cooling Fan Rationality Check
P0483.description: The ECM detects that the cooling fan response does not match command. Either the fan rotates without command, fails to rotate when commanded or its current draw is implausible.

P0484.title: Cooling Fan Current Too High
P0484.description: The current draw of the cooling fan exceeds the permitted maximum. Caused by a seized or worn fan motor or wiring shorted to ground at high load.

P0485.title: Cooling Fan Power/Ground Circuit
P0485.description: A fault is detected in the supply or ground path of the cooling fan circuit. Voltage drops or open ground prevent reliable fan operation.

P0486.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit
P0486.description: A general electrical fault on EGR sensor B — second EGR sensor on dual-loop or HP/LP EGR systems. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P0487.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A/Open
P0487.description: The drive circuit of EGR throttle A is open. EGR throttles partially close intake to increase exhaust gas recirculation flow at low loads.

P0488.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P0488.description: EGR throttle A is electrically OK but does not move as commanded. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0489.title: EGR A Control Circuit Low
P0489.description: EGR A drive line stuck low — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P048A.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Stuck Closed
P048A.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A is mechanically stuck closed — backpressure runs away, can stall the engine.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P048B.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit
P048B.description: A general electrical fault on the position sensor of exhaust pressure control valve A.

P048C.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P048C.description: Position sensor reads in range but plausibility check fails. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P048D.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P048D.description: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P048E.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P048E.description: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P048F.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P048F.description: Position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0490.title: EGR A Control Circuit High
P0490.description: EGR A drive line stuck high — short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0491.title: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 1)
P0491.description: AIR system flow on bank 1 is below threshold during the cold-start self-test — typically a clogged check valve, leaking hose, or weak air pump.

P0492.title: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 2)
P0492.description: AIR system flow on bank 2 is below threshold during the cold-start self-test — typically a clogged check valve, leaking hose, or weak air pump.

P0493.title: Fan Overspeed
P0493.description: Fan Overspeed: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.cause: Fan relay welded closed - fan runs uncontrolled

P0494.title: Fan 1 Underspeed
P0494.description: Cooling fan 1 is rotating slower than commanded. The ECU sees the tachometer feedback below the expected window for the requested duty cycle - usually a worn fan motor, a high-resistance harness or feed, or a partially seized impeller.

causes.cause: Fan 1 motor worn or brushes degraded

P0495.title: Fan 1 Overspeed
P0495.description: Fan 1 Overspeed: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0496.title: Evaporative Emission System High Purge Flow
P0496.description: The ECU detected EVAP purge flow during a non-purge condition, or higher than commanded purge flow. Typical causes are a stuck-open purge valve or a damaged vent system that draws unmetered air.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0497.title: EVAP System Low Purge Flow
P0497.description: The evaporative emissions system measures purge flow either via a dedicated purge flow sensor or via short-term fuel trim response when the purge valve opens. The flow is significantly lower than expected for the commanded purge rate - typically a clogged purge line, a stuck purge valve, or a leaking vapor canister vent.

causes.cause: Purge line restricted by debris or kinks

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0498.title: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit Low
P0498.description: The vent valve closes the EVAP canister to atmosphere during leak tests. The control line for that valve is shorted to ground - the ECU drives the valve and measures voltage below the expected level, indicating either a harness short or an internal solenoid short.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P0499.title: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit High
