P0499.description: Same as P0498 with the control line open or shorted to supply. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P049A.title: EGR B Flow
P049A.description: The exhaust-gas recirculation system has a second EGR loop (B) - typically used on engines with a dedicated low-pressure EGR for emissions or on twin-bank V engines. The ECU detects an EGR B flow fault - the measured or modelled flow does not match the requested rate, without yet diagnosing it as too low or too high.

causes.cause: EGR valve B sticking due to soot

P049B.title: EGR B Flow Insufficient Detected
P049B.description: Same as P049A but specifically with measured flow below the required rate - typically EGR valve sticking closed or cooler heavily clogged.

causes.cause: EGR cooler B heavily clogged with soot

P049C.title: EGR B Flow Excessive Detected
P049C.description: Same as P049A but with measured flow above the required rate - typically EGR valve sticking open or position sensor offset low.

P049D.title: EGR A Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P049D.description: EGR A Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.cause: Heavy carbon deposits on EGR A seat

P049E.title: EGR B Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P049E.description: EGR B Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.cause: Heavy carbon deposits on EGR B seat

P049F.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B
P049F.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the second exhaust pressure control valve (B) - used for example on dual exhaust brakes, twin-bank diesels with separate back-pressure flaps, or for DPF regeneration backpressure assist on the second bank. The ECU loses control of this stage.

causes.cause: Open in harness or actuator winding
Connector corroded by exhaust heat or moisture

P04A0.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Range or Performance
P04A0.description: Same as P049F with feedback in plausible range yet not matching the engine model - actuator slow, slipping or position sensor offset.

P04A1.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Low
P04A1.description: Same as P049F with the control line shorted to ground.

P04A2.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B High
P04A2.description: Same as P049F with the control line shorted to supply.

P04A3.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Intermittent
P04A3.description: Same as P049F with intermittent or erratic feedback - typically a connector or harness fault.

causes.cause: Intermittent contact at connector or terminal
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P04A4.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Stuck Open
P04A4.description: The exhaust pressure control valve B is mechanically stuck in the open position. The ECU commands closing for back-pressure assist or exhaust braking, but the position feedback shows it remains open - typically heavy soot, broken linkage, or a sticky valve shaft.

causes.cause: Valve stuck open due to soot or broken linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P04A5.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Stuck Closed
P04A5.description: Same as P04A4 but the valve B is stuck closed - back-pressure stays high even when the engine should run with low restriction; risk of overheating or excessive fuel consumption.

causes.cause: Valve stuck closed due to soot or broken linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P04A6.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit
P04A6.description: A circuit fault is detected on the position sensor of exhaust pressure control valve B. Without valid position feedback the ECU cannot run closed-loop control of the valve and falls back to a default substitute.

causes.cause: Open in sensor signal, supply or ground

P04A7.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P04A7.description: Same as P04A6 with the signal in plausible range but not matching the actual valve angle.

P04A8.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit Low
P04A8.description: Same as P04A6 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P04A9.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit High
P04A9.description: Same as P04A6 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P04AA.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04AA.description: Same as P04A6 with intermittent or erratic feedback - typically a connector or harness fault. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P04AB.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Circuit Open
P04AB.description: The second EVAP purge control valve (B) - used on systems with a divided purge path or on twin-bank engines - shows an open control circuit. The ECU cannot drive the valve, so vapor cannot be purged through this stage; tank pressure may rise and emissions diagnostics fail.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04AC.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Circuit Low
P04AC.description: Same as P04AB with the control line shorted to ground. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04AD.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Circuit High
P04AD.description: Same as P04AB with the control line shorted to supply. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04AE.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Performance Stuck Open
P04AE.description: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Performance Stuck Open: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

causes.cause: Debris on valve seat prevents full closing
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04AF.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Stuck Closed
P04AF.description: Same as P04AE but the valve B is stuck closed - no vapor purge possible through this stage, leading to elevated tank pressure and possible canister saturation.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04B0.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Circuit Open
P04B0.description: The refueling vapor control valve - typically part of the ORVR or capless fueling system - has an open control circuit. The valve directs fuel vapor from the tank into the canister during refueling and must open when the fuel filler is opened. Without it, vapor escapes during refueling and the system fails leak diagnostics.

causes.cause: Open in harness or solenoid winding
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P04B1.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Circuit Low
P04B1.description: Same as P04B0 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P04B2.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Circuit High
P04B2.description: Same as P04B0 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P04B3.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Performance Stuck Open
P04B3.description: The refueling vapor control valve is stuck open. Vapor pathways meant to be closed except during refueling stay permanently open, distorting EVAP leak diagnostics and allowing vapor flow even with the fuel cap closed.

causes.cause: Valve stuck open due to debris or weak spring
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P04B4.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Stuck Closed
P04B4.description: Same as P04B3 with the valve stuck closed - vapor cannot reach the canister during refueling, vapor escape from the filler is possible.

causes.cause: Valve stuck closed due to seal or debris
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P04B5.title: Fuel Fill Door Stuck Open
P04B5.description: On vehicles with a motorised fuel fill door (no manual lever) the actuator and position switch report that the door is mechanically stuck open. The motor cannot retract it, typically due to a frozen or dirty hinge, broken cable, or jammed actuator.

causes.cause: Hinge jammed by ice, dirt or debris
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P04B6.title: Fuel Fill Door Stuck Closed
P04B6.description: Same as P04B5 with the door stuck closed - the user cannot refuel until the fault is cleared.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P04B7.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04B7.description: The position sensor or switch on the fuel fill door reports an intermittent signal - opens and closes randomly without matching the actual door position. Typically a connector or chafed harness fault.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P04B8.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor Circuit
P04B8.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the fuel fill door position sensor or switch - the ECU cannot determine whether the door is open or closed. Usually an open in supply, signal or ground.

P04B9.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor Circuit Low
P04B9.description: Same as P04B8 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P04BA.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor Circuit High
P04BA.description: Same as P04B8 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P04BB.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Circuit Open
P04BB.description: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Circuit Open: the control circuit is open. Likely a broken wire, disconnected connector, or failed actuator.

causes.cause: Open in harness or actuator winding
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P04BC.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Range or Performance
P04BC.description: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Range or Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

causes.cause: Linkage binding due to dirt or ice

P04BD.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Circuit Low
P04BD.description: Same as P04BB with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P04BE.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Circuit High
P04BE.description: Same as P04BB with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P04BF.title: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Circuit Open
P04BF.description: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Circuit Open: the control circuit is open. Likely a broken wire, disconnected connector, or failed actuator.

causes.cause: Open in harness or actuator winding
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P04C0.title: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Range or Performance
P04C0.description: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Range or Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P04C1.title: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Circuit Low
P04C1.description: Same as P04BD on the unlock side. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P04C2.title: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Circuit High
P04C2.description: Same as P04BE on the unlock side. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P04C3.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Position Sensor Circuit
P04C3.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the fuel fill door lock position sensor or switch. Without it the ECU cannot determine whether the lock has actually engaged or released.

P04C4.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Position Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P04C4.description: Same as P04C3 with feedback in plausible range yet not matching the commanded lock state.

P04C5.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Position Sensor Circuit Low
P04C5.description: Same as P04C3 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P04C6.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Position Sensor Circuit High
P04C6.description: Same as P04C3 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P04C7.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04C7.description: Same as P04C3 with intermittent feedback. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P04C8.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Circuit
P04C8.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the open-request input - the button or switch the driver presses to release the fuel fill door. The ECU loses the request signal, so motorised release becomes unavailable.

P04C9.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Performance Stuck Off
P04C9.description: The open-request switch never registers an active state - either the contact stays open mechanically or the wiring is permanently broken. The driver cannot trigger door release.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P04CA.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Circuit Low
P04CA.description: Same as P04C8 with the signal voltage shorted to ground or constantly low. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P04CB.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Circuit High
P04CB.description: Same as P04C8 with the signal voltage shorted to supply or constantly high. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P04CC.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04CC.description: Same as P04C8 with intermittent or erratic signal - typically a connector or harness fault. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P04CD.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Stuck On
P04CD.description: The open-request switch is stuck in the active state - the ECU continuously reads a request to open the fuel fill door. Either the switch is mechanically held closed or the line is shorted to its active level.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P04CE.title: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit
P04CE.description: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.cause: Open in sensor signal, supply or ground

P04CF.title: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit Range or Performance
P04CF.description: Same as P04CE with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model - typically sensor drift or a slow response after engine warm-up.

P04D0.title: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit Low
P04D0.description: Same as P04CE with the signal voltage below the plausible range. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P04D1.title: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit High
P04D1.description: Same as P04CE with the signal voltage above the plausible range. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P04D2.title: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04D2.description: Same as P04CE with intermittent or erratic signal. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P04D3.title: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit
P04D3.description: The exhaust brake activation input - typically from a stalk lever, brake pedal switch, or vehicle bus message - shows a circuit fault. The ECU cannot accept a request to engage the exhaust brake, which limits engine braking on heavy vehicles.

P04D4.title: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit Range or Performance
P04D4.description: Same as P04D3 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching expected behaviour - e.g. activation request without driver input or no response after a request.

causes.cause: Signal implausible against driver action or bus

P04D5.title: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit Low
P04D5.description: Same as P04D3 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P04D6.title: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit High
P04D6.description: Same as P04D3 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P04D7.title: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04D7.description: Same as P04D3 with intermittent or erratic signal. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P04D8.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop EGR Control
P04D8.description: After cold start the ECU operates EGR open-loop until preconditions (cooler temperature, sensor warm-up, engine load) are met, then transitions into closed-loop control. The transition is taking too long - typically due to a slow EGR temperature sensor, a stuck EGR valve still warming up, or a long-trip drive cycle that does not meet load conditions.

causes.cause: Short-trip operation - load conditions not met

P04D9.title: Closed Loop EGR Control At Limit Flow Too Low
P04D9.description: With EGR running in closed loop the controller has driven the actuator to its maximum opening but cannot reach the required EGR flow. The valve, cooler, or pipework is restricted enough that even full open does not deliver the modelled rate.

causes.cause: Valve effective opening reduced by carbon

P04DA.title: Closed Loop EGR Control At Limit Flow Too High
P04DA.description: Same as P04D9 with the controller fully closing the actuator yet still measuring more EGR flow than required. The valve does not seat fully, or position feedback under-reads.

causes.cause: Valve does not seat fully (debris or wear)

P04DB.title: Crankcase Ventilation System Disconnected
P04DB.description: A pressure or flow sensor in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) circuit reports atmospheric conditions where it should see crankcase or intake vacuum - the hose between crankcase and intake is disconnected, cracked, or open. PCV no longer routes blow-by gases into the intake, increasing oil mist emissions and risking oil leaks.

causes.cause: PCV hose pulled off or split
Oil filler cap missing or loose

P04DC.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P04DC.description: Same as P04B8 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the actuator command - door reports closed when motor commanded open, or vice versa.

causes.cause: Sensor signal offset against actual position

P04DD.title: Cold Start EGR A Flow Insufficient Detected
P04DD.description: During the cold-start strategy the ECU briefly opens EGR A to slow combustion temperatures and reduce engine-out NOx during catalyst light-off. The measured EGR flow stays below the calibrated target despite the requested opening - typically a stuck-closed valve, restricted cold-start path, or sensor offset that under-reports flow.

causes.cause: EGR valve A sticking closed when cold

P04DE.title: Cold Start EGR A Flow Excessive Detected
P04DE.description: Same as P04DD with EGR flow above the cold-start target - typically valve sticking open during the cold phase or position sensor offset low.

causes.cause: EGR valve A sticking open when cold

P04DF.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Performance Stuck Open
P04DF.description: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Performance Stuck Open: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

causes.cause: Debris on valve seat prevents full closing
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04E0.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Stuck Closed
P04E0.description: Same as P04AF on EVAP purge valve A. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04E1.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit
P04E1.description: A dedicated sensor monitors whether the PCV hose is fitted to its connector at the engine. The ECU detects a circuit fault on this sensor - cannot determine whether the hose is connected. Required by some emissions regulations to flag a disconnected PCV hose immediately.

P04E2.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Low
P04E2.description: Same as P04E1 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P04E3.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit High
P04E3.description: Same as P04E1 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P04E4.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04E4.description: Same as P04E1 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P04E5.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit
P04E5.description: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.cause: Open in sensor signal, supply or ground

P04E6.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Range or Performance
P04E6.description: Same as P04CF on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P04E7.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Low
P04E7.description: Same as P04D0 on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P04E8.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit High
P04E8.description: Same as P04D1 on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P04E9.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04E9.description: Same as P04D2 on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P04EA.title: EVAP System Small Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side
P04EA.description: The EVAP leak diagnostic has detected a small leak on the fuel tank side of the system - typically a hose, gasket, fuel cap, or fuel sender flange that does not seal completely. Vapor escapes during pressure or vacuum tests.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04EB.title: EVAP System Small Leak Detected Fresh Air Side
P04EB.description: Same as P04EA but on the fresh-air side - the path between vent valve and atmosphere is not sealing completely during the active test phase.

causes.cause: Vent valve does not seal in test mode

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04EC.title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side
P04EC.description: Same as P04EA but the leak is large enough that the system cannot build the test pressure or vacuum at all - typically a missing fuel cap, an unseated hose or a torn vapor line on the tank side.

causes.cause: Fuel cap missing or not seated
Vapor hose pulled off or torn

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04ED.title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected Fresh Air Side
P04ED.description: Same as P04EB on the fresh-air side, but with a leak large enough to prevent test build-up. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04EE.title: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side
P04EE.description: Same as P04EA but at the most sensitive leak threshold - typically the OBD-II 0.020-inch (~0.5 mm) test. The system holds pressure for some time but loses it slower than the diagnostic limit allows; usually fuel cap O-ring fatigue or microcracks in a hose.

causes.cause: Fuel cap O-ring aged or stiffened

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04EF.title: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected Fresh Air Side
P04EF.description: Same as P04EE on the fresh-air side - microcrack in a hose or imperfect vent valve seal at the most sensitive test threshold.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04F0.title: EVAP System High Load Purge Line A Performance
P04F0.description: On engines that have a separate high-load purge line - to use boost pressure to pull vapor on turbo applications - the ECU monitors flow when this path is commanded. The flow is below the expected level - the venturi, line, or check valve is restricted, or the line is incorrectly routed.

causes.cause: Line, venturi or check valve restricted

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04F1.title: EVAP System Purge Line Performance
P04F1.description: A general performance fault on the EVAP purge line - flow does not match the requested rate, without specifying which segment. Usually a partially blocked line, a stuck purge valve, or a leak that decouples flow from valve commands.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P04F2.title: Catalyst Heater Supply Voltage Bank 1
P04F2.description: The electric catalyst heater on bank 1 - used on hybrids and modern petrol cars to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature within seconds of cold start - reports that its supply voltage is outside the expected window. The heater cannot deliver the rated power, so cold-start emissions rise until the catalyst reaches light-off conventionally.

causes.cause: Heater supply voltage low or unstable
DC/DC converter fault on heater rail

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P04F3.title: Catalyst Heater Supply Voltage Bank 2
P04F3.description: The electric catalyst heater on bank 2 - used on hybrids and modern petrol cars to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature within seconds of cold start - reports that its supply voltage is outside the expected window. The heater cannot deliver the rated power, so cold-start emissions rise until the catalyst reaches light-off conventionally.

causes.cause: Heater supply voltage low or unstable
DC/DC converter fault on heater rail

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P04F4.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Low Bank 1
P04F4.description: The control or supply line to the electric catalyst heater on bank 1 is shorted to ground or measures below the expected voltage when the heater is commanded on.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P04F5.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Low Bank 2
P04F5.description: The control or supply line to the electric catalyst heater on bank 2 is shorted to ground or measures below the expected voltage when the heater is commanded on.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P04F6.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit High Bank 1
P04F6.description: Same as P04F4 with the line shorted to supply or open - the ECU measures higher voltage than the commanded duty cycle allows.

causes.cause: Open in heater element or harness
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P04F7.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit High Bank 2
P04F7.description: Same as P04F6 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P04F8.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Intermittent Bank 1
P04F8.description: Same as P04F4 with intermittent or erratic signal - typically a connector or harness fault on the heater feed.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P04F9.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Intermittent Bank 2
P04F9.description: Same as P04F8 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P04FA.title: EGR A Control Temperature Too High
P04FA.description: The ECU monitors the operating temperature of the EGR A actuator (or its control electronics). The reading has exceeded the safe upper threshold and the control unit derates or disables EGR A to protect the actuator from thermal damage.

causes.cause: Actuator overheated due to nearby exhaust heat or duty-cycle stress
Cooling jacket or air flow insufficient

P04FB.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Range or Performance
P04FB.description: The sensor that monitors PCV hose connection reports a value within plausible range yet inconsistent with the engine model - signal does not switch when the hose is moved during diagnosis, or shows offset against actual hose state.

P04FC.title: Crankcase Ventilation System Performance
P04FC.description: A general performance fault of the crankcase ventilation system - PCV pressure or flow does not match the engine model. Possible causes are a clogged PCV valve, blocked separator, oil-filler cap with a damaged seal, or excessive blow-by from worn rings.

causes.cause: Excessive blow-by from worn piston rings

P04FD.title: EGR Actuator A Control Processor Performance
P04FD.description: Modern smart EGR actuators contain their own microcontroller that handles position control internally and reports back over LIN or PWM. The ECU detects implausible behaviour from the actuator processor - missed messages, incorrect responses, or watchdog resets.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P04FE.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Performance Bank 1
P04FE.description: The catalyst heater on bank 1 is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - measured catalyst light-off time is longer than calibrated. Heater element ageing, increased contact resistance, or a partial winding failure are typical causes.

causes.cause: Heater element aged - reduced power output

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P04FF.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Performance Bank 2
P04FF.description: The catalyst heater on bank 2 is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - measured catalyst light-off time is longer than calibrated. Heater element ageing, increased contact resistance, or a partial winding failure are typical causes.

causes.cause: Heater element aged - reduced power output

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P0500.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Malfunction
P0500.description: The vehicle speed sensor (VSS) signal is missing or implausible. On automatic transmissions this often disables cruise control and shift adaptation; ABS-equipped cars typically derive speed from wheel speed sensors as a fallback.

P0501.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Range/Performance
P0501.description: The VSS signal is present but inconsistent — either values jump implausibly or the sensor reports a speed inconsistent with engine RPM in gear. Often a damaged reluctor ring or a sensor with degraded magnetic response.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0502.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P0502.description: The primary vehicle speed sensor (VSS A) reports a signal voltage below the plausible lower limit. With no usable speed signal the ECU loses cruise control, gear-shift logic and certain anti-stall functions.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0503.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent Erratic or High
P0503.description: Same as P0502 with the signal noisy, erratic or above the plausible upper limit - typical for a chafed harness, missing reluctor tooth or a sensor with a weakened magnet.

causes.cause: Noise on signal line or intermittent open
Reluctor ring damaged or missing teeth
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0504.title: Brake Switch "A"/"B" Correlation
P0504.description: Modern vehicles use two redundant brake switch signals (often one normally-open and one normally-closed). When the two signals disagree, this code is set; common causes include a misadjusted switch, internal switch failure, or wiring fault.

P0505.title: Idle Air Control System Malfunction
P0505.description: A general fault has been detected in the idle air control (IAC) system. On older vehicles with a separate IAC valve, this means the valve cannot maintain commanded idle RPM; on drive-by-wire systems, the equivalent fault is in the throttle body's idle adaptation.
symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P0506.title: Idle Air Control System RPM Lower Than Expected
P0506.description: The engine idles below the target RPM despite the IAC opening fully. Indicates restricted air path past the IAC — typically a heavily fouled throttle body or stuck IAC valve.

causes.cause: Throttle body or idle bypass passage clogged

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P0507.title: Idle Air Control System RPM Higher Than Expected
P0507.description: Idle RPM exceeds the target despite the IAC commanded fully closed. Almost always caused by a vacuum leak that lets air bypass the IAC — torn intake hose, leaking PCV, brake booster, or intake manifold gasket.
symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P0508.title: Idle Air Control System Circuit Low
P0508.description: The control line to the idle air control valve - which opens a small bypass around the throttle to set idle airflow - is shorted to ground or measures a voltage below the plausible level.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P0509.title: Idle Air Control System Circuit High
P0509.description: Same as P0508 with the line shorted to supply or open. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Open in IAC valve or harness
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P050A.title: Cold Start Idle Control System Performance
P050A.description: During the cold-start phase the ECU runs an elevated idle speed and a richer mixture to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature quickly. The cold-start idle does not behave as commanded - speed sags, hunts, or fails to come up. Possible causes are intake leaks active when cold, an IAC valve sticking, or implausible coolant temperature.

causes.cause: Intake leak only when cold (gasket shrinks)

P050B.title: Cold Start Ignition Timing Performance
P050B.description: During cold-start the ECU retards ignition timing to raise exhaust temperature for catalyst light-off. The strategy does not deliver the expected timing - feedback from knock sensor or combustion model shows ignition too far advanced or retarded for the demanded calibration.

causes.cause: Knock sensor drift causes wrong feedback

P050C.title: Cold Start Engine Coolant Temperature Performance
P050C.description: During cold-start the ECU expects coolant temperature to rise within a calibrated time window. Either the engine warms up too slowly (stuck-open thermostat, weak combustion) or the temperature signal does not reflect the actual warm-up.

causes.cause: Thermostat stuck open - engine warms too slowly

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P050D.title: Cold Start Rough Idle
P050D.description: The ECU detects rough idle behaviour during the cold-start phase only. Once the engine has warmed up the issue disappears. Typically caused by injector deposits, low compression on one cylinder when cold, or sticky valve guides.

causes.cause: Injector tip coked - poor cold spray pattern

P050E.title: Cold Start Engine Exhaust Temperature Too Low
P050E.description: During the cold-start strategy the ECU monitors exhaust temperature to ensure catalyst light-off. The measured EGT remains below the target threshold within the allowed time - heat-up strategy is not effective. Causes include excessive heat loss, very rich mixture cooling the exhaust, or a faulty EGT sensor.

causes.cause: Excessive heat loss between port and catalyst

P050F.title: Brake Assist Vacuum Too Low
P050F.description: The ECU monitors the vacuum supplied to the brake booster (either via a dedicated sensor or via intake manifold pressure). The level has dropped below the calibrated threshold; brake-pedal feel will be hard, and an electric vacuum pump may be commanded to restore vacuum.

causes.cause: Vacuum leak in booster line or check valve

P0510.title: Closed Throttle Position Switch
P0510.description: The dedicated closed-throttle switch (or closed-throttle bit on the TPS) does not behave as expected - either it never activates, never deactivates, or shows incoherent state against TPS voltage and engine load. Used by older systems for fuel-cutoff and idle recognition.

causes.cause: Switch out of adjustment or worn

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P0511.title: Idle Air Control Circuit
P0511.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the idle air control valve - open or short on supply, signal or ground. The ECU loses control of idle bypass airflow.
symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P0512.title: Starter Request Circuit
P0512.description: The starter request input - the signal that tells the ECU the driver wants to crank the engine - shows a circuit fault. Without it the engine cannot be started under software-managed start strategies (stop-start, push-button, immobiliser-coordinated start).

P0513.title: Incorrect Immobilizer Key
P0513.description: The immobiliser system has detected a key that is not authorised for this vehicle. Engine start is blocked. Possible causes are an unprogrammed replacement key, a transponder fault, or a deliberate attempt to start with the wrong key.

P0514.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P0514.description: The battery temperature sensor reports a value within plausible range yet inconsistent with engine bay or coolant temperature. Modern alternator regulation uses battery temperature to adjust charging voltage, so an offset here causes over- or undercharging.
symptoms: Reduced power output or limp mode
Charging may fail or be slowed

P0515.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0515.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the battery temperature sensor - open or short on supply, signal or ground.
symptoms: Reduced power output or limp mode
Charging may fail or be slowed

P0516.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0516.description: Same as P0515 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced power output or limp mode
Charging may fail or be slowed

P0517.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0517.description: Same as P0515 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Reduced power output or limp mode
Charging may fail or be slowed

P0518.title: Idle Air Control Circuit Intermittent
P0518.description: Same as P0511 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P0519.title: Idle Air Control System Performance
P0519.description: The idle air control system is electrically intact, but the actual idle airflow does not match the commanded value - typical for a sticky valve, intake leak, or carbon build-up around the throttle bore.

causes.cause: IAC valve sticking due to carbon

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P051A.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P051A.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the crankcase pressure sensor A - typically used to monitor PCV operation and detect a clogged separator or disconnected hose.

P051B.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range or Performance
P051B.description: Same as P051A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P051C.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P051C.description: Same as P051A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P051D.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P051D.description: Same as P051A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P051E.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P051E.description: Same as P051A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P051F.title: PCV Filter Restriction
P051F.description: The pressure or flow sensor in the PCV path detects increased restriction across the oil-mist filter element. Once saturated with oil mist, the filter no longer passes blow-by gas, raising crankcase pressure and pushing oil past seals.

causes.cause: PCV filter saturated with oil mist

P0520.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A Circuit
P0520.description: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0521.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
P0521.description: The engine oil pressure sensor or switch reports values that are not plausible for current RPM, oil temperature, and engine load. Could indicate a sensor fault or genuinely abnormal pressure.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0522.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Low Voltage
P0522.description: The oil pressure sensor signal is below the expected minimum. Often points to an electrical fault — short to ground or failed sensor — but can also indicate genuinely low oil pressure.

P0523.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A High
P0523.description: Same as P0520 with the signal voltage above the plausible range - usually a short to supply or sensor failure that pegs the output high.

P0524.title: Engine Oil Pressure Too Low
P0524.description: The ECU has determined that engine oil pressure is below the safe operating threshold. Caused by low oil level, worn oil pump, severe engine wear, or a stuck pressure relief valve. Continued operation can rapidly destroy the engine.

P0525.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Range or Performance
P0525.description: The control circuit to the cruise control servo (vacuum or electric actuator that holds throttle position) shows feedback in plausible range yet inconsistent with the commanded action - servo slow, sticking, or supply weak.

causes.cause: Servo response slow due to wear

P0526.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit
P0526.description: A general circuit fault on the cooling fan tachometer feedback - the ECU loses fan speed information needed to verify cooling capacity and detect a stalled or runaway fan.

P0527.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P0527.description: Same as P0526 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the commanded fan speed - typically sensor drift, weak magnet, or partial reluctor damage.

P0528.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0528.description: Same as P0526 with no detectable signal at all - sensor not producing pulses despite the fan being commanded on.

P0529.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0529.description: Same as P0526 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P052A.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
P052A.description: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P052B.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1
P052B.description: Same as P052A with the phaser stuck retarded - cold-start strategy cannot pull the cam to the advanced position needed for fast catalyst light-off.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P052C.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2
P052C.description: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P052D.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2
P052D.description: Same as P052B on bank 2. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P052E.title: PCV Regulator Valve Performance
P052E.description: The crankcase ventilation regulator valve - which throttles blow-by gas flow toward the intake based on engine load - is electrically intact but does not deliver the modelled pressure regulation. Either the valve diaphragm is fatigued or the spring is weak.

P052F.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 System Voltage
P052F.description: Glow Plug Control Module 1 System Voltage: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects diesel cold-start preheating.
symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P0530.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit
P0530.description: General electrical fault on the A/C refrigerant pressure sensor circuit. The ECU uses this signal to enable the compressor and cooling fan; without it the A/C is typically disabled.

P0531.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0531.description: The A/C refrigerant pressure sensor signal is implausible against operating conditions. Reading does not change as expected when the compressor cycles or ambient conditions change.

P0532.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Low
P0532.description: A/C pressure sensor signal voltage below the lower threshold — open, short to ground, sensor fault, or a refrigerant charge so low that the pressure is genuinely low.

causes.cause: Sensor circuit shorted to ground or open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0533.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit High
P0533.description: A/C pressure sensor signal voltage above the upper threshold — short to supply, defective sensor, or a system overcharge/blocked condenser causing genuine high pressure.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0534.title: A/C Refrigerant Charge Loss
P0534.description: The system detects an abnormally low refrigerant charge. Compressor operation is typically inhibited to prevent damage.

P0535.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0535.description: The evaporator temperature sensor signal is missing or out of range. Used to prevent icing of the evaporator core.

P0536.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P0536.description: The evaporator temperature sensor used to prevent evaporator icing reports a value within plausible range yet not matching the engine model or cabin conditions.

P0537.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0537.description: The evaporator temperature sensor signal voltage is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Indicates a short to ground or sensor fault.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0538.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0538.description: The evaporator temperature sensor signal voltage is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Typically open circuit or short to power.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0539.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0539.description: Same as P0536 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P053A.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Open
P053A.description: The heater on PCV path A - used to prevent ice plugs in the crankcase ventilation hose during cold weather - has an open control circuit. Without it, condensation can freeze and block PCV flow, raising crankcase pressure dangerously.

causes.cause: Open in harness or heater element
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P053B.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Low
P053B.description: Same as P053A with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P053C.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit High
P053C.description: Same as P053A with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P053D.title: PCV Heater A Performance
P053D.description: The PCV heater on path A is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - hose temperature does not rise as commanded. Heater element aged or contact resistance increased.

P053E.title: Crankcase Pressure Too High
P053E.description: The crankcase pressure sensor reports a value above the safe upper threshold. Excessive crankcase pressure pushes oil past seals and contaminates the PCV path with mist - causes are clogged PCV system, frozen breather hose, or excessive blow-by from worn rings.

P053F.title: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 1
P053F.description: During cold-start the ECU runs an elevated rail pressure on direct-injection systems for better cold spray atomisation. The pressure target on bank 1 is not reached within the calibrated time window - typical for a high-pressure pump that loses output when cold or a pressure regulator with cold-stickiness.

causes.cause: HP pump output low when cold

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P0540.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit
P0540.description: Intake Air Heater A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. Used on diesel and some petrol engines for cold-start emissions and starting reliability.

P0541.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Low
P0541.description: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Used on diesel and some petrol engines for cold-start emissions and starting reliability.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0542.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit High
P0542.description: Intake Air Heater A Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Used on diesel and some petrol engines for cold-start emissions and starting reliability.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0543.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Open
P0543.description: The intake air heater (grid heater) on path A - used on cold-start of diesel engines to warm intake air for reliable combustion - has an open control circuit. Without it, cold-start emissions and idle quality on cold days suffer.

causes.cause: Open in harness, relay or heater element
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0544.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0544.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst). The ECU loses thermal protection feedback for the catalyst and DPF.

P0545.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Bank 1 Sensor 1 Low
P0545.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor signal at bank 1, sensor 1 is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Indicates short to ground or sensor fault.

P0546.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Bank 1 Sensor 1 High
P0546.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor signal at bank 1, sensor 1 is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Typically open circuit or short to power.

P0547.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0547.description: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 1: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

P0548.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0548.description: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1: the signal voltage is below the expected range. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0549.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0549.description: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1: the signal voltage is above the expected range. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P054A.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
P054A.description: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P054B.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1
P054B.description: Same as P052B on the B camshaft of bank 1. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P054C.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2
P054C.description: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P054D.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2
P054D.description: Same as P052B on the B camshaft of bank 2. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.
symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P054E.title: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Lower Than Expected
P054E.description: At idle the ECU expects a calibrated fuel quantity to maintain set-speed. The actual quantity is significantly less than modelled - typical for a tight engine, very low friction, dragging accessory load missing, or implausible idle airflow.

P054F.title: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Higher Than Expected
P054F.description: Same as P054E with actual fuel quantity above the model - high friction, sticky throttle, or accessory drag.

P0550.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0550.description: General electrical fault on the power steering pressure sensor. The ECU uses this signal to compensate idle speed when the steering load increases; without it idle stability can suffer during parking maneuvers.

P0551.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0551.description: The PS pressure sensor signal stays in electrical range but is implausible for the operating state, e.g. high pressure reported with the wheels straight.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0552.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Input
P0552.description: PS pressure sensor signal voltage below threshold — open, short to ground, or sensor failure. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Sensor circuit shorted to ground or open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0553.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Circuit High Input
P0553.description: PS pressure sensor signal voltage above threshold — short to supply or sensor failure. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0554.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Intermittent
P0554.description: The power steering pressure sensor signal is intermittent. The ECM cannot consistently raise idle to compensate for steering load.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0555.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0555.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the brake booster pressure sensor - the ECU cannot determine vacuum reserve in the booster, which limits the safe operation of stop-start, regenerative-braking blending, and electric vacuum pump control.
symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P0556.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P0556.description: Same as P0555 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model - drift, partial blockage of the reference port.
symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P0557.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P0557.description: Same as P0555 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P0558.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P0558.description: Same as P0555 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P0559.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0559.description: Same as P0555 with intermittent or erratic signal. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P055A.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit
P055A.description: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P055B.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Range or Performance
P055B.description: Same as P055A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P055C.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Low
P055C.description: Same as P055A with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P055D.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B High
P055D.description: Same as P055A with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P055E.title: Oxygen Sensor Control Module System Voltage
P055E.description: The dedicated O2 sensor control module - found on systems with a wide-band sensor needing its own pumping current driver - reports its supply voltage outside the calibrated window.

P055F.title: Engine Oil Pressure Out of Range
P055F.description: The measured oil pressure is far outside the expected range for current engine speed and oil temperature - either too low (oil pump weak, oil level low, bearing wear) or anomalously high (relief valve stuck closed, blocked oil cooler).

causes.cause: Oil pump worn or oil level low

P0560.title: System Voltage Malfunction
P0560.description: A general fault in the system voltage seen by the ECU — value implausible, missing, or unstable but without crossing the specific thresholds of P0562 (low) or P0563 (high). Often appears intermittently with a marginal alternator or weak battery.

causes.cause: Charging system marginal (aged battery or alternator)
Corroded battery terminals or ground strap

P0561.title: System Voltage Unstable
P0561.description: The ECU monitors battery voltage and detects unstable behaviour - rapid fluctuations beyond what current load changes explain. Typical causes are a failing alternator, loose battery terminals, weak battery, or a heavy load (radiator fan, glow plugs, heated screen) drawing voltage down briefly.

P0562.title: System Voltage Low
P0562.description: Battery / charging system voltage seen by the ECU has dropped below the lower threshold (typically around 10.5 V). Modern ECUs are sensitive to under-voltage and may set this code briefly during cranking on a weak battery.

causes.cause: Corroded battery terminals or ground strap

P0563.title: System Voltage High
P0563.description: Battery / charging system voltage seen by the ECU exceeds the upper threshold (typically around 16 V). Caused by a failing voltage regulator inside the alternator. Sustained over-voltage can damage other electronics.

P0564.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit
P0564.description: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

causes.cause: Open in stalk switch or harness

P0565.title: Cruise Control On Signal
P0565.description: The ECU detects an implausible state of the cruise control on/off signal - either the master switch is stuck on, intermittent, or shows a logic level that does not match other dash signals.

P0566.title: Cruise Control Cancel Input Circuit
P0566.description: Cruise Control Cancel Input Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

P0567.title: Cruise Control Resume Input Circuit
P0567.description: Cruise Control Resume Input Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

P0568.title: Cruise Control Set Input Circuit
P0568.description: Cruise Control Set Input Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

P0569.title: Cruise Control Coast Signal
P0569.description: The coast (decelerate) signal of the cruise control reports an implausible state - typically a stuck or shorted contact.

P056A.title: Cruise Control Increase Distance Signal
P056A.description: Cruise Control Increase Distance Signal: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects cruise-control operation.

P056B.title: Cruise Control Decrease Distance Signal
P056B.description: Cruise Control Decrease Distance Signal: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects cruise-control operation.

P056C.title: Cruise Control Cancel Signal
P056C.description: The cancel signal (driver-initiated cruise off) reports an implausible state - stuck, missing, or shorted.

causes.cause: Stalk or brake switch contact stuck

P056D.title: Reductant Control Module System Voltage
P056D.description: The reductant (AdBlue) control module reports its supply voltage outside the calibrated window. Reductant dosing is suspended until voltage returns to range, which can drive NOx emissions out of compliance.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P056E.title: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control A Performance
P056E.description: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control A Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.
symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P056F.title: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control B Performance
P056F.description: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control B Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.
symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P0570.title: Cruise Control Accel Signal Malfunction
P0570.description: The cruise control accelerate input signal is implausible — switch contacts welded, wiring fault, or stalk defect. The ECU disables cruise control to prevent unintended acceleration.

P0571.title: Brake Switch "A" Circuit Malfunction
P0571.description: The brake light switch signal seen by the ECU is implausible — for example, both contacts active simultaneously, or no signal change despite the brake pedal being pressed (cruise control engages and disengages on this signal). On many cars also disables shift interlock.

causes.cause: Brake switch failed (worn contacts, internal break)
Switch misadjusted (does not actuate at correct pedal position)

P0572.title: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit Low
P0572.description: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. This affects cruise-control operation.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0573.title: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit High
P0573.description: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. This affects cruise-control operation.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0574.title: Cruise Control System Vehicle Speed Too High
P0574.description: The cruise control sees actual vehicle speed exceed the set-speed by more than the diagnostic margin (typically going downhill or with throttle override). Persistent oversize means the system cannot bring speed down - either an actuator fault, brake-blending failure, or driver kick-down stuck.

P0575.title: Cruise Control Input Circuit
P0575.description: A general circuit fault is detected on a cruise control input that is not specifically multiplexed - typically the dedicated set/resume button input.

P0576.title: Cruise Control Input Circuit Low
P0576.description: Same as P0575 with the input voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0577.title: Cruise Control Input Circuit High
P0577.description: Same as P0575 with the input voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0578.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Stuck
P0578.description: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Stuck: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

P0579.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Range or Performance
P0579.description: Same as P0564 with the analogue level inside the plausible range yet not matching any of the calibrated button levels - resistor ladder drifted, contact resistance increased, or wrong stalk module fitted.

P057A.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Open
P057A.description: The brake pedal position sensor A has an open control circuit. The ECU loses analogue feedback about pedal travel - used by stop-start, regenerative braking and adaptive cruise to coordinate engine, motor and friction brakes.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P057B.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Range or Performance
P057B.description: Same as P057A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the brake-light switch state - typical for a sensor offset against pedal travel or a worn potentiometer track.

P057C.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P057C.description: Same as P057A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P057D.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
P057D.description: Same as P057A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P057E.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P057E.description: Same as P057A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
