causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P057F.title: Battery A State of Charge Performance
P057F.description: The battery monitor reports a State of Charge (SoC) value that does not match the rest-voltage and current pattern - typically a battery near end of life, sulfation, or a deep discharge that the SoC algorithm has not converged on.

P0580.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Low
P0580.description: Same as P0564 with the analogue input voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0581.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit High
P0581.description: Same as P0564 with the analogue input voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0582.title: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit Open
P0582.description: The vacuum-control solenoid of a vacuum-driven cruise servo (older systems) has an open control circuit - the servo cannot pull the throttle.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0583.title: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit Low
P0583.description: Same as P0582 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0584.title: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit High
P0584.description: Same as P0582 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0585.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A and B Correlation
P0585.description: Cruise control uses two redundant multiplexed inputs (A and B) for safety. The two inputs do not agree - one reports a button press the other does not, or both report incompatible levels at the same time.

causes.cause: Stalk module ageing - drift between A and B

P0586.title: Cruise Control Vent Control Circuit Open
P0586.description: The vent solenoid of a vacuum-driven cruise servo - which releases vacuum to drop throttle - has an open control circuit. The servo cannot release vacuum, so cruise speed cannot be reduced.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0587.title: Cruise Control Vent Control Circuit Low
P0587.description: Same as P0586 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0588.title: Cruise Control Vent Control Circuit High
P0588.description: Same as P0586 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0589.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit
P0589.description: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

causes.cause: Open in stalk switch or harness

P058A.title: Battery Monitor Module Performance
P058A.description: Battery Monitor Module Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. The module reports battery current, voltage and temperature for charge management.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P058B.title: Battery Monitor Module Current Monitoring Performance
P058B.description: Battery Monitor Module Current Monitoring Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. The module reports battery current, voltage and temperature for charge management.

P058C.title: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Monitoring Performance
P058C.description: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Monitoring Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. The module reports battery current, voltage and temperature for charge management.

P058D.title: Battery Monitor Module Voltage Monitoring Performance
P058D.description: Battery Monitor Module Voltage Monitoring Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. The module reports battery current, voltage and temperature for charge management.

P058E.title: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Too High
P058E.description: The battery monitor module measures battery temperature above the safe upper threshold - charging is derated or stopped to prevent thermal runaway. Causes are heat soak from a hot engine bay, hard charging on a depleted battery, or a faulty sensor.

P058F.title: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Too Low
P058F.description: Same as P058E with the temperature below the safe lower threshold - charging current is reduced to prevent damage to a frozen battery.

P0590.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Stuck
P0590.description: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Stuck: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

P0591.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Range or Performance
P0591.description: Same as P0579 on input B.

P0592.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Low
P0592.description: Same as P0580 on input B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0593.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit High
P0593.description: Same as P0581 on input B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0594.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Open
P0594.description: The servo motor that drives the cruise control throttle actuator has an open control circuit. The ECU cannot drive the servo - cruise control is unavailable.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0595.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Low
P0595.description: Same as P0594 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0596.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit High
P0596.description: Same as P0594 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0597.title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit Open
P0597.description: The map-controlled thermostat - electrically heated to lower its opening temperature on demand for emissions or torque mapping - has an open control circuit. The ECU loses the ability to override coolant flow timing.

causes.cause: Open in heater element or harness
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0598.title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit Low
P0598.description: Same as P0597 with the control line shorted to ground. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0599.title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit High
P0599.description: Same as P0597 with the control line shorted to supply. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P059A.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit
P059A.description: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. Active grille shutters manage airflow for engine cooling and aerodynamics.

P059B.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Range or Performance
P059B.description: Same as P059A with feedback in plausible range yet not matching the commanded angle.

P059C.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit High
P059C.description: Same as P059A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P059D.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit Low
P059D.description: Same as P059A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P059E.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P059E.description: Same as P059A with intermittent signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P059F.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Performance Stuck Off
P059F.description: Active Grille Air Shutter A Performance Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position. Active grille shutters manage airflow for engine cooling and aerodynamics.

causes.cause: Shutter jammed by debris or ice
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P05A0.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Stuck On
P05A0.description: Same as P059F with the shutter A stuck in the open or active position - typically broken return spring or seized linkage.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P05A1.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Minimum or Maximum Stop Performance
P05A1.description: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Minimum or Maximum Stop Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. Active grille shutters manage airflow for engine cooling and aerodynamics.

P05A2.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit Open
P05A2.description: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit Open: the control circuit is open. Active grille shutters manage airflow for engine cooling and aerodynamics.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P05A3.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit Range or Performance
P05A3.description: Same as P05A2 with electrical drive intact but the shutter response not matching the commanded movement - actuator slow or weak.

P05A4.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit High
P05A4.description: Same as P05A2 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P05A5.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit Low

P0600.title: Serial Communication Link
P0600.description: A general fault on a serial communication link - typically used by older single-wire diagnostic protocols (KWP2000, ISO 9141) before CAN became universal. ECU has lost or corrupted communication with another module.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0601.title: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
P0601.description: The ECU's internal memory checksum does not match the expected value at startup — the firmware/calibration in flash has become corrupt. Often appears after a failed flash, low battery during programming, or genuine module hardware failure.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0602.title: Control Module Programming Error
P0602.description: The ECU is reporting that it is missing required calibration data — typically appears after a virgin module is installed but never coded/programmed for the vehicle, or after a flash that did not write all blocks.

causes.cause: Replacement ECU not coded to vehicle

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0603.title: Internal Control Module Keep Alive Memory (KAM) Error
P0603.description: The ECU detected a fault in its KAM (battery-backed memory used to store adaptations and DTCs). Often appears after battery disconnect or low battery; persistent codes indicate an internal ECU fault.

causes.cause: Battery disconnected or voltage too low
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0604.title: Internal Control Module Random Access Memory (RAM) Error
P0604.description: ECU self-test detected a RAM fault during runtime checks. This is an internal ECU defect; replacement or reflash with manufacturer support is generally required.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0605.title: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
P0605.description: ECU self-test detected a ROM/checksum failure on the program memory. The control software cannot be trusted; vehicle typically defaults to limp-home with reduced function.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0606.title: ECM/PCM Processor Fault
P0606.description: The ECU's internal processor self-test has failed. This is a hard module fault — the ECU usually triggers limp-home mode and may not respond to scan tools fully until replaced or repaired.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0607.title: Control Module Performance
P0607.description: The ECM performs an internal self-test and detects a processor or memory performance fault that does not fit the more specific P0601 to P0606 codes.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0608.title: Control Module VSS Output A
P0608.description: The vehicle speed signal output from the control module to other systems is faulty. Other modules expect a speed signal that the ECM no longer provides correctly.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0609.title: Control Module VSS Output B
P0609.description: A fault is detected on the secondary vehicle speed signal output (VSS B) that the ECU sends to other modules (instrument cluster, ABS, transmission). Output level inconsistent with the internal speed value.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P060A.title: Internal Control Module Monitoring Processor Performance
P060A.description: Modern ECUs have a separate watchdog or monitoring processor that supervises the main processor. This processor reports a self-diagnosis fault - typically a watchdog event, ROM/RAM mismatch, or check-sum error in its monitor section. The ECU runs in a safety-fallback mode until repair.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P060B.title: Internal Control Module A and D Processing Performance
P060B.description: The ECU's analog-to-digital converter does not deliver consistent results - typically reference voltage drift, multiplexer fault, or noise on the analog ground.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P060C.title: Internal Control Module Main Processor Performance
P060C.description: The ECU main processor self-diagnosis flagged a performance fault - watchdog, ROM check, or instruction-set self-test failed. Engine runs on safety strategy.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P060D.title: Internal Control Module Accelerator Pedal Position Performance
P060D.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "accelerator pedal position" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P060E.title: Internal Control Module Throttle Position Performance
P060E.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "throttle position" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P060F.title: Internal Control Module Coolant Temperature Performance
P060F.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine coolant temperature" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0610.title: Control Module Vehicle Options Error
P0610.description: The ECU's stored vehicle option configuration is invalid or does not match the connected hardware. Common after replacing or swapping a control module without proper coding/configuration.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0611.title: Fuel Injector Control Module Performance
P0611.description: Modern direct-injection systems use a dedicated injector driver module that generates the high-voltage charge pulses needed to open piezo or solenoid injectors. The module reports an internal performance fault.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P0612.title: Fuel Injector Control Module Relay Control
P0612.description: A circuit fault on the relay that powers the injector driver module - either control line or contact integrity issue.
symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P0613.title: TCM Processor
P0613.description: The transmission control module performs an internal self-test and detects a processor performance fault.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0614.title: ECM and TCM Incompatible
P0614.description: The ECM and TCM exchange identification or calibration data over the powertrain bus and detect that they are not a valid pair - typically appears after replacing one of the modules with a unit from a different vehicle variant.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0615.title: Starter Relay Circuit
P0615.description: General electrical fault on the starter relay control circuit driven by the ECU/PCM. Typical symptom is a no-crank or intermittent crank condition.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0616.title: Starter Relay A Circuit Low
P0616.description: The control line for starter relay A is shorted to ground - the ECU drives the relay and measures voltage too low.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0617.title: Starter Relay Circuit High
P0617.description: The starter relay control circuit voltage is above the upper threshold — short to supply or stuck driver.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0618.title: Alternative Fuel Control Module KAM Error
P0618.description: The control module for alternative fuel (CNG, LPG, hydrogen) reports a Keep-Alive-Memory error - persistent calibration values are corrupt or unreadable. Adaptive learning is reset.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0619.title: Alternative Fuel Control Module RAM and ROM Error
P0619.description: The alternative fuel control module reports an internal RAM or ROM check failure - module no longer trustworthy.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P061A.title: Internal Control Module Torque Performance
P061A.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine torque" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P061B.title: Internal Control Module Torque Calculation Performance
P061B.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "torque calculation" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P061C.title: Internal Control Module Engine RPM Performance
P061C.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine speed (RPM)" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P061D.title: Internal Control Module Engine Air Mass Performance
P061D.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "intake air mass" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P061E.title: Internal Control Module Brake Signal Performance
P061E.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "brake signal" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P061F.title: Internal Control Module Throttle Actuator Controller Performance
P061F.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "throttle actuator control" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P0620.title: Generator Control Circuit
P0620.description: General electrical fault detected in the alternator/generator control circuit. The ECU regulates field excitation on most modern alternators; a fault here causes charging issues and may set additional battery voltage codes.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0621.title: Generator Lamp L Control Circuit
P0621.description: The control circuit for the generator warning lamp output (L terminal) reports a fault.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0622.title: Generator Field F Control Circuit
P0622.description: The control circuit for the generator field terminal (F) reports a fault. The ECM cannot regulate field current as expected.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0623.title: Generator Lamp Control Circuit
P0623.description: Generic generator warning lamp control circuit fault, often used where the lamp terminal designation is not L or where multiple lamps share a single output.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0624.title: Fuel Cap Lamp Control Circuit
P0624.description: The control circuit for the fuel cap warning lamp reports a fault. The ECM cannot drive the indicator that warns of an open or loose fuel cap.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0625.title: Generator Field Terminal Circuit Low
P0625.description: Voltage on the alternator F terminal (field excitation) is below threshold — open or short to ground in the excitation path.

causes.cause: Field circuit open or shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0626.title: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit Performance
P0626.description: The generator field circuit response does not match command. Field current ramps slowly, drifts or fails to reach commanded values during regulation.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0627.title: Fuel Pump "A" Control Circuit Open
P0627.description: The ECU detected an open circuit in the fuel pump A control output. With no pump operation the engine cannot run; this code is often paired with no-start and no fuel pressure.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P0628.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Low
P0628.description: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Low: the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P0629.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit High
P0629.description: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit High: the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P062A.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Range or Performance
P062A.description: The control output to the primary fuel pump A is electrically intact yet response and fuel pressure response do not match - typically a worn pump, a clogged strainer, or a partially shorted PWM driver.
symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P062B.title: Internal Control Module Fuel Injector Control Performance
P062B.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "fuel injector control" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P062C.title: Internal Control Module Vehicle Speed Performance
P062C.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "vehicle speed" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P062D.title: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 1
P062D.description: The injector driver stage on bank 1 - the high-side or low-side switching transistor that fires the injectors - reports a performance fault. Typical for a partial driver short, drift in the boost capacitor, or supply ripple under load.
symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P062E.title: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 2
P062E.description: The injector driver stage on bank 2 - the high-side or low-side switching transistor that fires the injectors - reports a performance fault. Typical for a partial driver short, drift in the boost capacitor, or supply ripple under load.
symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P062F.title: Internal Control Module EEPROM Error
P062F.description: The ECU's EEPROM (persistent calibration storage) reports a check-sum or write error. Calibration values may be corrupted - the ECU runs on safe defaults until repair.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0630.title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible ECM or PCM
P0630.description: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible ECM or PCM: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0631.title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible TCM
P0631.description: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible TCM: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0632.title: Odometer Not Programmed ECM or PCM
P0632.description: The odometer value stored in the ECM/PCM is missing or implausible - typical after a module replacement without odometer programming, or after persistent storage corruption.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0633.title: Immobiliser Key Not Programmed
P0633.description: The immobiliser system rejects the current key because it is not programmed to this vehicle. Engine start is inhibited.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0634.title: Control Module Internal Temperature A Too High
P0634.description: Control Module Internal Temperature A Too High: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0635.title: Power Steering Control Circuit
P0635.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the power steering control output - typically the line that the ECU uses to request raised idle when steering load is high, or to enable an electric pump.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0636.title: Power Steering Control Circuit Low
P0636.description: Same as P0635 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0637.title: Power Steering Control Circuit High
P0637.description: Same as P0635 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0638.title: Throttle Actuator Control Range or Performance Bank 1
P0638.description: The drive-by-wire throttle actuator on bank 1 does not respond as commanded - actuator slow, gearing slipping, or position feedback offset against actual blade angle.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P0639.title: Throttle Actuator Control Range or Performance Bank 2
P0639.description: The drive-by-wire throttle actuator on bank 2 does not respond as commanded - actuator slow, gearing slipping, or position feedback offset against actual blade angle.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P063A.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A
P063A.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the alternator voltage sense line A - the line over which the regulator measures battery-side voltage to set charging output.

causes.cause: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P063B.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A Range or Performance
P063B.description: Same as P063A with the sense voltage in plausible range yet not matching the alternator output - high contact resistance or wrong calibration.

causes.cause: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P063C.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A Low
P063C.description: Same as P063A with the sense voltage below the plausible range.

causes.cause: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P063D.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A High
P063D.description: Same as P063A with the sense voltage above the plausible range.

causes.cause: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P063E.title: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 1
P063E.description: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P063F.title: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present
P063F.description: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P0640.title: Intake Air Heater Control Circuit
P0640.description: A general circuit fault on the intake air heater control - the ECU cannot drive the grid heater at cold-start.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0641.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit Open
P0641.description: The 5 V reference voltage that the ECU supplies to multiple sensors (TPS, MAP, accelerator pedal, etc.) has dropped out or is open-circuit. Symptoms cascade — many sensor codes appear at once, all related to the same reference rail.

causes.cause: Reference wire shorted to ground (one defective sensor pulls the rail down)
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0642.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit Low
P0642.description: The 5 V reference voltage on the A circuit (used by multiple sensors) is below threshold — short to ground or excessive current draw by a single sensor pulling the rail down.

causes.cause: Sensor or harness shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0643.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit High
P0643.description: 5 V reference rail A above threshold — short to a higher voltage source. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Sensor or harness shorted to higher voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0644.title: Driver Display Serial Communication Circuit
P0644.description: The serial communication line to the driver display (instrument cluster, MIL/check-engine warning) shows a circuit fault. Driver may not see warning lights as expected.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0645.title: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit
P0645.description: A general circuit fault on the A/C clutch relay control - the line over which the ECU engages the magnetic clutch to drive the A/C compressor.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0646.title: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit Low
P0646.description: Same as P0645 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0647.title: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit High
P0647.description: Same as P0645 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0648.title: Immobilizer Lamp Control Circuit
P0648.description: Immobilizer Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0649.title: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit
P0649.description: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P064A.title: Fuel Pump Control Module A
P064A.description: A general fault is detected on the dedicated fuel pump control module A. Used on PWM-controlled returnless fuel systems to vary pump speed against demand. The module reports an internal performance issue.
symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P064B.title: PTO Control Module
P064B.description: A general fault on the power take-off (PTO) control module - reports internal performance issue or communication trouble. Affects vehicles with auxiliary mechanical drives (cranes, snow ploughs, hydraulic pumps).
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P064C.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1
P064C.description: A general fault is detected on the first glow plug control module - typically a self-diagnosis flag for an internal driver, supply, or watchdog issue.
symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P064D.title: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1
P064D.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "oxygen sensor processing, bank 1" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P064E.title: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance Bank 2
P064E.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "oxygen sensor processing, bank 2" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P064F.title: Unauthorized Software or Calibration Detected
P064F.description: The ECU's secure boot or signature check has detected calibration data that is not signed by the manufacturer - typically appears after chip-tuning or unauthorised flash programming. The ECU may run on safe defaults or refuse to start.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0650.title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp Control Circuit Malfunction
P0650.description: A fault in the wiring or control circuit between the ECU and the malfunction indicator lamp (MIL). The MIL may stay on permanently, fail to light at key-on, or flicker — the OBD-II self-check on the bulb itself failed.

causes.cause: Wiring fault between ECU and cluster

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0651.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Open
P0651.description: The 5-volt sensor reference rail B is open — the module supplies no voltage on this circuit. Every sensor powered from reference B loses its supply and reads invalid, so the ECU substitutes default values and may limit engine operation. Causes: a broken reference wire, a disconnected connector, or an internal open in the module's voltage regulator for rail B.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0652.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Low
P0652.description: Same as P0651 with the reference rail shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0653.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit High
P0653.description: Same as P0651 with the reference rail shorted to supply or above the design voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0654.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit Open
P0654.description: The engine RPM signal output that the ECU sends to other modules (tachometer, transmission, ABS) has an open circuit.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0655.title: Engine Hot Lamp Output Control Circuit

P0670.title: Glow Plug Module Control Circuit
P0670.description: The control circuit between the engine controller and the glow plug control module reports a fault. The ECU can no longer reliably command the module that drives the glow plugs, so cold-start pre-heating may not run. On a diesel this causes hard starting, white smoke, and rough running until warm. Causes: open or shorted wiring between ECU and glow plug module, a failed module, or a power/ground fault at the module.
symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P0671.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit
P0671.description: An electrical fault is present in the glow plug circuit for cylinder 1. The glow plug control module cannot drive this plug correctly — open circuit, short, or out-of-range resistance — so cylinder 1 is not pre-heated. On a cold start this causes hard starting, white smoke, and a misfire-like rough run until the engine warms. Causes: a failed glow plug, a broken supply lead to that plug, corrosion at the plug connector, or a faulty module output for cylinder 1.
symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P06E9.description: The ECU detects unusual cranking behaviour - excessive crank time, slow crank speed, or starter draw outside the normal envelope. Could be a worn starter, weak battery, high engine drag, or excess starter solenoid resistance.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P06EA.title: NOx Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P06EA.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "NOx sensor processing, bank 1 sensor 1" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P06EB.title: NOx Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1 Sensor 2

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P06EC.title: Fuel Injector Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P06EC.description: The fuel injector control module has reported a fault to the ECM and requested MIL illumination. Read the FICM-side code for the actual fault.
symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P06ED.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit Low
P06ED.description: Same as P0654 with the output line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P06EE.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit High
P06EE.description: Same as P0654 with the output line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P06EF.title: Engine Restart Performance
P06EF.description: After a stop-start auto-stop the engine takes longer than calibrated to restart, or restart is missed. Possible causes are weak starter, low battery state of charge, weak crank position signal at low RPM, or a fuel rail that lost prime.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P06F0.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit
P06F0.description: A general circuit fault on the internal temperature sensor of the reductant control module.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P06F1.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Range or Performance
P06F1.description: Same as P06F0 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine bay environment.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P06F2.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P06F2.description: Same as P06F0 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P06F6.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Control Circuit Open

Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)

P06F7.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Control Circuit Low

P06F9.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 System Voltage

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)

White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P06FA.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Performance
P06FA.description: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. This affects diesel cold-start preheating.
symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P06FB.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Memory Checksum Error
P06FB.description: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Memory Checksum Error: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects diesel cold-start preheating.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P06FC.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 to PCM Communication Circuit

causes.cause: Open or short on communication wire
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P06FE.title: Cold Start Diesel Intake Air Flow Control Performance
P06FE.description: During cold-start of a diesel engine the ECU controls intake airflow (e.g. anti-shudder valve, swirl flaps) to support smooth ignition. The control loop does not deliver the expected airflow - flap stuck or position offset.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P06FF.title: Economy Mode Lamp Control Circuit
P06FF.description: Economy Mode Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.
symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P0700.title: Transmission Control System Malfunction
P0700.description: A request from the transmission control module (TCM) to illuminate the MIL. P0700 itself carries no specific information — it is a wrapper that tells the engine ECU "the TCM has a code". Read the TCM directly to find the actual transmission DTC.

causes.cause: TCM has a sub-code that needs to be read separately

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0701.title: Transmission Control System Range/Performance
P0701.description: The TCM has detected a transmission performance issue without identifying a specific component fault — typically slip outside expected range, shift timing outside spec, or a hydraulic issue not yet diagnosed by a more specific code.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0702.title: Transmission Control System Electrical
P0702.description: A general electrical fault is detected in the transmission control system. The TCM has flagged a circuit problem (open, short, or supply issue) without specifying which component. Look up additional codes from the TCM for detail.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0703.title: Brake Switch B Circuit
P0703.description: A general circuit fault on the secondary brake switch B - typically used as redundant input for safety-critical functions like cruise control cancellation and shift-interlock.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0704.title: Clutch Switch Input Circuit
P0704.description: A circuit fault on the clutch pedal position switch input - used by the ECU to inhibit cruise control, allow cranking, and time gear-shift events on manual transmissions.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0705.title: Transmission Range Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0705.description: The transmission range sensor (PRNDL switch / inhibitor switch) signal is implausible — multiple positions active simultaneously, or no position recognized. Engine may refuse to start unless P or N is detected.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0706.title: Transmission Range Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0706.description: The transmission range sensor reports a position that is implausible against vehicle speed and engine state. Often caused by sensor misadjustment or worn contacts.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0707.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Low
P0707.description: The primary transmission range sensor A (PRNDL switch position) reports voltage below the plausible range - signal shorted to ground or sensor fault.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P070F.description: The fluid level sensor reports level below the safe minimum - risk of pump cavitation, hydraulic pressure loss and gearbox damage. Drive carefully or stop and refill.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0710.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0710.description: The transmission fluid temperature sensor A signal is missing or out of range. Used by shift logic to adapt timings to fluid viscosity.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0711.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range or Performance
P0711.description: The transmission fluid temperature sensor A reports a value within plausible range yet not matching the engine model - sensor drift or slow response.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0712.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0712.description: ATF temperature sensor signal voltage below the lower threshold — open, short to ground, or sensor fault.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0715.title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor "A" Circuit Malfunction
P0715.description: The transmission input speed (turbine) sensor signal is missing or implausible. Without this signal, the TCM cannot detect torque converter slip or calculate gear ratio in real time, and shifts become harsh.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0716.title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance
P0716.description: The transmission input/turbine speed sensor signal is implausible compared to engine RPM and current gear ratio. Often caused by a failing sensor, debris on the reluctor, or wiring noise.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0717.title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0717.description: TCM detects no signal from the input/turbine speed sensor while the engine is running and the transmission is in gear. Without this signal the TCM cannot compute slip, and the transmission usually enters limp mode.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0718.title: Input or Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0718.description: Input or Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent: the signal is intermittent or erratic. Often a loose connector or chafed wiring; a wiggle test often locates it.

P0720.title: Output Speed Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0720.description: The transmission output speed sensor signal is missing or implausible. The TCM uses this signal together with input speed to determine actual gear ratio; many vehicles also use it as a backup vehicle speed signal for the cluster and ECU.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0721.title: Output Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0721.description: The transmission output speed sensor signal is implausible compared to vehicle speed and gear ratio. Sometimes set together with VSS or input-speed-sensor codes.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0722.title: Output Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0722.description: TCM detects no output shaft speed signal while the vehicle is moving. Triggers shift abnormalities, speedometer issues, and limp-home mode.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0723.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0723.description: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent: the signal is intermittent or erratic. Often a loose connector or chafed wiring; a wiggle test often locates it.

P0726.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit Range or Performance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P0728.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit Intermittent

P0729.title: Gear 6 Incorrect Ratio
P0729.description: When gear 6 is engaged, the measured ratio between the input- and output-shaft speed sensors does not match the expected ratio for that gear. This means the transmission is slipping in gear 6 rather than transmitting power solidly. Causes: worn clutch packs or bands, low fluid level or pressure, a stuck shift solenoid, or a valve-body fault affecting gear 6.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P072A.title: Stuck in Neutral

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P072B.title: Stuck In Reverse

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P072C.title: Stuck in Gear 1

Causes: a stuck or failed shift solenoid, a valve-body fault, a hydraulic pressure problem, or internal mechanical damage.

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
