Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P20D7.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit/Open
P20D7.description: The control circuit for the dedicated aftertreatment fuel supply pump or solenoid is open — HC dosing into the exhaust will fail.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P20D8.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Performance
P20D8.description: Aftertreatment fuel supply is electrically OK but does not deliver the commanded pressure or flow during regeneration — weak pump or partial blockage.

causes.cause: Pump weak — flow or pressure below threshold

P20D9.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit Low
P20D9.description: Aftertreatment fuel supply control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P20DA.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit High
P20DA.description: Aftertreatment fuel supply control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P20DB.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Stuck Open
P20DB.description: Aftertreatment fuel supply solenoid stuck open mechanically — fuel pressure cannot be cut off, risk of over-fueling exhaust.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20DC.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Stuck Closed
P20DC.description: Aftertreatment fuel supply solenoid stuck closed — HC dosing into exhaust fails, regeneration cannot raise temperature.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P20DD.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit
P20DD.description: A general electrical fault is reported on the aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor — used to verify the dedicated HC-dosing rail is primed.
symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P20DE.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P20DE.description: Aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor reads in range but plausibility fails — pressure does not rise during prime, drift across a regeneration.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P20DF.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P20DF.description: Aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P20E0.title: Reductant Pressure Too Low
P20E0.description: The pressure in the SCR reductant (AdBlue/DEF) line is below the calibrated minimum. Without sufficient pressure the dosing module cannot atomise reagent properly, leading to NOx exceedence.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E1.title: Reductant Pressure Too Low
P20E1.description: The reductant (AdBlue/DEF) line pressure stays below the demanded value during dosing. The dosing system needs a stable supply pressure to inject metered amounts; without it the system cannot meet NOx targets.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E2.title: Reductant Pressure Too High
P20E2.description: The reductant line pressure exceeds the upper limit. A blocked return path, a stuck pump or a faulty pressure sensor are common causes; over-pressure can damage the dosing valve and the pump head.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E3.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/3 Correlation (Bank 1)
P20E3.description: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/3 Correlation (Bank 1): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

causes.cause: Exhaust leak between the two sensor positions

P20E4.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 2/3 Correlation (Bank 1)
P20E4.description: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 2/3 Correlation (Bank 1): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

P20E5.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 2)
P20E5.description: EGT sensors 1 and 3 on bank 2 disagree by more than the allowed tolerance — one is reading off, or there is a real temperature gradient that exceeds the calibrated map (e.g. from a leaking exhaust joint between the two locations).

P20E6.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too Low
P20E6.description: The DEF system air-assist pressure is below the required threshold — pump weak, line leak, or pressure-control valve stuck open.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E7.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too High
P20E7.description: The DEF system air-assist pressure exceeds the upper threshold — pressure-control valve stuck closed or air pump runaway.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E8.title: Reductant Pressure Too Low
P20E8.description: Pressure in the AdBlue/DEF supply line is below the target. Usually a failing reductant pump, a clogged filter, frozen lines, or a leak in the pressurised circuit.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E9.title: Reductant Pressure Too High
P20E9.description: Manufacturer-specific variant of the reductant over-pressure condition. The pressure exceeds the upper threshold during a defined operating window; on some platforms used in addition to P20E2 to flag a different test path.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20EA.title: Reductant Pump Control Circuit Open
P20EA.description: The control circuit to the reductant (DEF) dosing pump is open — no current flow detected. Without pump pressure no AdBlue reaches the SCR catalyst and NOx reduction stops.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20EB.title: Reductant Reservoir Heater "A" Control Circuit
P20EB.description: A general electrical fault on the reductant tank heater "A" control circuit. AdBlue freezes at -11 C, so the tank heater must work for cold-start dosing.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20EC.title: Reductant Heater "A" Control Stuck Off
P20EC.description: The reductant tank heater "A" does not heat when commanded on. Either a failed element or a stuck-off driver in the dosing module.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20ED.title: Reductant Heater "A" Control Stuck On
P20ED.description: The reductant tank heater "A" stays energised even when not commanded — usually a shorted driver stage. Continuous heating wastes current and can overheat the heater element.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20EE.title: NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P20EE.description: The SCR catalyst on bank 1 is no longer reducing NOx to the level the ECU expects, even with proper reductant dosing and quality. Often the result of catalyst poisoning by sulphur or hydrocarbons, thermal aging, or a leak between the upstream and downstream NOx sensors.

causes.cause: Exhaust leak between upstream and downstream NOx sensors

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P20EF.title: Reductant Injection Valve Performance
P20EF.description: The SCR reductant injection valve does not deliver the commanded amount of reagent. Causes include clogging by urea crystals, electrical faults or incorrect spray pattern.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20F0.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P20F0.description: SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2): the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P20F1.title: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P20F1.description: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2): the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P20F2.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F2.description: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.cause: Catalyst poisoning from sulphur or oil ash

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P20F3.title: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F3.description: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P20F4.title: Reductant Consumption Too Low
P20F4.description: The DEF consumption observed over the dosing window is below the model expectation — typically a clogged dosing nozzle, weak pump, or leak between pump and injector that recirculates DEF back to the tank.

causes.cause: Dosing nozzle clogged with crystallised DEF

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20F5.title: Reductant Consumption Too High
P20F5.description: The DEF consumption observed over the dosing window is above the model expectation — typically a leaking injector seat, leaking line fitting, or a pressure-control valve that vents constantly to the tank.

causes.cause: Injector seat leaks DEF into exhaust

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20F6.title: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P20F6.description: The DEF injection valve at bank 1 unit 1 does not close when commanded — DEF flows continuously into the SCR. Risk of crystallisation in the catalyst and over-dosing.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20F7.title: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P20F7.description: The DEF injection valve at bank 2 unit 1 does not close when commanded — DEF flows continuously into the SCR. Risk of crystallisation in the catalyst and over-dosing.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20F8.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 1)
P20F8.description: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 1 is electrically OK but its current draw or duty-cycle response is outside the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or a partially shorted driver.

P20F9.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 2)
P20F9.description: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 2 is electrically OK but its current draw or duty-cycle response is outside the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or a partially shorted driver.

P20FA.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
P20FA.description: The control line driving DEF pump B is open. On large engines or dual-tank systems a second pump (B) supplements pump A; with B offline the system loses redundancy.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20FB.title: Reductant Pump B Control Performance/Stuck Off
P20FB.description: DEF pump B receives a run command but does not start, or shuts off prematurely.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20FC.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P20FC.description: DEF pump B control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20FD.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit High
P20FD.description: DEF pump B control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20FE.title: Reductant Metering Unit 1 Performance
P20FE.description: The first DEF metering unit (the integrated module that combines pump, filter, level sensor, and dosing valve) is electrically OK but does not deliver the expected pressure or flow during operation.

causes.cause: Metering unit aged or partially clogged

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20FF.title: Reductant Control Module Performance
P20FF.description: The dedicated SCR/reductant control module reports an internal performance fault — failed self-tests, watchdog resets, or calibration mismatch. Frequently a forerunner of total module failure.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2100.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Open
P2100.description: The drive-by-wire throttle motor circuit is open — no current flow detected. The ECU loses authority over the throttle plate and forces a limp-home with reduced power.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2101.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P2101.description: The throttle motor responds, but its actual position does not track the commanded position within tolerance. Often a dirty throttle bore where the plate sticks, or a worn motor.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2102.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Low
P2102.description: Drive voltage to the throttle motor is below the lower limit. Typically a short to ground or a failed driver stage in the ECU.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2103.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit High
P2103.description: Drive voltage to the throttle motor is above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply or an open ground.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2104.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Idle
P2104.description: The ECU has detected a fault severe enough that it forces the throttle actuator to the idle stop. The driver loses pedal authority — only idle is available until the underlying TAC fault clears.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2105.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Engine Shutdown
P2105.description: The TAC monitor commanded an engine shutdown because throttle authority can no longer be guaranteed safely. The most aggressive TAC limp mode — used when both throttle position sensors disagree or the motor is uncontrollable.

causes.cause: TPS1 and TPS2 disagree beyond limit

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2106.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Limited Power
P2106.description: The TAC monitor restricts maximum throttle opening as a safety response to a TAC fault. The vehicle can still be driven, but accelerator pedal travel is capped.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2107.title: Throttle Actuator Control Module Internal Processor
P2107.description: The internal processor or watchdog of the throttle actuator control module reports an internal fault. Communication between the TAC monitor core and the main ECU core has failed plausibility — typical for a defective ECU.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2108.title: Throttle Actuator Control Module Performance
P2108.description: Self-tests within the TAC module fail their performance criteria — for example RAM/ROM checks or analog reference voltages drift. Indicates an aging ECU rather than a wiring fault.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2109.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
P2109.description: The ECU detects that the throttle position sensor A signal at the closed-throttle stop does not match the learned minimum value. The mechanical or electrical zero reference of the throttle has drifted out of the expected range, often after cleaning, replacement or wear.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit/Open
P210A.description: The drive circuit of throttle actuator motor B is open. Throttle B is the secondary throttle on engines with two throttle bodies — typically used for tumble flap or charge-motion control.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210B.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P210B.description: Throttle actuator B motor responds electrically but does not move the throttle plate as commanded — typically high-resistance brushes, partial winding fault, or a sticky throttle bore.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210C.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Low
P210C.description: Throttle actuator B motor drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210D.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit High
P210D.description: Throttle actuator B motor drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210E.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C/F Voltage Correlation
P210E.description: The redundant throttle or accelerator pedal position channels C and F disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Drive-by-wire systems compare two or three independent channels to detect a faulty potentiometer track.

causes.cause: One potentiometer track worn — voltage drift

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210F.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Forced Limited RPM
P210F.description: Throttle B control has detected an unsafe condition and forced an RPM limit. Common protective response when motor current, throttle position feedback, or supply voltage on the B path is out of spec.

causes.cause: Protection mode triggered by paired throttle-B fault

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2110.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Limited RPM
P2110.description: The TAC monitor caps engine speed at a fixed limp-home rpm because it can no longer trust the throttle response. Driver may notice a hard rev limit well below redline.

causes.cause: Underlying TAC fault triggers rpm cap
Throttle response time out of spec

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2111.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Stuck Open
P2111.description: The throttle plate cannot be commanded back to the closed/idle position. Idle speed runs high or the engine cannot decelerate properly — safety-critical fault that usually triggers immediate limp mode.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2112.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Stuck Closed
P2112.description: The throttle plate cannot be commanded open. The engine stays at idle or stalls under load. Often caused by a seized motor, broken gear, or heavy carbon coking inside the throttle bore.

causes.cause: Throttle motor seized or gear broken
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2113.title: Throttle Actuator Control System Forced Limited RPM
P2113.description: The throttle actuator control has detected a fault and limits engine speed to a defined emergency value. The vehicle stays drivable but with severely reduced power until the underlying fault is cleared.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2114.title: Throttle Actuator Control System Forced Below Limit RPM
P2114.description: The throttle actuator system has dropped engine speed below the normal limp limit because of a more serious fault. The engine may run only at idle or stall.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2115.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
P2115.description: The minimum stop calibration of throttle position sensor A is outside the expected range during the ECU self-check. The signal at fully closed throttle does not match the stored reference, indicating a mechanical or sensor issue.

causes.cause: Throttle plate sticking due to carbon

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2116.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Minimum Stop Performance
P2116.description: The minimum stop calibration of throttle position sensor B does not match the learned reference during ECU self-test. Sensor B is the redundant channel used to cross-check sensor A.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2117.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Minimum Stop Performance
P2117.description: The minimum stop signal from throttle/pedal position sensor C is out of specification during initialization. Used on systems with three redundant sensor channels for safety-critical drive-by-wire control.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2118.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P2118.description: The current draw of the throttle motor lies outside the expected range — either much higher (binding plate) or much lower (worn brushes, open winding) than calibrated.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2119.title: Throttle Closed Position Performance
P2119.description: When commanded to idle, the throttle plate does not reach the calibrated closed position. Often a coked throttle bore preventing the plate from seating fully.

causes.cause: Throttle bore coked at closed-position stop
Plate or stop misadjusted after service

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Open
P211A.description: Throttle B is mechanically stuck open — typically carbon buildup or a broken return spring on the secondary throttle plate.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211B.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Closed
P211B.description: Throttle B is mechanically stuck closed — carbon buildup or a seized bearing on the secondary throttle.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211C.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P211C.description: Throttle B motor current draw does not match the calibrated map for the commanded position — high friction, partial short, or stiction.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211D.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
P211D.description: The throttle B body itself does not respond as commanded — position feedback is plausible but does not track the setpoint within the calibrated time window.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211E.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Processor
P211E.description: The processor monitoring throttle B inside the throttle/PCM has reported a self-test failure — RAM check, ROM check, or watchdog timeout.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211F.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Performance
P211F.description: The throttle control module on the B path reports general performance issues — internal fault, communication mismatch, or calibration drift.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2120.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit
P2120.description: A general electrical fault on the "C" channel of the throttle or pedal position sensor. Drive-by-wire pedals carry two or three redundant tracks; "C" is the third channel.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2121.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Range/Performance
P2121.description: The "C" channel of the throttle or pedal sensor produces an electrically valid signal that does not match the other channels or the operating point.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2122.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit Low
P2122.description: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2123.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit High
P2123.description: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2124.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit Low
P2124.description: The "C" channel signal is below the lower threshold — usually a short to ground or an open signal wire.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2125.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit High
P2125.description: The "C" channel signal is above the upper threshold — typically a short to positive or an open ground.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2126.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit Intermittent
P2126.description: The "C" channel produces an intermittent signal — usually a marginal connector or a worn track inside the pedal sensor.

causes.cause: Track C worn at common pedal angle

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2127.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit Low
P2127.description: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2128.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit High
P2128.description: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2129.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit Intermittent
P2129.description: The "D" channel of the throttle or pedal sensor produces an intermittent signal — typically marginal connector contacts.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P212A.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit
P212A.description: A general electrical fault is reported on throttle position sensor G — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. Sensor G is part of a multi-channel redundancy on dual-throttle systems.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P212B.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Range/Performance
P212B.description: TPS G reads in range but plausibility check fails — value sticks, lags, or does not match the commanded throttle position.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P212C.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Low
P212C.description: TPS G below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P212D.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit High
P212D.description: TPS G above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P212E.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Intermittent
P212E.description: TPS G signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P212F.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F/G Voltage Correlation
P212F.description: Channels F and G of the throttle/pedal position sensor disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Drive-by-wire system has lost redundancy and may force limp mode.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2130.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit
P2130.description: A general electrical fault is reported on throttle/pedal position sensor F — open, shorted, or out of plausibility.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2131.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Range/Performance
P2131.description: The "E" channel of the pedal/throttle sensor produces electrically valid values that do not match other channels or the operating window.

causes.cause: Track E worn at common angle
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2132.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit Low
P2132.description: The "E" channel signal is below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or an open signal wire.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2133.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit High
P2133.description: The "E" channel signal is above the upper threshold — usually a short to positive or an open ground.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2134.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit Intermittent
P2134.description: TPS/APP sensor F signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2135.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A"/"B" Voltage Correlation
P2135.description: The two redundant throttle position sensors on the throttle body disagree by more than allowed. Distinct from P2138 which monitors the pedal pair — P2135 monitors the throttle-body pair on drive-by-wire systems.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2136.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A/C Voltage Correlation
P2136.description: The "A" and "C" channels of the throttle or pedal sensor disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. The ECU cannot trust either reading and forces limp-home with reduced torque.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2137.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B/C Voltage Correlation
P2137.description: The "B" and "C" channels of the throttle or pedal sensor disagree beyond tolerance — the ECU cannot trust either signal and reverts to limp-home.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2138.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D"/"E" Voltage Correlation
P2138.description: The two redundant accelerator pedal position sensors disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. The ECU cannot trust either signal and switches to limp-home with very limited torque. Often appears intermittently with a worn pedal sensor before failing outright.

causes.cause: Pedal position sensor worn or contaminated

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2139.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D/F Voltage Correlation
P2139.description: Channels D and F of the throttle/pedal position sensor disagree by more than the allowed tolerance.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P213A.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B/Open
P213A.description: The drive circuit of EGR throttle B is open. EGR throttles partially close intake to increase exhaust gas recirculation flow at low loads.

P213B.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B Range/Performance
P213B.description: EGR throttle B is electrically OK but does not move as commanded — typically carbon buildup or a sticking actuator.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P213C.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B Low
P213C.description: EGR throttle B drive line stuck low — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P213D.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B High
P213D.description: EGR throttle B drive line stuck high — short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P213E.title: Fuel Injection System Fault - Forced Engine Shutdown
P213E.description: A safety-critical fuel-injection fault has been detected and the PCM has shut down the engine to prevent damage. Examples are common-rail pressure runaway, multiple stuck-open injectors, or HPFP failure.

P213F.title: Fuel Pump System Fault - Forced Engine Shutdown
P213F.description: A safety-critical fuel-pump fault has been detected and the engine has been shut down. Typical for HPFP runaway or low-pressure pump that loses control authority.
symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2140.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E/F Voltage Correlation
P2140.description: Channels E and F of the throttle/pedal position sensor disagree by more than the allowed tolerance.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2141.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A Low
P2141.description: EGR throttle A drive line stuck low — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P2142.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A High
P2142.description: EGR throttle A drive line stuck high — short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P2143.title: EGR Vent Control Circuit/Open
P2143.description: The drive circuit of the EGR vent solenoid is open — the solenoid releases vacuum from the EGR actuator. Open circuit means the EGR cannot reset its position.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2144.title: EGR Vent Control Circuit Low
P2144.description: EGR vent solenoid drive line stuck low — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2145.title: EGR Vent Control Circuit High
P2145.description: EGR vent solenoid drive line stuck high — short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2146.title: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2146.description: The ECU detects an open or missing supply voltage on injector group A. The injectors of this bank cannot be energized; the affected cylinders may not fire and the engine runs rough or stalls.
symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2147.title: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2147.description: The supply voltage measured at injector group A is below the calibrated threshold. Either the supply is shorted to ground or the source voltage has collapsed during cranking or load.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2148.title: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2148.description: The injector group A supply voltage exceeds the calibrated upper limit. Often a sign of a short to battery voltage on the supply line, an over-charging alternator or an internal driver failure.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2149.title: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2149.description: The ECU detects an open or missing supply voltage on injector group B. The injectors on this bank cannot be energized, leading to misfire on the affected cylinders.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P214A.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High
P214A.description: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P214B.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration
P214B.description: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P214C.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High
P214C.description: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P214D.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration
P214D.description: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P214E.title: Reductant Pump A Current Too High
P214E.description: DEF pump A current draw exceeds the upper threshold — typically a seized pump head or partial winding short.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P214F.title: Reductant Heater A Current Too High
P214F.description: DEF heater A current draw exceeds the upper threshold — typically a partial short in the heating element.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2150.title: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2150.description: The supply voltage feeding injector group B has dropped below the lower limit. The injectors in this group lose drive voltage and may stop firing, so the cylinders they serve run lean or cut out. Causes: a blown fuse, a failed injector supply relay, a voltage drop in the supply harness, or a poor ground or connector on the group-B supply.

causes.cause: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2151.title: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2151.description: The supply voltage on injector group B is above the upper limit. Overvoltage on the group-B supply can mis-time or damage the injectors. Causes: charging-system overvoltage, a stuck supply relay or regulator, or a wiring fault shorting the group-B supply to a higher voltage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2152.title: Fuel Injector Group C Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2152.description: The supply rail to injector group C is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. The affected cylinders produce no power and the engine runs rough or on reduced cylinders. Causes: a broken supply wire, an open relay or fuse, or a disconnected group-C supply connector.

causes.cause: Open supply wire or blown fuse
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2153.title: Fuel Injector Group C Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2153.description: The supply voltage feeding injector group C has dropped below the lower limit. Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2154.description: The supply voltage on injector group C is above the upper limit. Overvoltage on the group-C supply can mis-time or damage the injectors. Causes: charging-system overvoltage, a stuck supply relay or regulator, or a wiring fault shorting the group-C supply to a higher voltage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2155.title: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2155.description: The supply rail to injector group D is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. The affected cylinders produce no power and the engine runs rough or on reduced cylinders. Causes: a broken supply wire, an open relay or fuse, or a disconnected group-D supply connector.

causes.cause: Open supply wire or blown fuse
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2156.title: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2156.description: The supply voltage feeding injector group D has dropped below the lower limit. The injectors in this group lose drive voltage and may stop firing, so the cylinders they serve run lean or cut out. Causes: a blown fuse, a failed injector supply relay, a voltage drop in the supply harness, or a poor ground or connector on the group-D supply.

causes.cause: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2157.title: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2157.description: The supply voltage on injector group D is above the upper limit. Overvoltage on the group-D supply can mis-time or damage the injectors. Causes: charging-system overvoltage, a stuck supply relay or regulator, or a wiring fault shorting the group-D supply to a higher voltage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2158.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit
P2158.description: A general electrical fault is reported on vehicle speed sensor B — second VSS used either at the transmission output or as redundancy. Open, short, or implausible signal.

P2159.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Range/Performance
P2159.description: The signal of the secondary vehicle speed sensor is implausible compared to other sensors. The ECU cannot use the value for fuel and ignition control or transmission shifting.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P215A.title: Vehicle Speed - Wheel Speed Correlation
P215A.description: The vehicle speed signal computed from VSS does not match the wheel-speed signal from ABS within tolerance. One of the two sources is wrong, or there is a tyre-size mismatch.

P215B.title: Vehicle Speed - Output Shaft Speed Correlation
P215B.description: VSS does not match transmission output-shaft speed within tolerance. Possible transmission slip, sensor fault, or harness issue.

P215C.title: Output Shaft Speed - Wheel Speed Correlation
P215C.description: Transmission output-shaft speed does not match ABS wheel speed within tolerance — typically transmission slip, driveline fault, or one sensor drift.

P215D.title: Reductant Pump B Stuck On
P215D.description: Reductant Pump B Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P215E.title: Reductant Heater D Current Too Low
P215E.description: DEF heater D current draw is below threshold — typically a partially-open winding.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P215F.title: Reductant Heater D Current Too High
P215F.description: DEF heater D current draw exceeds threshold — element partially shorted.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2160.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P2160.description: VSS B reads below lower plausibility — short to ground or sensor not signalling. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2161.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic/High
P2161.description: VSS B signal jumps, drops out, or reads above plausibility — connector or harness issue, or magnetic ring damaged.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2162.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A/B Correlation
P2162.description: VSS A and VSS B disagree by more than the allowed tolerance.

P2163.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Maximum Stop Performance
P2163.description: Throttle/pedal position sensor A does not reach the calibrated maximum-stop value during the wide-open self-test. Sensor wear, mechanical stop misalignment, or a stuck pedal.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

Idle too high or too low

P2169.title: Exhaust Pressure Regulator Vent Solenoid Control Circuit/Open
P2169.description: The drive circuit of the exhaust pressure regulator vent solenoid is open. The solenoid releases pressure from the exhaust backpressure regulator, which is part of the exhaust brake system on diesel trucks.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P216A.title: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P216A.description: The supply rail to injector group E is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. The affected cylinders produce no power and the engine runs rough or on reduced cylinders. Causes: a broken supply wire, an open relay or fuse, or a disconnected group-E supply connector.

causes.cause: Open supply wire or blown fuse
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P216B.title: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P216B.description: The supply voltage feeding injector group E has dropped below the lower limit. The injectors in this group lose drive voltage and may stop firing, so the cylinders they serve run lean or cut out. Causes: a blown fuse, a failed injector supply relay, a voltage drop in the supply harness, or a poor ground or connector on the group-E supply.

causes.cause: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P216C.title: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit High
P216C.description: The supply voltage on injector group E is above the upper limit. Overvoltage on the group-E supply can mis-time or damage the injectors. Causes: charging-system overvoltage, a stuck supply relay or regulator, or a wiring fault shorting the group-E supply to a higher voltage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2170.description: EPR vent solenoid drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2171.title: Exhaust Pressure Regulator Vent Solenoid Control Circuit High
P2171.description: EPR vent solenoid drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

P2172.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Sudden High Air Flow Detected
P2172.description: A sudden, large jump in MAF/MAP signal not matched by a corresponding pedal change has been detected — typically a torn intake boot, dropped MAF sensor, or actively-stuck-open throttle plate.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2173.title: High Airflow/Vacuum Leak Detected (Slow Accumulation)
P2173.description: Long-term fuel and air adaptation values indicate a slow but continuous excess of air entering the engine. The ECU concludes that an unmetered air leak is gradually growing in the intake system.

causes.cause: Cracked vacuum hose or intake gasket

P2174.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Sudden Low Air Flow Detected
P2174.description: A sudden, large drop in MAF/MAP signal not matched by a pedal change — typically intake restriction, MAF failure, or actively-stuck-closed throttle plate.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2175.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Low Air Flow Detected
P2175.description: Sustained low air-flow condition detected — slower than P2174 but persistent. Restricted air filter, dirty MAF, or partially-stuck throttle.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2176.title: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
P2176.description: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Idle Position Not Learned: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2177.title: System Too Lean Off Idle Bank 1
P2177.description: Fuel trim values on bank 1 indicate a lean condition during off-idle operation. The ECU has to add significant fuel correction to maintain stoichiometric mixture above idle.

P2178.title: System Too Rich Off Idle Bank 1
P2178.description: Bank 1 fuel trim shows a strong rich correction during off-idle operation. The ECU is forced to subtract fuel to keep the mixture near stoichiometric.
symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2179.title: System Too Lean Off Idle Bank 2
P2179.description: Fuel trims on bank 2 show a lean deviation during off-idle operating conditions. Causes are similar to bank 1 but isolated to the second cylinder bank.

P217A.description: The supply rail to injector group G is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. P2180.title: System Too Rich Off Idle Bank 2
P2180.description: Bank 2 fuel trim shows a rich shift during off-idle conditions. The ECU subtracts fuel to maintain proper combustion. Common causes are stuck injectors or excess fuel pressure.
symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2181.title: Cooling System Performance
P2181.description: The engine cooling system does not reach or maintain the expected temperature within the diagnostic window — usually a stuck-open thermostat, but also a low coolant level or a stuck cooling fan that overcools the engine.

P2182.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit
P2182.description: A general electrical fault is reported on engine coolant temperature sensor 2 — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. Sensor 2 is typically at the radiator outlet or as redundancy on the second cylinder bank.
symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P2183.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
P2183.description: ECT sensor 2 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response, stuck reading, or value does not track ECT 1 across a warm-up.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P2184.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P2184.description: ECT sensor 2 reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P2185.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit High
P2185.description: The second coolant temperature sensor (often radiator-outlet or cylinder-head bank) reports a voltage above the upper threshold — typically an open signal wire or a sensor with infinite resistance.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P2186.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P2186.description: The second coolant temperature sensor reports a voltage below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or a sensor with very low resistance.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P2187.title: System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)
P2187.description: Fuel trim on bank 1 hits the lean limit only at idle, while trim returns to normal at higher load. This pattern strongly indicates a vacuum leak — leaks become a larger fraction of total airflow at idle and so dominate the trim, but disappear into background noise above idle.

causes.cause: Vacuum leak (intake gasket, brake booster, hoses)

P2188.title: System Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1)
P2188.description: Fuel trim on bank 1 hits the rich limit only at idle. Often a leaking injector dribbling fuel at low load, a sticky purge valve dumping fuel vapour, or fuel pressure regulator that fails to relieve pressure when intake vacuum is high.
symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2189.title: System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 2)
P2189.description: Fuel trim on bank 2 hits the lean limit only at idle, while trim returns to normal at higher load. This pattern strongly indicates a vacuum leak — leaks become a larger fraction of total airflow at idle and so dominate the trim, but disappear into background noise above idle.

P218A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
P218A.description: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Idle Position Not Learned: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P218B.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit
P218B.description: A general electrical fault on the throttle/fuel inhibit signal B — used by anti-theft, immobiliser, or transmission to forbid throttle/fuel until released.

P218C.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit Range/Performance
P218C.description: Throttle/fuel inhibit B signal reads in range but plausibility fails — does not assert/release as expected.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P218D.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit Low
P218D.description: Throttle/fuel inhibit B line stuck low. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P218E.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit High
P218E.description: Throttle/fuel inhibit B line stuck high. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P218F.title: Reductant No Flow Detected
P218F.description: The DEF dosing system commands flow but the pressure or flow sensor reports no actual delivery — typically a fully blocked dosing nozzle, a frozen line, or a dead pump.

causes.cause: Dosing line or nozzle fully blocked
Line frozen at very low ambient temperature

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2190.title: System Too Rich at Idle (Bank 2)
P2190.description: Fuel trim on bank 2 hits the rich limit only at idle. Often a leaking injector dribbling fuel at low load, a sticky purge valve dumping fuel vapour, or fuel pressure regulator that fails to relieve pressure when intake vacuum is high.

causes.cause: Leaking injector at idle on bank 2

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2191.title: System Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P2191.description: Bank 1 fuel trim hits the lean limit only at higher engine load. Pattern points to a fuel-supply restriction — failing fuel pump, blocked filter, or weak injectors — rather than a vacuum leak (which would dominate at idle).

causes.cause: MAF reads low at high airflow

P2192.title: System Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P2192.description: Bank 1 fuel trim hits the rich limit only at higher load. Often excessive fuel pressure, a stuck-closed MAF reading low, or coolant temperature signal stuck cold causing over-fuelling.
symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2193.title: System Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P2193.description: Bank 2 fuel trim hits the lean limit only at higher engine load. Pattern points to a fuel-supply restriction — failing fuel pump, blocked filter, or weak injectors — rather than a vacuum leak (which would dominate at idle).

P2194.title: System Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P2194.description: Bank 2 fuel trim hits the rich limit only at higher load. Often excessive fuel pressure, a stuck-closed MAF reading low, or coolant temperature signal stuck cold causing over-fuelling.
symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2195.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P2195.description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 returns a constant lean signal during conditions where rich content is expected (for example after a deceleration fuel cut-off recovery). Usually a sensor that has lost its rich-side response or a slow heater warm-up.

causes.cause: Sensor heater slow to warm up

P2196.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P2196.description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 returns a constant rich signal under deceleration fuel cut-off where lean is expected. Often a contaminated sensor (silicone, oil, coolant) or short to ground that pulls the signal high in some sensor types.

P2197.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P2197.description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 returns a constant lean signal during conditions where rich content is expected (for example after a deceleration fuel cut-off recovery). Usually a sensor that has lost its rich-side response or a slow heater warm-up.

P2198.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P2198.description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 returns a constant rich signal under deceleration fuel cut-off where lean is expected. Often a contaminated sensor (silicone, oil, coolant) or short to ground that pulls the signal high in some sensor types.

P2199.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P2199.description: The two intake air temperature sensors disagree by more than the calibrated correlation threshold during stable conditions. The ECU cannot determine which value is correct.

P219A.title: Bank 1 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P219A.description: The fuel-trim values across cylinders on bank 1 differ enough that the bank-average air-fuel ratio is biased — a single cylinder is significantly leaner or richer than the rest. Detected by short-term-fuel-trim variance or by the wide-band O2 sensor harmonic monitor.

causes.cause: Vacuum leak at one intake runner

P219B.title: Bank 2 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance

P21A8.description: A general electrical fault is reported on DEF level sensor B — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. Some tanks use multiple level senders to cover irregular tank shapes; this is the primary one.

P21B5.title: NOx Adsorber Over Temperature (Bank 2)

Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

Possible no-start countdown after ignore period
