causes.cause: Supply line open or relay defective
Fuse for regulator B supply blown
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P233E.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit Low
P233E.description: The supply line that powers the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator B is below the expected voltage with the regulator commanded active - typically a high-resistance feed, partial short to ground or weak relay contact.

causes.cause: Supply feed has high contact resistance
Partial short to ground on supply line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P233F.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit High
P233F.description: Same as P233D but with the supply line shorted to a higher potential than expected, so the ECU measures more voltage on the regulator B feed than the commanded level allows.

causes.cause: Supply line shorted to a higher voltage rail
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2340.title: Cylinder 5 Above Knock Threshold
P2340.description: The knock-sensor evaluation reports cylinder 5 above the knock threshold over a sustained window. The ECU retards ignition for that cylinder; persistent knock indicates poor fuel quality, carbon deposits or cooling issues.

P2341.title: Cylinder 6 Above Knock Threshold
P2341.description: Same condition as P2340 but on cylinder 6 — sustained knock above the threshold with retarded ignition correction.

P2342.title: Cylinder 7 Above Knock Threshold
P2342.description: Sustained knock above the threshold on cylinder 7 — usual causes are fuel quality, carbon deposits, or cooling issues at this cylinder.

P2343.title: Cylinder 8 Above Knock Threshold
P2343.description: Sustained knock above the threshold on cylinder 8 — typical on V8 engines under load with poor fuel.

P2344.title: Cylinder 9 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold
P2344.description: The knock or combustion-vibration sensor monitors the structure-borne noise of each cylinder. The signal level for cylinder 9 has stayed above the diagnostic threshold for an extended period, indicating either persistent knock or an electrical fault that biases the channel high.

causes.cause: Persistent knocking on cylinder 9 (low-octane fuel, carbon deposits, hot spot)
Sensor or wiring biased high by short or moisture
Mechanical knock from bearings, piston pin or wrong torque

P2345.title: Cylinder 10 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold
P2345.description: The knock or combustion-vibration sensor monitors the structure-borne noise of each cylinder. The signal level for cylinder 10 has stayed above the diagnostic threshold for an extended period, indicating either persistent knock or an electrical fault that biases the channel high.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

causes.cause: Injector B for cylinder 6 has drifted in flow rate

P23F8.title: Cylinder 7 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23F8.description: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 7 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.cause: Injector B for cylinder 7 has drifted in flow rate

P23F9.title: Cylinder 8 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23F9.description: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 8 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.cause: Injector B for cylinder 8 has drifted in flow rate

P23FA.title: Cylinder 9 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FA.description: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 9 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.cause: Injector B for cylinder 9 has drifted in flow rate

P23FB.title: Cylinder 10 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FB.description: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 10 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.cause: Injector B for cylinder 10 has drifted in flow rate

P23FC.title: Cylinder 11 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FC.description: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 11 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.cause: Injector B for cylinder 11 has drifted in flow rate

P23FD.title: Cylinder 12 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FD.description: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 12 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.cause: Injector B for cylinder 12 has drifted in flow rate

P23FE.title: Bank 1 System B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FE.description: The secondary fuel system B on bank 1 (e.g. port-injection rail in a dual-injection engine, or LPG/CNG rail in a bi-fuel system) does not maintain calibrated mixture - lambda response on bank 1 is biased by an offset on the B system.

P23FF.title: Bank 2 System B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FF.description: The secondary fuel system B on bank 2 (e.g. port-injection rail in a dual-injection engine, or LPG/CNG rail in a bi-fuel system) does not maintain calibrated mixture - lambda response on bank 2 is biased by an offset on the B system.

P2400.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Open
P2400.description: The control circuit to the EVAP leak-detection pump is open. Without that pump the ECU cannot pressurise the fuel-vapour system to test for leaks.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2401.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Low
P2401.description: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is below the lower limit. Often a short to ground in the harness.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2402.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit High
P2402.description: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply or open ground.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2403.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Open
P2403.description: The leak detection pump (LDP) - which actively pressurises the EVAP system to find leaks - has an open sense circuit. The ECU cannot read the pump status during the diagnostic cycle.

causes.cause: Open in pump or sense wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2404.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2404.description: The sense (reed-switch or current-feedback) signal from the leak-detection pump is electrically valid but does not match expectations during a leak test. Often a worn pump diaphragm or a sticking reed contact.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2405.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Low
P2405.description: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage below the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2406.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit High
P2406.description: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage above the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2407.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2407.description: The leak detection pump returns a sense signal that is electrically valid but does not match the expected response during the pump's self-test or pressure cycle.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2408.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P2408.description: On vehicles with a sensed fuel cap, the cap-status signal is electrically valid but does not change as expected when the cap is opened or closed.

causes.cause: Cap seal aged, switch never seats
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2409.title: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Range or Performance
P2409.description: The sensor or switch that detects whether the fuel cap is properly closed reports a value within plausible range yet not matching driver action.

P240A.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Open
P240A.description: The leak detection pump heater - keeps the pump diaphragm warm in cold weather - has an open control circuit.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P240B.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Low
P240B.description: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to ground. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P240C.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit High
P240C.description: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to supply. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P240D.title: Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak
P240D.description: Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak: a leak has been detected in this brake-hydraulic circuit, which reduces braking pressure. Safety-critical.

P240E.title: Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Leak
P240E.description: Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Leak: a leak has been detected in this brake-hydraulic circuit, which reduces braking pressure. Safety-critical.

causes.cause: Hose, fitting or cylinder valve leak

P240F.title: EGR Slow Response
P240F.description: The EGR system reacts to commanded changes more slowly than calibrated - typically a partly clogged EGR cooler, sticky valve, or worn actuator.

P2410.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Stuck
P2410.description: The fuel cap status switch is stuck in one position — the ECU never sees the expected transition between open and closed.

P2411.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Circuit
P2411.description: A general electrical fault on the fuel cap sensor/switch circuit — open or short.

P2412.title: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P2412.description: Same as P2409 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2413.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation System Performance
P2413.description: The ECU monitors EGR flow indirectly through MAF, MAP or differential-pressure feedback and finds that actual EGR flow does not match the commanded value over a sustained period.

P2414.title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2414.description: Same as P237A but on the upstream sensor B1S1 (pre-catalyst). A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P2415.title: EVAP Switching Valve Circuit Open
P2415.description: The ECU detects an open circuit on the EVAP switching valve drive line. The valve cannot be commanded between its purge and isolation positions.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2416.title: EVAP Switching Valve Performance
P2416.description: The EVAP switching valve responds electrically but does not produce the expected pressure change. Often a stuck valve seat or a torn diaphragm.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2417.title: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Closed
P2417.description: The EVAP switching valve cannot reach the open position. Purge flow is blocked and the EVAP system cannot vent the canister.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2418.title: EVAP Switching Valve Control Circuit Performance
P2418.description: The evaporative switching valve — used on multi-path EVAP systems to route purge or pressure-test flow — does not respond as expected. Self-test fails because tank pressure does not change in the calibrated direction.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2419.title: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Open
P2419.description: The EVAP switching valve cannot close. Tank pressure cannot be isolated for the leak detection test, and purge routing may bypass the canister.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P241A.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
P241A.description: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 1 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

P241B.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 2 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
P241B.description: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 2 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

P241C.title: Throttle Actuator Control System Ice Blockage Bank 2
P241C.description: The throttle actuator on bank 2 cannot move because of ice formation - typical for very cold ambient temperature with humid intake. Engine de-ices on warm-up.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P241D.title: SCR Inducement Forced Engine Shutdown
P241D.description: The SCR inducement strategy (mandatory regulatory measure to enforce AdBlue refilling and emissions compliance) has reached the final stage and shut down the engine. Refill AdBlue and clear inducement fault to restart.

causes.cause: AdBlue tank empty or out of compliance

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P241E.title: Reductant Heater Coolant Control Valve Stuck Closed
P241E.description: The valve that routes engine coolant to heat the AdBlue lines is stuck closed - AdBlue lines do not warm up and may freeze in cold weather, blocking dosing.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P241F.title: EGR Cooler B Efficiency Below Threshold
P241F.description: The temperature drop across EGR cooler B is below the calibrated threshold - cooler is fouled with soot, has internal scaling, or coolant flow is restricted. Recirculated gas reaches the intake hotter than designed, increasing NOx and combustion temperatures.

causes.cause: Cooler fouled with soot or scaled

P2420.title: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Closed
P2420.description: The EVAP switching valve cannot open when commanded. Purge or test flow cannot reach the appropriate path and the leak monitor aborts.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2421.title: EVAP Vent Valve Stuck Open
P2421.description: The evaporative emission system vent valve does not close on command. The ECU detects that the evap system cannot hold pressure or vacuum because the canister is permanently vented to atmosphere.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2422.title: EVAP Canister Vent Valve Stuck Closed
P2422.description: The vent valve at the canister end of the EVAP system cannot open. Without ambient air entering the canister, fresh fuel cannot purge the stored vapors and refueling may trigger ORVR issues. Common with rusted or rodent-damaged vent valves.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2423.title: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P2423.description: The ECU determines that the hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 1 no longer holds enough HC during cold start to meet emission targets. Often due to ageing or thermal damage.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2424.title: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 2
P2424.description: The hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 2 - which traps HC during cold-start until the main catalyst lights off - is degraded; HC slip during cold start is above the calibrated threshold.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2425.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Open
P2425.description: The valve that admits coolant flow to the EGR cooler has an open control circuit - cooling cannot be enabled and EGR temperatures stay too high.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2426.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Low
P2426.description: Same as P2425 with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2427.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit High
P2427.description: Same as P2425 with the control line shorted to supply. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2428.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 1
P2428.description: An EGT sensor on bank 1 reports a temperature above the safety threshold for prolonged operation - typical for blocked DPF, restricted exhaust, or excessive fuelling. Risk of catalyst, DPF or turbo damage.

P2429.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 2
P2429.description: An EGT sensor on bank 2 reports a temperature above the safety threshold for prolonged operation - typical for blocked DPF, restricted exhaust, or excessive fuelling. Risk of catalyst, DPF or turbo damage.

P242A.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242A.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 3 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst). The ECU loses thermal protection feedback for the catalyst and DPF.

P242B.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242B.description: Same as P242A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P242C.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242C.description: Same as P242A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P242D.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242D.description: Same as P242A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P242E.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242E.description: Same as P242A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P242F.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Ash Accumulation Bank 1
P242F.description: The diesel particulate filter on bank 1 reports backpressure attributable to ash (non-combustible residue from oil and fuel additives, not removable by regeneration). The filter has reached the end of its service life and needs cleaning or replacement.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2430.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P2430.description: A general circuit fault on the secondary air injection (AIR) system flow or pressure sensor on bank 1 - the sensor that verifies air pump flow during cold-start enrichment compensation.

P2431.title: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2431.description: The ECU detects a general fault in the secondary air injection system air flow or pressure sensor circuit. The diagnostic cannot verify proper SAI operation.

P2432.title: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2432.description: The signal of the SAI air flow or pressure sensor is implausible during operation. The reading does not change as expected when the air pump is commanded.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2433.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P2433.description: Same as P2430 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2434.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 1
P2434.description: Same as P2430 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2435.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 2
P2435.description: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 2: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P2436.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 2
P2436.description: Same as P2430 on bank 2 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P2437.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2
P2437.description: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2438.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit High Bank 2
P2438.description: Same as P2433 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2439.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 2
P2439.description: Same as P2434 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P243A.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Ash Accumulation Bank 2
P243A.description: The diesel particulate filter on bank 2 reports backpressure attributable to ash (non-combustible residue from oil and fuel additives, not removable by regeneration). The filter has reached the end of its service life and needs cleaning or replacement.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243B.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2
P243B.description: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243C.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency Bank 2
P243C.description: The DPF on bank 2 needs regeneration more often than calibrated. Possible causes are an oil-burning engine, fuel-injector leak, short-trip operation, or a sensor offset.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243D.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Duration Bank 2
P243D.description: Regenerations on bank 2 take longer than calibrated to complete - typically a low EGT during the cycle (cold weather, short trips) or a partially aged catalyst before the DPF.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243E.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 2
P243E.description: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243F.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2
P243F.description: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2440.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2440.description: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 1 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.

causes.cause: Switching valve stuck open by carbon or corrosion
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2441.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2441.description: The switching valve on bank 1 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.

causes.cause: Switching valve stuck closed by carbon
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2442.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P2442.description: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 2 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2443.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
P2443.description: The switching valve on bank 2 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2444.title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck Off (Bank 1)
P2444.description: The secondary-air pump does not run when commanded during cold start. Often a seized pump (after exhaust back-feed corroded the impeller), a blown fuse, or a failed relay.

P2445.title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck On (Bank 1)
P2445.description: The secondary-air pump continues to run after the cold-start window, when the ECU has commanded it off. Usually a stuck-closed relay welding the pump permanently to battery voltage.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2446.title: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck Off (Bank 2)
P2446.description: Bank 2 secondary air pump does not deliver air when commanded. The catalyst light-off process is delayed and cold-start emissions rise.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2447.title: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck On (Bank 2)
P2447.description: Bank 2 secondary air pump runs continuously. Either a stuck-on relay or a shorted control output keeps the pump powered when it should be off.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2448.title: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 1
P2448.description: The secondary air injection system on bank 1 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

P2449.title: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 2
P2449.description: The secondary air injection system on bank 2 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

P244A.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too Low
P244A.description: The differential pressure across the DPF is below the calibrated minimum even at higher loads. Often a sign of a damaged or missing filter substrate, or a leak in the sensing line.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244B.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Sensor Offset
P244B.description: At engine off, the DPF differential pressure sensor does not return to zero within the allowed offset window. The static offset is too large to be ignored.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244C.title: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
P244C.description: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 1 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held. Driving in higher load is needed.

causes.cause: Engine load too low for regeneration

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244D.title: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
P244D.description: Same as P244C with the EGT too high - regeneration paused to protect filter substrate from melt damage.

causes.cause: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244E.title: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2
P244E.description: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 2 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held. Driving in higher load is needed.

causes.cause: Engine load too low for regeneration

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244F.title: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2

causes.cause: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2450.title: EVAP System Switching Valve Performance/Stuck
P2450.description: The EVAP switching valve does not respond to commands as expected. The valve is mechanically stuck or unable to switch between purge and vent paths, blocking proper leak diagnosis.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2451.title: EVAP System Switching Valve Stuck Closed
P2451.description: The EVAP switching valve - which directs vapor flow between purge and leak-detection paths - is stuck in the closed position. The diagnostic cycle cannot complete.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2452.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2452.description: A general electrical fault on the DPF differential-pressure sensor circuit. Without a valid pressure reading the ECU cannot estimate soot load and may inhibit regeneration.

causes.cause: Sensor sample hoses clogged with soot

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2453.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2453.description: The DPF differential-pressure sensor produces a value that is electrically valid but does not match expectations — for example a non-zero reading with engine off or no change between idle and load.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2454.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2454.description: Voltage on the DPF differential-pressure sensor signal line is below the lower threshold. Typically a short to ground or an open in the supply line.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2455.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2455.description: Voltage on the DPF pressure sensor line exceeds the upper threshold. Usually a short to supply or an open ground on the sensor.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2456.title: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P2456.description: The DPF differential-pressure sensor delivers an intermittent signal — usually a marginal connector or a chafed wiring section that breaks contact during temperature or vibration.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2457.title: EGR Cooler Performance
P2457.description: The EGR cooler does not lower exhaust gas temperature as expected — typically internal coolant fouling, a partial blockage, or a cracked cooler that mixes coolant with exhaust gas.

P2458.title: DPF Regeneration Duration
P2458.description: The DPF regeneration cycle takes longer than the calibrated maximum. The ECU sets this code when the soot load is not being burned off within the expected window — common after many short trips or with degraded post-injection.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2459.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency
P2459.description: Active DPF regenerations are being requested more often than the calibration window allows. Indicates that soot accumulates faster than the filter can burn it off — typically due to short-trip use, leaking injectors, or excessive engine oil consumption.

causes.cause: High engine oil consumption (turbo seals, valve stems)

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P245A.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Open Bank 1
P245A.description: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1 - routes EGR around the cooler during cold-start to keep cabin and engine warm-up fast - has an open control circuit.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P245B.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1
P245B.description: Same as P245A with the actuator electrically intact yet not delivering the commanded position. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Bypass valve sticking due to soot

P245C.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P245C.description: Same as P245A with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P245D.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit High Bank 1
P245D.description: Same as P245A with the control line shorted to supply. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P245E.title: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P245E.description: A general circuit fault on the secondary differential pressure sensor B across the DPF - measures backpressure for the regeneration strategy.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P245F.title: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range or Performance
P245F.description: Same as P245E with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2460.title: DPF Restriction — Forced Limited Power
P2460.description: The DPF restriction has reached a level that forces the ECU to limit engine power. The driver must allow a forced regeneration or have the filter serviced before normal power is restored.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2461.title: DPF Restriction — Forced Limited
P2461.description: The DPF restriction has reached the limit defined for forced limited operation. Vehicle behaviour depends on the manufacturer — usually a hard torque cap with a service warning.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2462.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction - Soot Accumulation
P2462.description: The DPF differential pressure sensor reports a backpressure rise consistent with excessive soot accumulation. The filter cannot regenerate fast enough, eventually causing limp mode.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2463.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction — Soot Accumulation
P2463.description: The estimated soot mass in the DPF has crossed the upper limit and the ECU could not complete a regeneration to bring it back down. Very common on cars used on short trips. Continued driving in this state risks a runaway regeneration that destroys the filter.

causes.cause: DPF heavily loaded after multiple aborted regenerations
Differential pressure sensor reading drifted high

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2464.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too High
P2464.description: The differential pressure across the DPF exceeds the calibrated upper threshold during operation. Indicates severe blockage of the filter element.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2465.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P2465.description: The DPF differential pressure sensor signal is implausible compared to engine load and exhaust flow. Either the sensor or the pressure tubes leading to it are at fault.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2466.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2466.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 2 sensor 3 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst). The ECU loses thermal protection feedback for the catalyst and DPF.

P2467.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2467.description: Same as P242B on bank 2 sensor 3.

P2468.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2468.description: Same as P242C on bank 2 sensor 3. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2469.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2469.description: Same as P242D on bank 2 sensor 3. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P246A.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 2 Sensor 3
P246A.description: Same as P242E on bank 2 sensor 3. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P246B.title: Vehicle Conditions Incorrect for Particulate Filter Regeneration
P246B.description: The driving pattern (short trips, low speed, frequent stops) does not provide the load and EGT needed for passive or active DPF regeneration. Filter loading rises until limit reached.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P246C.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 1
P246C.description: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P246D.title: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A and B Correlation
P246D.description: The two DPF differential pressure sensors A and B disagree by more than the diagnostic tolerance - one of them has drifted.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P246E.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 4
P246E.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 4 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst). The ECU loses thermal protection feedback for the catalyst and DPF.

P246F.title: Reductant System Cold Start Performance
P246F.description: At cold start the SCR system is unable to begin reductant dosing within the required time. Typical cause on diesel cars in winter — frozen AdBlue in the tank or lines, failed tank heater, or a slow-warming SCR catalyst.

causes.cause: AdBlue frozen — tank or line heater not working
SCR catalyst slow to reach light-off

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2470.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2470.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor 3 on bank 1 (often after the DPF) shows intermittent dropouts. Erratic readings disturb DPF regeneration logic.

P2471.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2471.description: EGT sensor 3 on bank 1 reports values that are not plausible for current operating conditions. Either drift or wiring resistance changes the signal away from the expected value.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2472.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2472.description: The voltage from EGT sensor 3 on bank 1 is below the calibrated minimum. The signal indicates either a short to ground or a sensor returning impossibly low temperature.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2473.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2473.description: The voltage of EGT sensor 3 on bank 1 is above the calibrated maximum. Often a sign of an open sensor circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2474.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 2 Sensor 4
P2474.description: Same as P242B on bank 2 sensor 4.

P2475.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 4
P2475.description: Same as P242C on bank 2 sensor 4. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

P2478.description: The EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 reports a value outside its plausible operating range over time - typically a degraded element giving an offset that the substitute logic flags as implausible.

P2479.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Out of Range Bank 1 Sensor 2
P2479.description: The EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 2 reports a value outside its plausible operating range over time - typically a degraded element giving an offset that the substitute logic flags as implausible.

P247A.description: The EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 3 reports a value outside its plausible operating range over time - typically a degraded element giving an offset that the substitute logic flags as implausible.

P247F.description: The EGT sensor at bank 2 sensor 4 reports a value outside its plausible operating range over time - typically a degraded element giving an offset that the substitute logic flags as implausible.

P2480.description: General electrical fault on EGT sensor 3 on bank 2. The ECU loses the temperature reference required for DPF regeneration management on bank 2.

P248A.title: Reductant Heater A Sense Circuit Low
P248A.description: Reductant Heater A Sense Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P248E.description: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 2 - routes EGR around the cooler during cold-start to keep cabin and engine warm-up fast - has an open control circuit.

P2490.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P2490.description: Same as P245C on bank 2. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P2492.description: A general circuit fault on the position feedback sensor of the EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P2493.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Position Sensor Range or Performance Bank 1
P2493.description: Same as P2492 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the actuator command. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P2494.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1
P2494.description: Same as P2492 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2495.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 1

P2497.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Position Sensor Circuit Bank 2

P249C.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Reductant Injection Control
P249C.description: After cold start the AdBlue injection runs open-loop until SCR temperature is reached. The transition into closed-loop is taking longer than calibrated.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P249D.title: Closed Loop Reductant Injection Control At Limit Flow Too Low
P249D.description: With reductant injection running closed-loop the controller drives the dosing valve to maximum opening but cannot reach the required AdBlue flow.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P249E.title: Closed Loop Reductant Injection Control At Limit Flow Too High
P249E.description: Same as P249D with the controller fully closing the dosing valve yet still measuring more flow than needed - the valve does not seat fully.

causes.cause: Dosing valve does not seat fully

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P249F.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Particulate Filter Regeneration Control
P249F.description: The DPF regeneration controller cannot transition into its closed-loop temperature control quickly enough - typically because EGT does not rise to setpoint within the calibrated window.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P24A0.title: Closed Loop Particulate Filter Regeneration Control At Limit Temperature Too Low
P24A0.description: With regeneration running closed-loop the controller is at maximum heat-input demand yet cannot raise EGT to setpoint - typical for a load-poor drive cycle.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P24A1.title: Closed Loop Particulate Filter Regeneration Control At Limit Temperature Too High
P24A1.description: Same as P24A0 with the controller fully reducing heat input yet EGT still rising - typical for a runaway exotherm in the DPF (oil contamination).
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P24A2.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 1
P24A2.description: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P24A3.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Bank 2
P24A3.description: The DPF on bank 2 has accumulated soot beyond the normal operating window. Active regeneration will be requested.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P24A4.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 1
P24A4.description: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P24A5.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Open Bank 1
P24A5.description: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1 is mechanically stuck in the open (bypassing) position - EGR always bypasses the cooler, gas reaches the intake hotter than designed.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P24A8.title: EGR Cooler Coolant Pump Performance Stuck Off
P24A8.description: The pump is electrically intact but does not deliver flow when commanded - typically a worn impeller or seized rotor.

causes.cause: Pump impeller worn or rotor seized
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P24AC.title: EGR Cooler Coolant Pump Feedback Circuit Low

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24B7.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Resistance

P24BB.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P24BB.description: Same as P24B8 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24BC.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P24BC.description: Same as P24B8 with intermittent or erratic signal. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24BD.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Switching Valve Control Circuit Open
P24BD.description: The switching valve in the LDP - directs pump output between EVAP test path and reference orifice - has an open control circuit.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24BE.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Switching Valve Control Circuit Low
P24BE.description: Same as P24BD with the control line shorted to ground. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24BF.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Switching Valve Control Circuit High
P24BF.description: Same as P24BD with the control line shorted to supply. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24C0.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Switching Valve Stuck On
P24C0.description: The LDP switching valve is stuck in the activated position. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24C1.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Switching Valve Performance Stuck Off
P24C1.description: Same as P24C0 with the valve stuck off. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24C2.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Measurement System Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 1
P24C2.description: The multiple EGT sensors on bank 1 disagree by more than the diagnostic tolerance under stable conditions - one of them has drifted relative to the others.

P24C3.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Measurement System Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 2
P24C3.description: The multiple EGT sensors on bank 2 disagree by more than the diagnostic tolerance under stable conditions - one of them has drifted relative to the others.

P24C4.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Position Sensor Exceeded Learning Limit Bank 1
P24C4.description: The bypass valve position sensor learning has reached its software-side limit on bank 1 - typically heavy soot deposits have shifted the mechanical zero beyond the design adaptation range.

causes.cause: Heavy carbon build-up on valve seat

P24C5.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Position Sensor Exceeded Learning Limit Bank 2
P24C5.description: The bypass valve position sensor learning has reached its software-side limit on bank 2 - typically heavy soot deposits have shifted the mechanical zero beyond the design adaptation range.

causes.cause: Heavy carbon build-up on valve seat

P24C6.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Temperature Circuit
P24C6.description: A general circuit fault on the temperature element of the PM sensor - used to verify that the sensor is hot enough for measurement after regeneration.

P24C7.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Temperature Circuit Range or Performance
P24C7.description: Same as P24C6 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P24C8.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Temperature Circuit Low
P24C8.description: Same as P24C6 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24C9.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Temperature Circuit High
P24C9.description: Same as P24C6 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P24CA.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Temperature Circuit Intermittent
P24CA.description: Same as P24C6 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P24CB.title: Reductant Tank Cap Switch Circuit
P24CB.description: A general circuit fault on the AdBlue tank cap switch - reports whether the cap is properly closed.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24CC.title: Reductant Tank Cap Switch Circuit Range or Performance
P24CC.description: Same as P24CB with input in plausible range yet not matching driver action.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24CD.title: Reductant Tank Cap Switch Circuit Low
P24CD.description: Same as P24CB with the signal shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24CE.title: Reductant Tank Cap Switch Circuit High
P24CE.description: Same as P24CB with the signal shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24CF.title: Reductant Tank Cap Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P24CF.description: Same as P24CB with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24D0.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P24D0.description: The PM sensor supply voltage is below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24D1.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Regeneration Incomplete
P24D1.description: A sensor regeneration cycle (heating to burn off accumulated soot) did not complete - sensor cannot return to measurement mode.

P24D2.title: Reductant Heater A Sense Circuit
P24D2.description: Reductant Heater A Sense Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24D3.title: Reductant Heater B Sense Circuit
P24D3.description: Reductant Heater B Sense Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24D4.title: EGR Cooler Coolant Pump Feedback Circuit
P24D4.description: A general circuit fault on the feedback line that the EGR cooler coolant pump reports speed on. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P24D5.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit
P24D5.description: A general circuit fault on the secondary EVAP system pressure sensor or switch B. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24D6.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit Range or Performance
P24D6.description: Same as P24D5 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24D7.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit Low
P24D7.description: Same as P24D5 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24D8.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit High
P24D8.description: Same as P24D5 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24D9.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit Intermittent
P24D9.description: Same as P24D5 with intermittent or erratic signal. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24DA.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1
P24DA.description: The PM sensor on bank 1 cannot acquire a valid exhaust sample - probe fouled, exhaust path obstructed at sensor, or sensor seal leaking.

P24DB.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Circuit Open
P24DB.description: The secondary reductant purge valve B - which clears AdBlue from injector and lines at shutdown to prevent crystallisation - has an open control circuit.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24DC.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Performance
P24DC.description: Same as P24DB with the actuator electrically intact yet not delivering the commanded purge flow. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24DD.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Circuit Low
P24DD.description: Same as P24DB with the control line shorted to ground. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24DE.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Circuit High
P24DE.description: Same as P24DB with the control line shorted to supply. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24DF.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Stuck Open
P24DF.description: Purge valve B is mechanically stuck open - AdBlue lines drain continuously, dosing pressure cannot build.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24E0.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Stuck Closed
P24E0.description: Same as P24DF with valve B stuck closed - AdBlue cannot be cleared at shutdown, risk of crystallisation in injector and lines.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24E1.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit
P24E1.description: A general circuit fault on the NH3 (ammonia) sensor - measures ammonia slip downstream of the SCR catalyst to detect AdBlue overdose.

P24E2.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P24E2.description: Same as P24E1 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P24E3.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit Low
P24E3.description: Same as P24E1 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24E4.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit High
P24E4.description: Same as P24E1 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P24E5.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P24E5.description: The ammonia (NH3) slip sensor downstream of the SCR catalyst delivers an intermittent or erratic signal. The ECM expects a smooth voltage proportional to ammonia concentration in the tailpipe — sudden jumps, dropouts or noise mean the wiring, connector or sensing element is failing. Used to close-loop the AdBlue/DEF dosing strategy.

causes.cause: Chafed or vibrating harness near the exhaust
Aged ceramic sensor element drifting under heat cycles

P24E6.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit/Open
P24E6.description: The heater inside the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor warms the sensing cell to operating temperature so it can read tailpipe ammonia. The ECM detects an open in the heater control circuit — no current flows when the heater should be active, so the sensor never reaches its working point and SCR closed-loop control is suspended.

causes.cause: Burnt-out heater winding inside the sensor
Failed heater driver stage in the dosing module

P24E7.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit Low
P24E7.description: The heater control circuit of the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor reads below the expected voltage range. Either the wiring is shorted to ground or the heater driver in the SCR/dosing module is stuck low. The sensor element never warms up, NH3 readings stay invalid and the SCR strategy falls back to open-loop dosing.

causes.cause: Heater control wire shorted to ground
Internal short across the heater element
Low-side driver pulled down in the control module

P24E8.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit High
P24E8.description: The heater control circuit of the NH3 slip sensor reads above the expected voltage range. Typically a short to battery voltage or a heater driver stuck high — duty-cycle control is lost, the heater either runs continuously or not at all, and the sensor element risks overheating before the ECM disables it.

causes.cause: Heater control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24E9.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit Performance
P24E9.description: The heater of the NH3 slip sensor is electrically intact, but the warm-up profile or steady-state temperature feedback does not match the ECM model. The sensor takes too long to reach operating temperature or drifts away from setpoint, so SCR closed-loop control is delayed or held off.

causes.cause: Poor thermal contact between heater and sensing cell

P24EA.title: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit
P24EA.description: The supply rail that powers the NH3 slip sensor electronics (typically 5 V or 12 V from the dosing/SCR module) is out of tolerance. Without a stable supply the sensor cannot deliver a valid ammonia reading, and the ECM disables the closed-loop SCR strategy.

causes.cause: Failing supply rail inside the dosing module

P24EB.title: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P24EB.description: The NH3 slip sensor supply voltage drops below the lower limit. Usually a partial short to ground in the supply line, an undersized ground path with high resistance, or an internal supply collapse in the SCR/dosing module. Sensor output is held invalid until the supply recovers.

causes.cause: High-resistance ground at the SCR module
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24EC.title: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit High
P24EC.description: The NH3 slip sensor supply voltage rises above the upper limit. Either the supply is shorted to battery voltage or an internal regulator in the dosing module has failed open. The sensor electronics may be damaged if the condition persists, so the ECM disables the input.

causes.cause: Supply line shorted to battery voltage
Failed voltage regulator in the dosing module
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24ED.title: NH3 Sensor Calibration Memory
P24ED.description: The NH3 slip sensor stores its individual calibration coefficients in non-volatile memory (EEPROM/flash). The ECM cannot read valid calibration values — either checksum fails, the memory is empty after replacement, or communication with the sensor electronics is broken. Without the trim values the raw ammonia reading is unreliable.

causes.cause: New sensor installed but not coded/learned to the ECM
Corrupted calibration memory after voltage drop
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P24EE.title: NH3 Sensor Processor Performance
P24EE.description: The microcontroller inside the smart NH3 slip sensor reports an internal performance fault — failed self-test, watchdog reset, or out-of-range plausibility checks. The sensor cannot guarantee its output value, the ECM marks the channel invalid and disables SCR closed-loop control on this branch.

causes.cause: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P24EF.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit/Open
P24EF.description: The wake-up line that brings a sleeping ECU back from low-power mode is open. Many networks use a dedicated hardware wake-up wire (door-latch trigger, terminal 15, CAN wake-up) so modules can stay asleep with the ignition off. Without it, the module either fails to wake up at start-up or stays awake and drains the battery.

causes.cause: Broken wake-up wire or unplugged connector
Failed wake-up input stage in the module
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P24F0.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit Low
P24F0.description: The wake-up input on the control module reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a permanently asserted wake signal. The module either keeps waking up unnecessarily and drains the battery, or it cannot distinguish a real wake event from the stuck low level.

causes.cause: Door, hood or terminal switch stuck closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24F1.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit High
P24F1.description: The wake-up input reads above the expected range — typically a short to battery voltage. The module sees a permanent wake-up request, never enters sleep mode and drains the battery while parked.

causes.cause: Wake-up wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P24F2.title: EGR Temperature/Charge Air Cooler Temperature Correlation
P24F2.description: After a long key-off soak both the EGR temperature sensor and the charge-air cooler outlet temperature sensor must read approximately the same ambient temperature. The ECM compares them and detects an implausible delta. One of the sensors drifts, is wired wrong, or is exposed to a heat source the model does not know about.

causes.cause: Residual heat in the charge-air cooler after a hot soak

P24F3.title: Reductant Tank Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation
P24F3.description: After a long key-off soak the AdBlue/DEF tank temperature and the fuel tank temperature should read close to each other (both at ambient). The ECM detects an implausible spread, which usually means one of the two sensors drifts, is wired wrong, or has a heat source nearby that the plausibility model does not account for.

causes.cause: One temperature sensor drifting outside tolerance
Recently active reductant tank heater warming the tank above ambient

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24F4.title: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P24F4.description: The pre-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level — for example after a fuel cut or transition into low-load. Aged ceramic cells, soot deposits or condensation inside the sensor protective tube slow the diffusion of NOx to the measuring element.

causes.cause: Aged sensor element with reduced response speed

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24F5.title: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
P24F5.description: The post-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 2) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level. Same failure mechanism as the upstream sensor — aged element, soot or condensate — but post-catalyst the consequence is a degraded SCR conversion-efficiency monitor.

causes.cause: Aged sensor element with reduced response speed

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24F6.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Open
P24F6.description: On systems that inject HC dosing fuel or AIR-assisted reductant into the aftertreatment, a purge valve clears the line after each dosing event. The ECM detects the valve stuck open — pressure or flow does not build up against a closed valve, so the dosing line cannot be charged. Common on diesel HC-doser hardware (DPF regen support).

causes.cause: Mechanically stuck open valve from soot or coking
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P24F7.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Closed
P24F7.description: The aftertreatment HC dosing or reductant purge valve is stuck closed. The ECM commands purge but the line is not cleared, leaving residual fluid that can foul nozzles or freeze in cold weather. Subsequent dosing events also fail because backpressure does not match the model.

causes.cause: Stuck closed by deposits or seized armature
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P24F8.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit
P24F8.description: General electrical fault in the control circuit of the aftertreatment fuel/air purge valve. The ECM cannot drive the valve coil according to plausibility checks — open, short or unexpected feedback voltage. Until cleared, dosing line purge is suspended.

causes.cause: Failed driver stage in the dosing module

P24F9.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Range/Performance
P24F9.description: The valve coil is electrically intact, but the response (current rise time, return-current decay, position feedback) does not match the ECM model. Typical for solenoids losing magnetic strength after long thermal cycling, or armatures with increased friction from coking.

causes.cause: Aged solenoid with weakened magnetic force
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P24FA.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Low
P24FA.description: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a failed low-side driver. The valve is energised continuously when it should be off, or the diagnostic feedback voltage is pulled below threshold.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24FB.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit High
P24FB.description: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage or an open ground/return path. The driver cannot pull the line low to actuate the valve.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24FC.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P24FC.description: The PM (soot) sensor heater is driven by a current-limited stage so it can burn off accumulated soot before each measurement. The driver reports current or junction temperature above the safe limit and disables itself. Often a partial short across the heater or sensor element after coolant intrusion.

causes.cause: Partial short across the heater element
Driver overheating due to poor cooling on the module

P24FD.title: Particulate Filter A Incorrect
P24FD.description: The ECM identifies the installed particulate filter A as the wrong part — backpressure signature, regeneration efficiency or coded part-number do not match the application. Common after a non-OEM aftermarket DPF or a wrong-application replacement.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P24FE.title: SCR Catalyst Incorrect
