P25C7.description: The booster temperature signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to a 5 V reference in the harness.

causes.cause: Sensor signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C8.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P25C8.description: The booster temperature signal jumps or drops out for short moments. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire that opens during vibration or thermal expansion.

causes.cause: Sensor connector not fully seated or pin tension lost
Harness chafed against booster housing or pedal bracket
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C9.title: Brake System Control Module B Requested MIL Illumination
P25C9.description: A second brake system control module (typically the redundant secondary unit on by-wire or AV-grade brake systems) has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.

causes.cause: Active DTC stored in the secondary brake module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request

P25CA.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P25CA.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the intake camshaft phaser on bank 1 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.cause: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CB.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P25CB.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CC.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 1
P25CC.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CD.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P25CD.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the intake camshaft phaser on bank 2 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.cause: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CE.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P25CE.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CF.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 2
P25CF.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D0.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P25D0.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 1 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.cause: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D1.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P25D1.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D2.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 1
P25D2.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D3.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P25D3.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 2 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.cause: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D4.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P25D4.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D5.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 2
P25D5.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D6.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Stop Performance
P25D6.description: During self-calibration of the exhaust heat exchanger bypass valve A, the position sensor never reached the expected mechanical stop. The controller cannot zero the position reference, so commanded openings will be inaccurate.

causes.cause: Soot or carbon deposits prevent valve from reaching the stop
Worn linkage between actuator and valve flap
Position sensor not aligned with valve shaft

P25D7.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit
P25D7.description: A third fuel level sensor (C) used on multi-tank trucks, dual-saddle SUVs, or auxiliary fuel systems returns no usable signal. Without it, calculated fuel level and EVAP monitor enabling will be off.

causes.cause: Open sender resistor or broken float

P25D8.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Performance
P25D8.description: The third fuel level sensor reading does not change as expected with consumption or refuelling. Float may be sticking, or the resistor track has localised wear.

causes.cause: Float arm stuck on baffle or fuel pump module
Worn spot on the resistor track at common fill level

P25D9.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit Low
P25D9.description: The third fuel level sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sender or a short to ground in the harness.

causes.cause: Internal short in the sender resistor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25DA.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit High
P25DA.description: The third fuel level sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sender or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25DB.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit Intermittent
P25DB.description: The third fuel level sensor signal jumps or drops out for short moments. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire that opens during driving vibration.

causes.cause: Tank module connector not fully seated
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P25DC.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Stuck
P25DC.description: The third fuel level sensor reads a constant value across known consumption or refuelling events. Float arm or resistor wiper is mechanically stuck.

causes.cause: Float arm jammed against tank wall, baffle or pump module
Resistor wiper seized by varnish from old fuel

P25DD.title: A Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 1
P25DD.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.cause: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25DE.title: A Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 1
P25DE.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.cause: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25DF.title: A Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 1
P25DF.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.cause: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E0.title: A Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 2
P25E0.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.cause: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E1.title: A Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 2
P25E1.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.cause: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E2.title: A Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 2
P25E2.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.cause: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E3.title: B Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 1
P25E3.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.cause: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E4.title: B Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 1
P25E4.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.cause: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E5.title: B Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 1
P25E5.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.cause: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E6.title: B Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 2
P25E6.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.cause: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E7.title: B Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 2
P25E7.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.cause: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E8.title: B Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 2
P25E8.description: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.cause: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E9.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Stuck Open
P25E9.description: The clutch that engages the mechanical supercharger to the engine drive will not close. The supercharger stays disengaged so boost from this stage is unavailable, which limits torque and may also affect cooling pump drives shared with the same belt.

causes.cause: Worn friction surfaces leave the air gap too large to attract

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EA.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Stuck Closed
P25EA.description: The clutch that engages the mechanical supercharger to the engine drive will not open. The supercharger remains coupled at all loads, increasing parasitic loss and fuel consumption when boost is not needed.

causes.cause: Armature plate seized to the pulley face
Driver stuck on keeps clutch energised
Failed pulley bearing welds clutch surfaces

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EB.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Circuit Range/Performance
P25EB.description: The supercharger clutch control current does not match the commanded value within tolerance. Either coil resistance has drifted or the driver feedback is implausible.

causes.cause: Coil resistance increased due to thermal damage
High-resistance contact in the clutch connector
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EC.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Circuit Low
P25EC.description: Voltage on the supercharger clutch control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted clutch coil.

causes.cause: Internal short in the clutch coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25ED.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Circuit High
P25ED.description: Voltage on the supercharger clutch control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open coil that lets the driver float high.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EE.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B / Open
P25EE.description: The controller cannot drive the secondary electric vacuum pump (B). Brake servo or HVAC actuators that depend on engine vacuum may not get enough vacuum during low-load operation or with engine off in stop-start mode.

causes.cause: Open pump motor winding or worn brushes
Broken control wire between ECU and pump

P25EF.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B Range/Performance
P25EF.description: The secondary vacuum pump does not produce the expected vacuum within the commanded run time. Leak in the pump line or worn pump diaphragm reduces output.

causes.cause: Worn diaphragm or vanes inside the pump
Cracked vacuum hose or loose connection
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P25F0.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B Low
P25F0.description: Voltage on the secondary vacuum pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.cause: Internal short in pump motor winding

P25F1.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B High
P25F1.description: Voltage on the secondary vacuum pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor that lets the driver float high.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open motor winding or worn brushes

P25F2.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit
P25F2.description: A third boost pressure sensor (C) used on twin-stage or sequential boost systems returns no usable signal. Without it, boost control of the third stage runs open-loop or is disabled.

causes.cause: Open sensor element or broken signal wire

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F3.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P25F3.description: The third boost pressure sensor reading is implausible compared with manifold pressure or commanded boost. Either drift, leak in the sensing line, or contamination on the sensor diaphragm.

causes.cause: Sensing hose blocked by oil residue
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F4.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit Low
P25F4.description: The third boost pressure sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sensor element or a short to ground.

causes.cause: Internal short in the sensor element
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F5.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit High
P25F5.description: The third boost pressure sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F6.title: AIR System B
P25F6.description: A general fault in the second secondary air injection (AIR) circuit. Detected by the O2 sensors which expect a lean swing during cold-start AIR pump operation but do not see one.

causes.cause: Failed AIR pump motor or impeller
Check valve seized by exhaust soot
Corroded or cracked air injection pipe

P25F7.title: AIR System B Incorrect Flow Detected
P25F7.description: The second AIR system delivers measurably more or less air than expected. Often a partially blocked pipe, a worn pump, or a leak between pump and check valve.

causes.cause: Air pipe partially blocked by carbon
Leak between pump and check valve

P25F8.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit
P25F8.description: A third bypass (recirculation or wastegate) valve used in three-stage charging systems is not responding to control commands. Boost balancing across stages can no longer be achieved.

causes.cause: Open or shorted wiring to the valve

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25F9.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit Low
P25F9.description: Voltage on the third bypass valve control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Internal short in the solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25FA.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit High
P25FA.description: Voltage on the third bypass valve control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25FB.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P25FB.description: The third bypass valve current does not match the commanded value within tolerance. Drifted coil resistance or high-resistance contact in the connector.

causes.cause: Coil resistance changed by thermal stress
High-resistance contact in the valve connector
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25FC.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C - Mechanical
P25FC.description: The third bypass valve is mechanically jammed. Solenoid is energised correctly but the valve flap or disc does not move as expected.

causes.cause: Carbon buildup blocks the valve flap

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25FD.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Temperature Too High
P25FD.description: The third bypass valve has reached over-temperature. Either coil duty cycle is too high for too long, or cooling air flow around the valve is restricted.

causes.cause: Sustained high duty cycle from charge balancing strategy
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25FE.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch
P25FE.description: A general performance fault in the supercharger disconnect clutch. Engagement or release is slow, sticky, or out of tolerance without a clear electrical-side cause.

causes.cause: Worn friction surfaces or air gap drift
Oil or debris on the clutch face

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25FF.title: Electrical System Voltage Stabilizer Control Module Performance
P25FF.description: The voltage stabiliser module (DC/DC converter for stop-start engine cranking events) does not maintain the regulated 12 V output during high transient loads. Sensitive electronics may reset during cranking.

causes.cause: Battery condition causes input voltage to drop too far
Internal fault in the converter switching stage

P2600.title: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit / Open
P2600.description: The controller cannot drive the electric coolant pump A control line. Without circulation, engine and aftertreatment can overheat or warm up incorrectly.

causes.cause: Broken control wire to the pump

P2601.title: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P2601.description: The electric coolant pump A is commanded on but does not run. Coolant temperature climbs faster than expected with no flow detected.

causes.cause: Pump motor seized by debris or sediment
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2602.title: Coolant Pump Control Circuit Open
P2602.description: The ECU detects an open circuit on the electric coolant pump control line. Without pump control the engine cannot actively manage warm-up and cool-down phases.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2603.title: Coolant Pump Control Circuit Low
P2603.description: The electric coolant pump drive line reads below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or a failed driver stage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2604.title: Coolant Pump Control Circuit High
P2604.description: The electric coolant pump drive line reads above the upper threshold — usually a short to positive or a stuck-on driver stage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2605.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit / Open
P2605.description: The controller cannot drive the secondary intake air heater (heater grid B) used on diesel engines for cold-start support. The grid stays cold so cold-start emissions and white smoke increase.

causes.cause: Failed heater relay or open coil

P2606.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit Range/Performance
P2606.description: The secondary intake air heater current does not match expected resistance. Either the grid is partially open or the relay contacts have high resistance.

causes.cause: Partial element failure raises grid resistance
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2607.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit Low
P2607.description: Voltage on the secondary intake air heater control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted relay coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2608.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit High
P2608.description: Voltage on the secondary intake air heater control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open relay coil.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2609.title: Intake Air Heater System Performance
P2609.description: The intake air heater system did not raise intake temperature by the expected amount during cold-start support. Suggests low current draw, poor connection to the grid, or a failed temperature feedback path.

causes.cause: High-resistance battery feed to the heater
Intake air temperature sensor reads with offset

P260A.title: PTO Control Circuit / Open
P260A.description: The controller cannot drive the power take-off (PTO) engagement line on commercial vehicles. The PTO will not engage even when commanded by the body controller or operator switch.

causes.cause: Open coil in the PTO engagement solenoid
Broken wire to the PTO solenoid

P260B.title: PTO Control Circuit Low
P260B.description: Voltage on the PTO engagement control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Internal short in the solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P260C.title: PTO Control Circuit High
P260C.description: Voltage on the PTO engagement control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P260D.title: PTO Engaged Lamp Control Circuit
P260D.description: The dashboard PTO engaged lamp control circuit is faulty. Driver may not see whether the PTO is currently driving an external accessory.

causes.cause: Open or shorted wire between cluster and ECU

P260E.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Lamp Control Circuit
P260E.description: The DPF regeneration warning lamp circuit is faulty. The driver may not be alerted to a required highway run that supports passive regeneration.

causes.cause: Open or shorted wire to the cluster

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P260F.title: EVAP System Monitoring Processor Performance
P260F.description: The dedicated EVAP monitoring processor (often a small auxiliary CPU inside the engine controller or a separate module) does not pass its self-test or runs out of step with the main monitor logic.

causes.cause: Internal fault in the monitoring processor
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2610.title: ECM/PCM Internal Engine Off Timer Performance
P2610.description: The engine controller's internal soak-time/engine-off timer fails its plausibility check — for example readings claim instant cool-down or never-cooled. Cold-start enrichment, EVAP and catalyst monitors depend on this timer; a fault freezes those readiness monitors.

P2611.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit / Open
P2611.description: The A/C refrigerant distribution valve A (used to switch refrigerant flow between front and rear evaporators or between cabin and battery cooling on EVs) cannot be driven by the controller.

causes.cause: Open coil in the valve solenoid

P2612.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit Low
P2612.description: Voltage on the A/C distribution valve A control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Internal short in the valve solenoid
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2613.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit High
P2613.description: Voltage on the A/C distribution valve A control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2614.title: Camshaft Position Output Circuit/Open
P2614.description: The camshaft position output signal sent from the ECU to other modules is interrupted. Other systems that rely on the cam reference (e.g. transmission, hybrid module) do not receive a valid signal.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P2615.title: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit Low Bank 1
P2615.description: The buffered camshaft A position output that the engine controller sends to other modules (transmission, body, ignition module) is below the expected level on bank 1. Other modules cannot use the cam phase reference for synchronisation.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P2616.title: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit High Bank 1
P2616.description: The buffered camshaft A position output is above the expected level on bank 1. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P2617.title: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit / Open
P2617.description: The buffered crankshaft position output that the engine controller sends to ignition modules and the transmission cannot drive its line. Open detected on the output side.

causes.cause: Open wire between ECU and downstream module

P2618.title: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit Low
P2618.description: The buffered crankshaft position output is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground on the output line or a failed buffer.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2619.title: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit High
P2619.description: The buffered crankshaft position output is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P261A.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit / Open
P261A.description: The controller cannot drive the second electric coolant pump (B). Often used for aftertreatment, turbo cool-down, or hybrid battery loops — fault stops circulation in that loop.

causes.cause: Broken control wire to the pump

P261B.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P261B.description: The second electric coolant pump is commanded on but does not run. Cooling demand of the connected loop is not satisfied.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P261C.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P261C.description: Voltage on the second coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P261D.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit High
P261D.description: Voltage on the second coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P261E.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Stuck On
P261E.description: The second coolant pump runs even when no command is active. Driver is stuck on or the wire is shorted to a permanent supply.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a permanent B+ supply
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P261F.title: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Stuck On
P261F.description: The first coolant pump runs even when no command is active. Driver is stuck on or the wire is shorted to a permanent supply.

causes.cause: Control wire shorted to a permanent B+ supply
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2620.title: Throttle Position Output Circuit
P2620.description: A general electrical fault on the ECU output that broadcasts the throttle position signal to other modules — for example to the transmission control or hybrid drive controller.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2621.title: Throttle Position Output Circuit Low
P2621.description: The buffered throttle position output that the engine controller sends to the transmission and body modules is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground or a failed output stage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2622.title: Throttle Position Output Circuit High
P2622.description: The buffered throttle position output is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2623.title: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit / Open
P2623.description: The Injector Control Pressure (ICP) regulator on hydraulically actuated injectors (HEUI diesel) or the high-pressure regulator on common-rail systems cannot be driven. Injection pressure cannot be controlled, engine may not start.

causes.cause: Open coil in the pressure regulator

P2624.title: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit Low
P2624.description: Voltage on the ICP regulator control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted regulator coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2625.title: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit High
P2625.description: Voltage on the ICP regulator control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open regulator coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2626.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit/Open Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2626.description: The ECU detects an open in the pumping current trim circuit of the wide-band oxygen sensor on bank 1 sensor 1. Without trim correction, the lambda value reported by the sensor is not accurate.

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2627.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2627.description: On a wide-band (broadband) O2 sensor, the trim resistor circuit that calibrates the pumping current is reading low on bank 1 sensor 1. Air-fuel feedback gain is wrong, causing rich or lean offsets.

causes.cause: Short in the calibration trim resistor
Water intrusion in the sensor connector
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2628.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2628.description: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 1 sensor 1 reads high. Air-fuel feedback gain is wrong, causing offsets that the controller cannot compensate.

causes.cause: Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2629.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit / Open Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2629.description: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 is open. Air-fuel feedback for bank 2 cannot be calibrated, fuel control runs degraded.

P262A.title: Fuel Injector - Pilot Injection Not Learned
P262A.description: The pilot (pre) injection learning routine on a common-rail diesel did not complete successfully. Without learned pilot quantity, combustion noise increases and NOx may rise.

causes.cause: Injector flow drift outside learning window
Unstable rail pressure during learning cycle

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P262B.title: Control Module Power Off Timer Performance
P262B.description: The internal power-down timer of the engine controller does not run as expected. The module either stays awake too long after key-off (battery drain) or shuts down too early (no aftertreatment cool-down or learn-write).

P262C.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit / Open
P262C.description: The 5 V reference G output that the engine controller supplies to a group of sensors is open. All sensors fed from this rail will report invalid readings.

causes.cause: Open wire on the reference rail
Open inside the ECU reference output

P262D.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit Low
P262D.description: The 5 V reference G voltage is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground or excessive load from a downstream sensor pulling the rail down.

causes.cause: Sensor on the rail shorted internally to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P262E.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit High
P262E.description: The 5 V reference G voltage is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an internal regulator failure.

causes.cause: Reference wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P262F.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit Range/Performance
P262F.description: The 5 V reference G voltage is within range but unstable or offset against expected. Loose ground or marginal regulator load.

causes.cause: High-resistance ground for the reference rail
One sensor draws excessive current and shifts the rail
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2630.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2630.description: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 reads low. Air-fuel feedback gain on bank 2 is wrong, causing rich or lean offsets.

causes.cause: Short in the calibration trim resistor
Water intrusion in the sensor connector
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2631.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2631.description: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 reads high. Air-fuel feedback gain on bank 2 is wrong, the controller cannot compensate the offset.

causes.cause: Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2632.title: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit / Open
P2632.description: The controller cannot drive the secondary fuel pump (B). Common on dual-tank trucks, GDI lift-pump systems, or alt-fuel installations — fault stops fuel delivery from this stage.
symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2633.title: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit Low
P2633.description: Voltage on the second fuel pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2634.title: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit High
P2634.description: Voltage on the second fuel pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2635.title: Fuel Pump A Low Flow / Performance
P2635.description: The ECU detects insufficient fuel flow from fuel pump A. Either the pump is worn out, the supply line is restricted, or the pressure regulator does not allow proper flow.
symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2636.title: Fuel Pump B Low Flow/Performance
P2636.description: The second fuel pump runs but does not deliver expected volume or pressure. Worn pump, restricted filter, or leaking pressure regulator.

causes.cause: Restricted in-tank or in-line fuel filter
Pressure regulator leaks back to tank

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2637.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A
P2637.description: The torque feedback signal A from the transmission or other torque user is missing or invalid. The engine controller cannot reduce torque on shift requests, which can cause harsh shifts.

causes.cause: Required CAN message not received in time
Source module reports an internal fault

P2638.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A Range/Performance
P2638.description: The torque feedback signal A is present but its value is implausible against measured engine load and speed. Sender calibration or sensor offset is suspected.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2639.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A Low
P2639.description: The torque feedback signal A reads below its valid range. Either the source reports a value below physical possibility or the bus signal is stuck low.

causes.cause: Source module sends invalid low value
Signal stuck low on the bus

P263A.title: MIL Control Circuit Low
P263A.description: Voltage on the malfunction indicator lamp control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted bulb driver.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P263B.title: MIL Control Circuit High
P263B.description: Voltage on the malfunction indicator lamp control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open lamp.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P263C.title: Glow Plug Control Driver Performance
P263C.description: The glow plug control driver does not respond to commands within tolerance. Cold-start glow function is degraded so cold starting can be delayed and white smoke increases.

causes.cause: Aged driver shows degraded switching behaviour

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P263D.title: Reductant Heater Driver Performance
P263D.description: The reductant (AdBlue) tank or line heater driver does not switch as expected. AdBlue may freeze in cold weather, blocking SCR dosing.

causes.cause: Aged driver shows degraded switching behaviour
Heater element resistance drifted out of range

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P263E.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Over Temperature
P263E.description: The first glow plug control module reports over-temperature. Sustained current draw or insufficient cooling has driven the module above its rated temperature.

causes.cause: One glow plug shorted to ground forces module overcurrent
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P263F.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Over Temperature
P263F.description: The second glow plug control module reports over-temperature. Sustained current draw or insufficient cooling has driven the module above its rated temperature.

causes.cause: One glow plug shorted to ground forces module overcurrent
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P2640.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A High
P2640.description: The torque feedback signal A reads above its valid range. Source module sends an implausibly high value or the bus signal is stuck high.

causes.cause: Source module sends invalid high value
Signal stuck high on the bus

P2641.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B
P2641.description: The torque feedback signal B from a second torque user is missing or invalid. The engine controller cannot coordinate torque reduction with this user.

causes.cause: Required CAN message not received in time
Source module reports an internal fault

P2642.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B Range/Performance
P2642.description: The torque feedback signal B is present but its value is implausible against measured engine load and speed. Sender calibration or sensor offset is suspected.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2643.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B Low
P2643.description: The torque feedback signal B reads below its valid range. Source sends a value below physical possibility or the bus signal is stuck low.

causes.cause: Source module sends invalid low value
Signal stuck low on the bus

P2644.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B High
P2644.description: The torque feedback signal B reads above its valid range. Source sends an implausibly high value or the bus signal is stuck high.

causes.cause: Source module sends invalid high value
Signal stuck high on the bus

P2645.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P2645.description: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator A on bank 1 (used in cylinder deactivation systems such as VTEC, AFM, MDS). The valve lift mode cannot be switched.

causes.cause: Open coil in oil control valve

P2646.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P2646.description: The rocker arm actuator A on bank 1 is commanded to engage (high lift or all-cylinder mode) but does not switch. Engine stays in low-lift or deactivated mode under load, causing reduced power.

causes.cause: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2647.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 1
P2647.description: On variable valve lift systems (e.g. Honda VTEC) the ECU detects that the bank 1 rocker arm actuator is stuck in the engaged (high lift) position. Idle quality and fuel economy are affected.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2648.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P2648.description: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 1 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2649.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 1
P2649.description: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 1 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P264A.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P264A.description: The position sensor that confirms the A rocker arm switching state on bank 1 returns no usable signal. Closed-loop control of valve lift cannot verify the state.

P264B.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
P264B.description: The position sensor reading does not transition cleanly between the two valve lift modes on bank 1. Sensor drift or mechanical wear leaves the signal between expected values.

causes.cause: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn lock pin reduces travel between modes
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P264C.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1
P264C.description: The position sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sensor or short to ground in the harness.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P264D.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P264D.description: The position sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P264E.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 1
P264E.description: The position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire in the harness.

causes.cause: Harness chafed against valve cover or cam carrier
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P264F.title: Engine Serial Number Not Programmed or Incompatible
P264F.description: The engine controller cannot read a valid engine serial number from its non-volatile memory, or the stored value does not match the expected pattern. Calibration sets keyed to the serial number cannot be applied.

causes.cause: Replacement ECU not programmed at install

P2650.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P2650.description: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator B on bank 1. The second valve lift mode cannot be commanded.

causes.cause: Open coil in oil control valve

P2651.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P2651.description: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 1 is commanded to engage but does not switch. Engine stays in the wrong lift or cylinder mode under load.

causes.cause: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2652.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 1
P2652.description: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 1 stays in the activated state when commanded off. Engine cannot return to the alternate lift or cylinder mode.

causes.cause: Mechanical lock pin stuck in activated position
Oil control valve spool stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2653.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P2653.description: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 1 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2654.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 1
P2654.description: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 1 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2655.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P2655.description: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator A on bank 2. The valve lift mode cannot be switched on this bank.

causes.cause: Open coil in oil control valve

P2656.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 2
P2656.description: The rocker arm actuator A on bank 2 is commanded to engage but does not switch. Engine stays in the wrong lift mode under load on this bank.

causes.cause: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2657.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 2
P2657.description: The rocker arm actuator A on bank 2 stays in the activated state when commanded off.

causes.cause: Mechanical lock pin stuck in activated position
Oil control valve spool stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2658.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P2658.description: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 2 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2659.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 2
P2659.description: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 2 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P265A.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P265A.description: The position sensor that confirms the B rocker arm switching state on bank 1 returns no usable signal.

P265B.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
P265B.description: The position sensor reading does not transition cleanly between the two valve lift modes for actuator B on bank 1.

causes.cause: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn lock pin reduces travel between modes
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P265C.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1
P265C.description: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 1 is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P265D.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P265D.description: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 1 is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P265E.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 1
P265E.description: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 1 jumps or drops out intermittently. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P265F.title: Variable A/C Compressor Control Circuit Range/Performance
P265F.description: The variable-displacement A/C compressor control valve does not respond to commands within tolerance. Refrigerant flow regulation is degraded so cabin temperature varies or efficiency drops.

causes.cause: Control valve spool sticky from oil residue
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2660.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P2660.description: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator B on bank 2.

causes.cause: Open coil in oil control valve

P2661.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 2
P2661.description: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 2 is commanded to engage but does not switch.

causes.cause: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2662.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 2
P2662.description: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 2 stays in the activated state when commanded off.

causes.cause: Mechanical lock pin stuck in activated position
Oil control valve spool stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2663.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P2663.description: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 2 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2664.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 2
P2664.description: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 2 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2665.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit / Open
P2665.description: The controller cannot drive the secondary fuel shutoff valve. Engine cannot be commanded off through this path during a safety event.

P2666.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit Low
P2666.description: Voltage on the secondary fuel shutoff valve control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2667.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit High
P2667.description: Voltage on the secondary fuel shutoff valve control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2668.title: Fuel Mode Indicator Lamp Control Circuit
P2668.description: The fuel mode indicator lamp circuit (showing whether a bi-fuel vehicle currently runs on gasoline or alternative fuel) is faulty. Driver may not know the active fuel.

causes.cause: Open or shorted wire to the cluster

P2669.title: Actuator Supply Voltage B Circuit / Open
P2669.description: The second power feed used to supply actuators (relays, solenoids, motor drivers) is open. All loads on this rail are powerless and report follow-on faults.

causes.cause: Blown fuse on the supply rail
Broken supply wire from main relay

P266A.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Bank 2
P266A.description: The position sensor that confirms the A rocker arm switching state on bank 2 returns no usable signal.

P266B.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
P266B.description: The position sensor reading does not transition cleanly between the two valve lift modes for actuator A on bank 2.

causes.cause: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn lock pin reduces travel between modes
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P266C.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2
P266C.description: The position sensor signal for actuator A on bank 2 is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P266D.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 2
P266D.description: The position sensor signal for actuator A on bank 2 is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P266E.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 2
P266E.description: The position sensor signal for actuator A on bank 2 jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P266F.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P266F.description: The driver stage for the A/C refrigerant distribution valve A is in current limit or over-temperature. Sustained overload from a partially shorted load or excessive switching frequency.

P2670.title: Actuator Supply Voltage B Circuit Low
P2670.description: The supply voltage to actuator group B (e.g. solenoids, valves driven by ECU) is below the calibrated threshold. The affected actuators may be slow or unable to switch.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2671.title: Actuator Supply Voltage B Circuit High
P2671.description: The second actuator supply rail is above the expected voltage. Likely a charging system overvoltage or a short to a higher-voltage source.

causes.cause: Wiring shorted to a higher-voltage circuit
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2672.title: Injection Pump Timing Offset
P2672.description: The high-pressure injection pump timing is offset from the expected reference. On distributor pumps with a timing solenoid, the actuator does not match the commanded position.

causes.cause: Worn timing actuator piston or seal
Stretched pump drive chain or belt

P2673.title: Injection Pump Timing Calibration Not Learned
P2673.description: The injection pump timing learning routine did not complete successfully. Without learned values, injection timing runs from default tables and combustion is suboptimal.

causes.cause: Learning routine aborted by other DTC or unstable conditions
Timing actuator drift outside learning window

P2674.title: Injection Pump Fuel Calibration Not Learned
P2674.description: The injection pump fuel quantity calibration did not complete successfully. Without learned fuel calibration, AFR runs from default tables and emissions or smoke can rise.

causes.cause: Learning routine aborted by other DTC or unstable conditions
Fuel quantity solenoid drift outside learning window

P2675.title: Air Cleaner Inlet Control Circuit / Open
P2675.description: The controller cannot drive the air cleaner inlet control valve (warm-air or snorkel switching for cold-start emissions). Stuck in default position so cold-start fueling is sub-optimal.

causes.cause: Open coil in inlet valve solenoid

P2676.title: Air Cleaner Inlet Control Circuit Low
P2676.description: Voltage on the air cleaner inlet valve control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2677.title: Air Cleaner Inlet Control Circuit High
P2677.description: Voltage on the air cleaner inlet valve control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2678.title: Coolant Degassing Valve Control Circuit / Open
P2678.description: The controller cannot drive the coolant degassing valve. Air pockets in the cooling system can form and cause local overheating.

P2679.title: Coolant Degassing Valve Control Circuit Low
P2679.description: Voltage on the coolant degassing valve control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P267A.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Bank 2
P267A.description: The position sensor that confirms the B rocker arm switching state on bank 2 returns no usable signal.

P267B.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
P267B.description: The position sensor reading does not transition cleanly between the two valve lift modes for actuator B on bank 2.

causes.cause: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn lock pin reduces travel between modes
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P267C.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2
P267C.description: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 2 is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P267D.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 2
P267D.description: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 2 is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P267E.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 2
P267E.description: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 2 jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P267F.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P267F.description: The internal temperature sensor of the control module shows intermittent jumps or dropouts. Module thermal protection may falsely activate or fail to activate when needed.

causes.cause: Cracked solder joint at internal sensor
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2680.title: Coolant Degassing Valve Control Circuit High
P2680.description: Voltage on the coolant degassing valve control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2681.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Control Circuit / Open
P2681.description: The controller cannot drive the engine coolant bypass valve A. The valve usually routes coolant around the radiator during warm-up; without it warm-up takes longer and emissions during the warm-up phase rise.

causes.cause: Open coil in bypass valve solenoid

P2682.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Low
P2682.description: Voltage on the coolant bypass valve A control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2683.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Control Circuit High
P2683.description: Voltage on the coolant bypass valve A control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2684.title: Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit / Open
P2684.description: The third actuator supply rail is open. All loads on this rail are powerless and report follow-on faults.

causes.cause: Blown fuse on the supply rail
Broken supply wire from main relay

P2685.title: Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit Low
P2685.description: The third actuator supply rail is below the expected voltage. Battery weakness, blown fuse, or excessive current draw collapses the supply.

causes.cause: Load on the rail shorted to ground
Battery condition causes voltage to drop
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2686.title: Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit High
P2686.description: The third actuator supply rail is above the expected voltage. Likely a charging system overvoltage or a short to a higher-voltage source.

causes.cause: Wiring shorted to a higher-voltage circuit
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2687.title: Fuel Supply Heater Control Circuit / Open
P2687.description: The controller cannot drive the diesel fuel filter or supply line heater. In cold weather diesel waxing can clog the filter.

P2688.title: Fuel Supply Heater Control Circuit Low
P2688.description: Voltage on the fuel supply heater control line is below the expected window. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2689.title: Fuel Supply Heater Control Circuit High
P2689.description: Voltage on the fuel supply heater control line is above the expected window. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P268A.title: Fuel Injector Calibration Not Learned/Programmed
P268A.description: After injector replacement the engine controller did not receive the per-injector flow calibration codes (IMA, ISA, IMV). Cylinder balance and emissions are out of tolerance.

causes.cause: Injector calibration codes not entered after replacement
Wrong codes entered for the wrong cylinder positions

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P268B.title: High Pressure Fuel Pump Calibration Not Learned/Programmed
P268B.description: After high-pressure pump replacement the engine controller did not receive the pump-specific calibration data. Rail pressure regulation runs from default values.

causes.cause: Pump calibration codes not entered after replacement

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P268C.title: Cylinder 1 Injector Data Incompatible
P268C.description: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 1 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software. Calibration was applied for the wrong injector type or family.

causes.cause: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P268D.title: Cylinder 2 Injector Data Incompatible
P268D.description: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 2 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.

causes.cause: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P268E.title: Cylinder 3 Injector Data Incompatible
P268E.description: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 3 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.

causes.cause: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P268F.title: Cylinder 4 Injector Data Incompatible
P268F.description: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 4 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.

causes.cause: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2690.title: Cylinder 5 Injector Data Incompatible
P2690.description: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 5 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.

causes.cause: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2691.title: Cylinder 6 Injector Data Incompatible
P2691.description: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 6 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.

causes.cause: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2692.title: Cylinder 7 Injector Data Incompatible
P2692.description: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 7 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.

causes.cause: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2693.title: Cylinder 8 Injector Data Incompatible
P2693.description: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 8 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.

causes.cause: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2694.title: Cylinder 9 Injector Data Incompatible
P2694.description: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 9 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.

causes.cause: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2695.title: Cylinder 10 Injector Data Incompatible
P2695.description: The flow calibration data programmed for cylinder 10 injector does not match the format expected by the controller software.

causes.cause: Replacement injector has different part number than software expects
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2696.title: Injector Data Incompatible
P2696.description: Generic counterpart to the cylinder-specific incompatibility codes. The injector calibration data set as a whole does not match the controller software.

causes.cause: Replacement injector set incompatible with software version
Calibration code format does not match controller version

P2697.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Circuit / Open
P2697.description: The 7th injector (HC dosing for DPF active regeneration) cannot be driven. Active regeneration cannot raise exhaust temperature, soot accumulates in the DPF.
symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2698.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Performance
P2698.description: The 7th injector responds to commands but does not deliver expected fuel during regeneration. Coking on the nozzle or worn pressure regulation reduces flow.

causes.cause: Fuel pressure to the dosing line out of tolerance

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P2699.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Circuit Low
P2699.description: Voltage on the 7th injector control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P269A.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Circuit High
P269A.description: Voltage on the 7th injector control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P269B.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Control Circuit / Open
P269B.description: The control line for the aftertreatment glow plug (used on some diesels to ignite injected HC during DPF regeneration) is open. Active regeneration cannot start.

causes.cause: Open coil in glow plug control relay

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P269C.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Control Performance
P269C.description: The aftertreatment glow plug control responds to commands but the resulting current draw is out of tolerance. Worn glow plug or high-resistance contact.

causes.cause: Worn glow plug element raises resistance

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P269D.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
P269D.description: Voltage on the aftertreatment glow plug control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P269E.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Control Circuit High
P269E.description: Voltage on the aftertreatment glow plug control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P269F.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Circuit / Open
P269F.description: The aftertreatment glow plug element itself is open. No current flows even with the relay closed.

causes.cause: Glow element burnt out from age or HC overload
Corroded terminal at the plug body

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P26A0.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Performance
P26A0.description: The aftertreatment glow plug heats but exhaust temperature does not rise as expected. Combustion of injected HC may not start.

causes.cause: Aged glow plug heats slowly or unevenly
HC supply from 7th injector below required

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P26A1.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Circuit Low
P26A1.description: The aftertreatment glow plug current is below expected. Either the element is partially open or supply is undersized.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P26A2.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Circuit High
P26A2.description: The aftertreatment glow plug current is above expected. Internal short reduces resistance. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Internal short in the glow plug element
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P26A3.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Range/Performance
