P26A3.description: The coolant bypass valve A responds to commands but the resulting coolant temperature behaviour is not as expected. Possibly stuck partially open or contaminated bore.

causes.cause: Weak return spring fails to close fully
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26A4.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit
P26A4.description: The position sensor on the coolant bypass valve A returns no usable signal. Closed-loop control of bypass position is lost.

P26A5.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P26A5.description: The bypass valve A position sensor reading does not correlate with commanded position. Sensor drift or worn linkage.

causes.cause: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn linkage between actuator and valve
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26A6.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Low
P26A6.description: The bypass valve A position sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26A7.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit High
P26A7.description: The bypass valve A position sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26A8.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P26A8.description: The bypass valve A position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P26A9.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Stop/Minimum Stop Performance
P26A9.description: During self-calibration the bypass valve A position sensor never reached the minimum mechanical stop. The position reference cannot be zeroed.

causes.cause: Sediment prevents valve from reaching minimum stop
Sensor not aligned with valve shaft

P26AA.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Maximum Stop Performance
P26AA.description: During self-calibration the bypass valve A position sensor never reached the maximum mechanical stop.

causes.cause: Sediment prevents valve from reaching maximum stop
Sensor not aligned with valve shaft

P26AB.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Stuck/Open
P26AB.description: The coolant bypass valve A is stuck in the open position. Coolant always bypasses the radiator, leading to overheating under load.

causes.cause: Valve seized open by sediment or wax

P26AC.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Control Circuit / Open
P26AC.description: The controller cannot drive the second coolant bypass valve. The associated cooling sub-loop cannot be regulated.

causes.cause: Open coil in bypass valve solenoid

P26AD.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Control Circuit Low
P26AD.description: Voltage on the second coolant bypass valve control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26AE.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Control Circuit High
P26AE.description: Voltage on the second coolant bypass valve control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26AF.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Stuck/Open
P26AF.description: The second coolant bypass valve is stuck in the open position. Coolant always bypasses the second radiator path.

P26B0.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Range/Performance
P26B0.description: The second coolant bypass valve responds to commands but the resulting coolant temperature behaviour is not as expected.

causes.cause: Weak return spring fails to close fully
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26B1.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Stuck Closed
P26B1.description: The coolant bypass valve A is stuck closed. Coolant cannot bypass the radiator during warm-up so warm-up takes longer and emissions in the warm-up phase rise.

causes.cause: Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B2.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Stuck Closed
P26B2.description: The second coolant bypass valve is stuck closed.

causes.cause: Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B3.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P26B3.description: The first fuel shutoff valve is commanded on but does not open. Fuel cannot reach the engine via this path.

causes.cause: Solenoid loses force from coil aging
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B4.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Stuck On
P26B4.description: The first fuel shutoff valve stays open when commanded closed. Fuel cannot be cut off via this path during a safety event.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B5.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P26B5.description: The second fuel shutoff valve is commanded on but does not open.

causes.cause: Solenoid loses force from coil aging
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B6.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit Stuck On
P26B6.description: The second fuel shutoff valve stays open when commanded closed.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26B7.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Control Circuit / Open
P26B7.description: The controller cannot drive the third coolant bypass valve.

causes.cause: Open coil in bypass valve solenoid

P26B8.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Control Circuit Low
P26B8.description: Voltage on the third coolant bypass valve control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26B9.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Control Circuit High
P26B9.description: Voltage on the third coolant bypass valve control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26BA.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Stuck/Open
P26BA.description: The third coolant bypass valve is stuck open.

P26BB.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Range/Performance
P26BB.description: The third coolant bypass valve responds to commands but the resulting coolant temperature behaviour is not as expected.

causes.cause: Weak return spring fails to close fully
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26BC.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Stuck Closed
P26BC.description: The third coolant bypass valve is stuck closed.

causes.cause: Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26BD.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Control Circuit / Open
P26BD.description: The controller cannot drive the fourth coolant bypass valve.

causes.cause: Open coil in bypass valve solenoid

P26BE.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Control Circuit Low
P26BE.description: Voltage on the fourth coolant bypass valve control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26BF.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Control Circuit High
P26BF.description: Voltage on the fourth coolant bypass valve control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26C0.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Stuck/Open
P26C0.description: The fourth coolant bypass valve is stuck open.

P26C1.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Range/Performance
P26C1.description: The fourth coolant bypass valve responds to commands but the resulting coolant temperature behaviour is not as expected.

causes.cause: Weak return spring fails to close fully
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26C2.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Stuck Closed
P26C2.description: The fourth coolant bypass valve is stuck closed.

causes.cause: Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26C3.title: Internal Control Module Transmission Range Sensor Performance
P26C3.description: The internal transmission range sensor inside the control module (used for redundancy on shift-by-wire systems) does not match the external sensor reading.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26C4.title: Internal Control Module Clutch Pedal Performance
P26C4.description: The internal clutch pedal interpretation logic in the control module does not match the external clutch switch state. Manual transmission start interlock or stop-start enable can misbehave.

causes.cause: Signal corruption between switch and ECU

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26C5.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit / Open
P26C5.description: The controller cannot drive the exhaust flow control valve A (used for exhaust acoustics, EGR boost, or aftertreatment heating).

P26C6.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit Low
P26C6.description: Voltage on the exhaust flow control valve A control line is below the expected window. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26C7.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit High
P26C7.description: Voltage on the exhaust flow control valve A control line is above the expected window. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26C8.title: Chassis Control Module 1 Requested MIL Illumination
P26C8.description: A chassis control module (typically active suspension, AWD coupling, or steering controller) has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.

causes.cause: Active DTC stored in the chassis module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request

P26C9.title: Chassis Control Module 2 Requested MIL Illumination
P26C9.description: A second chassis control module has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.

causes.cause: Active DTC stored in the chassis module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request

P26CA.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit / Open
P26CA.description: The controller cannot drive the main electric coolant pump. Without flow the engine and aftertreatment will overheat under load.

causes.cause: Broken control wire to the pump

P26CB.title: Engine Coolant Pump Performance/Stuck Off
P26CB.description: The main electric coolant pump is commanded on but does not run.

causes.cause: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26CC.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit Low
P26CC.description: Voltage on the engine coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26CD.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit High
P26CD.description: Voltage on the engine coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26CE.title: Engine Coolant Pump Overspeed/Air In System
P26CE.description: The coolant pump speed feedback is higher than the commanded value with no resistance from coolant. Indicates air in the cooling loop or low coolant level so the pump spins free.

causes.cause: Low coolant level due to leak or improper fill
Air pocket trapped in the cooling loop

P26CF.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage
P26CF.description: The integrated controller of the smart coolant pump reports a system voltage out of operating range.

causes.cause: Weak battery sags voltage under pump load

P26D0.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage Low
P26D0.description: The smart coolant pump module reports the system voltage below operating range. Pump output is reduced or disabled to protect the module.

causes.cause: Weak battery sags voltage under load

P26D1.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage High
P26D1.description: The smart coolant pump module reports the system voltage above operating range. Pump output is reduced or disabled to protect the module.

causes.cause: Alternator regulator failed to limit output
Load dump transient after disconnecting a heavy load

P26D2.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module Over Temperature
P26D2.description: The smart coolant pump controller has reached over-temperature. Sustained high duty or insufficient cooling air flow.

causes.cause: Sustained high duty cycle from cooling demand
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P26D3.title: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit
P26D3.description: The dedicated supply voltage line to the coolant pump module is faulty. Pump cannot operate without battery feed.

P26D4.title: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P26D4.description: The dedicated supply voltage to the coolant pump module is below operating range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Weak battery sags under pump current
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26D5.title: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit High
P26D5.description: The dedicated supply voltage to the coolant pump module is above operating range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Alternator regulator failed to limit output
Wiring shorted to a higher-voltage circuit
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26D6.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Control Circuit / Open
P26D6.description: The mechanical clutch on a belt-driven coolant pump (used to disengage the pump for fast warm-up) cannot be driven. Pump always engaged so warm-up takes longer.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26D7.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Performance/Stuck Off
P26D7.description: The coolant pump clutch is commanded on but does not engage. Coolant flow is missing under load, leading to overheating.

causes.cause: Worn friction surfaces enlarge air gap
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26D8.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Stuck On
P26D8.description: The coolant pump clutch remains engaged when commanded off. Pump runs continuously, slowing warm-up and increasing parasitic load.

causes.cause: Armature plate seized to the pulley face
Driver stuck on keeps clutch energised
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26D9.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Control Circuit Low
P26D9.description: Voltage on the coolant pump clutch control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26DA.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Control Circuit High
P26DA.description: Voltage on the coolant pump clutch control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26DB.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit / Open
P26DB.description: The active engine sound generator A (Active Sound Design or AVAS — Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System for EV/hybrid) cannot be driven. EV pedestrian warning sound or sport-mode engine sound is missing.

causes.cause: Open output stage in the sound amplifier

P26DC.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit Low
P26DC.description: Voltage on the sound generator A control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26DD.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit High
P26DD.description: Voltage on the sound generator A control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26DE.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit Performance
P26DE.description: The sound generator A circuit responds to commands but the resulting acoustic feedback is not as expected. Speaker damage or feedback path noise.

causes.cause: Speaker cone damaged or coil shorted

P26DF.title: Sensor Power Supply D Circuit / Open
P26DF.description: The 5 V supply rail D for sensors is open. All sensors fed from this rail report invalid readings.

causes.cause: Open wire on the supply rail
Open inside the ECU regulator output

P26E0.title: Sensor Power Supply D Circuit Low
P26E0.description: The 5 V supply rail D is below the expected level. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Sensor on the rail shorted internally to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E1.title: Sensor Power Supply D Circuit High
P26E1.description: The 5 V supply rail D is above the expected level. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Reference wire shorted to a B+ supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E2.title: Fuel Mode Indicator Lamp Control Circuit Low
P26E2.description: Voltage on the fuel mode indicator lamp control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E3.title: Fuel Mode Indicator Lamp Control Circuit High
P26E3.description: Voltage on the fuel mode indicator lamp control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E4.title: Starter Relay B Circuit
P26E4.description: The control circuit for the secondary starter relay (used on twin-starter heavy diesels or stop-start systems with a dedicated stop-start starter) returns no usable signal.

P26E5.title: Starter Relay B Circuit Low
P26E5.description: Voltage on the secondary starter relay control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E6.title: Starter Relay B Circuit High
P26E6.description: Voltage on the secondary starter relay control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E7.title: Actuator Supply Voltage D Circuit / Open
P26E7.description: The fourth actuator supply rail is open. All loads on this rail are powerless and report follow-on faults.

causes.cause: Blown fuse on the supply rail
Broken supply wire from main relay

P26E8.title: Actuator Supply Voltage D Circuit Low
P26E8.description: The fourth actuator supply rail is below the expected voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Load on the rail shorted to ground
Battery condition causes voltage to drop
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E9.title: Actuator Supply Voltage D Circuit High
P26E9.description: The fourth actuator supply rail is above the expected voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Wiring shorted to a higher-voltage circuit
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26EA.title: Fuel Pump Control Module B
P26EA.description: A general fault in the second fuel pump control module (smart pump controller, separate from the ECU). Internal self-test failed or communication with the ECU is degraded.

causes.cause: Internal fault in the pump module

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P26EB.title: Alternative Fuel Control Module System Voltage
P26EB.description: The alternative fuel control module reports a system voltage out of operating range. CNG, LPG, or hydrogen fuelling can be disabled until voltage is in spec.

causes.cause: Weak battery sags voltage under load

P26EC.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit / Open
P26EC.description: The second active sound generator (B) cannot be driven.

causes.cause: Open output stage in the sound amplifier

P26ED.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit Low
P26ED.description: Voltage on the sound generator B control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26EE.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit High
P26EE.description: Voltage on the sound generator B control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26EF.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit Performance
P26EF.description: The sound generator B circuit responds but the resulting acoustic feedback is not as expected.

causes.cause: Speaker cone damaged or coil shorted

P26F0.title: Starter Relay A Stuck On
P26F0.description: The first starter relay stays closed when commanded off. Starter motor remains engaged after the engine is running, which can destroy the starter pinion or ring gear.

causes.cause: Relay contacts welded shut by inrush current
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F1.title: Starter Relay A Stuck Off
P26F1.description: The first starter relay does not close when commanded on. Starter motor cannot crank, the engine will not start.

causes.cause: Burned relay contacts no longer make contact
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F2.title: Starter Relay B Stuck On
P26F2.description: The second starter relay stays closed when commanded off. Starter motor B remains engaged after the engine is running, which can destroy the starter pinion or ring gear.

causes.cause: Relay contacts welded shut by inrush current
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F3.title: Starter Relay B Stuck Off
P26F3.description: The second starter relay does not close when commanded on. The associated starter motor cannot crank.

causes.cause: Burned relay contacts no longer make contact
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F4.title: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit / Open
P26F4.description: The controller cannot drive the third electric coolant pump. Cooling demand of the connected loop (often hybrid power electronics or battery cooling) is not satisfied.

causes.cause: Broken control wire to the pump

P26F5.title: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit Low
P26F5.description: Voltage on the third coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.cause: Internal short in pump motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26F6.title: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit High
P26F6.description: Voltage on the third coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26F7.title: Coolant Pump C Supply Voltage Circuit
P26F7.description: The dedicated supply voltage line to the third coolant pump module is faulty. Pump cannot operate without battery feed.

P26F8.title: Coolant Pump C Stuck/Stalled
P26F8.description: The third coolant pump is commanded on but the rotor does not turn. Sediment, frozen coolant, or a foreign object jams the impeller.

causes.cause: Impeller jammed by sediment or debris
Pump motor seized by bearing failure

P26F9.title: Coolant Pump C Control Module Overtemperature
P26F9.description: The smart controller of the third coolant pump has reached over-temperature. Sustained high duty or insufficient cooling air flow around the pump electronics.

causes.cause: Sustained high duty cycle from cooling demand
Cooling air channel around pump blocked by debris

P26FA.title: Coolant Pump C Overspeed/Air in System
P26FA.description: The third coolant pump speed feedback is higher than commanded with no resistance from coolant. Indicates air in the cooling loop or low coolant level so the pump spins free.

causes.cause: Low coolant level due to leak or improper fill
Air pocket trapped in the cooling loop

P26FB.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Closed Bank 1
P26FB.description: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1 is stuck in the closed position. EGR gas always passes through the cooler, which slows engine warm-up and can degrade cold-start emissions.

causes.cause: Valve flap seized closed by soot
Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26FC.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Closed Bank 2
P26FC.description: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 2 is stuck in the closed position. EGR gas always passes through the cooler, slowing engine warm-up and degrading cold-start emissions.

causes.cause: Valve flap seized closed by soot
Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26FD.title: A/C Compressor Internal Control Module Performance
P26FD.description: The internal control module of an electrically driven A/C compressor (typical on hybrid and BEV vehicles) reports an internal performance fault. Compressor capacity may be reduced or shut down.

causes.cause: Internal fault in compressor inverter electronics
Software error in compressor control logic
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P26FE.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Performance
P26FE.description: The exhaust flow control valve A responds to commands but the resulting flow or back-pressure does not match expectations. Worn flap or carbon coking on the bore.

P26FF.title: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 2
P26FF.description: During controller auto-configuration the expected throttle input on bank 2 was not detected. Configuration cannot complete and the second throttle path cannot be used.

causes.cause: Broken signal wire from throttle B2
Hardware variant mismatch — sensor not installed

P2700.title: Transmission Friction Element A Apply Time Range/Performance
P2700.description: The transmission control module measured an apply time for friction element A (clutch or band) outside the calibrated window. Indicates worn clutch material, low line pressure, or a degrading shift solenoid.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2701.title: Transmission Friction Element B Apply Time Range/Performance
P2701.description: The time required to apply friction element B (a clutch or band inside the automatic transmission) is outside the expected window. Either too long (worn clutch, low pressure) or too short (sticky valve, mis-calibration).

causes.cause: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2702.title: Transmission Friction Element C Apply Time Range/Performance
P2702.description: The time required to apply friction element C is outside the expected window. Worn clutch, low pressure, or sticky valve.

causes.cause: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2703.title: Transmission Friction Element D Apply Time Range/Performance
P2703.description: The time required to apply friction element D is outside the expected window.

causes.cause: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2704.title: Transmission Friction Element E Apply Time Range/Performance
P2704.description: The time required to apply friction element E is outside the expected window.

causes.cause: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2705.title: Transmission Friction Element F Apply Time Range/Performance
P2705.description: The time required to apply friction element F is outside the expected window.

causes.cause: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2706.title: Shift Solenoid F
P2706.description: A general fault in shift solenoid F (the sixth gear-selection solenoid in 6-speed and higher transmissions). Detected through electrical resistance, hydraulic response, or downstream gear engagement check.

causes.cause: Worn valve body bore around the solenoid

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2707.title: Shift Solenoid F Performance/Stuck Off
P2707.description: Shift solenoid F is commanded on but does not produce the expected hydraulic response. Spool stuck closed or hydraulic apply circuit blocked.

causes.cause: Solenoid spool stuck in closed position
Apply circuit blocked by debris in valve body
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2708.title: Shift Solenoid F Stuck On
P2708.description: Shift solenoid F stays in the activated state when commanded off. Affected gear stays applied so the transmission cannot shift correctly.

causes.cause: Solenoid spool stuck in open position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2709.title: Shift Solenoid F Electrical
P2709.description: Electrical fault in shift solenoid F — open or shorted coil, or short to ground/battery in the harness.

causes.cause: Short to ground or battery in the harness

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P270A.title: Transmission Friction Element A Temperature Too High
P270A.description: Friction element A inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature. Excessive slip during shifts or trailer towing burns the clutch.

causes.cause: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P270B.title: Transmission Friction Element B Temperature Too High
P270B.description: Friction element B inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature.

causes.cause: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P270C.title: Transmission Friction Element C Temperature Too High
P270C.description: Friction element C inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature.

causes.cause: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P270D.title: Transmission Friction Element D Temperature Too High
P270D.description: Friction element D inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature.

causes.cause: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P270E.title: Transmission Friction Element E Temperature Too High
P270E.description: Friction element E inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature.

causes.cause: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P270F.title: Transmission Friction Element F Temperature Too High
P270F.description: Friction element F inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature.

causes.cause: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2710.title: Shift Solenoid F Intermittent
P2710.description: Shift solenoid F shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic faults that come and go. Loose connector or marginal coil.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2711.title: Unexpected Mechanical Gear Disengagement
P2711.description: The transmission disengaged mechanically without a corresponding command. The vehicle can free-wheel, which is a safety concern. Often a hydraulic or hardware fault inside the gearbox.

causes.cause: Clutch piston seal failure releases gear

P2712.title: Hydraulic Power Unit Leakage
P2712.description: The transmission hydraulic power unit (pump + accumulator) has detected a pressure drop that suggests internal leakage. Pressure cannot be held during shifts.

causes.cause: Worn or hardened seals in the valve body
Worn hydraulic pump cannot maintain pressure

P2713.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D
P2713.description: A general fault in pressure control solenoid D. Detected via electrical resistance, response to commanded duty cycle, or downstream pressure measurement.

causes.cause: Worn valve body bore around the solenoid

P2714.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Performance/Stuck Off
P2714.description: Pressure control solenoid D is commanded on but does not produce the expected pressure. Spool stuck closed or hydraulic feed restricted.

causes.cause: Solenoid spool stuck in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2715.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Stuck On
P2715.description: Pressure control solenoid D stays in the activated state when commanded off. Affected hydraulic circuit stays pressurised.

causes.cause: Solenoid spool stuck in open position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2716.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Electrical
P2716.description: The TCM detects an electrical fault on transmission pressure control solenoid D. Hydraulic pressure cannot be modulated as expected, causing harsh or slipping shifts.

P2717.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Intermittent
P2717.description: Pressure control solenoid D shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic faults. Loose connector or marginal coil.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2718.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit / Open
P2718.description: The control line to pressure control solenoid D is open. The solenoid cannot be driven.

P2719.title: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2719.description: The current through pressure control solenoid D does not match the commanded value within tolerance. Coil resistance drift or high-resistance contact.

causes.cause: Coil resistance changed by thermal stress
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P271A.title: Park Pawl Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P271A.description: The position sensor that confirms the park pawl A engagement state reads below the lower diagnostic threshold. Without confirmed park engagement the shift-by-wire controller cannot release the brake hold.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P271B.title: Park Pawl Position Sensor A Circuit High
P271B.description: The position sensor for park pawl A reads above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P271C.title: Park Pawl Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P271C.description: The redundant park pawl position sensor B reads below the lower diagnostic threshold. Redundancy for the park-engagement check is lost.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P271D.title: Park Pawl Position Sensor B Circuit High
P271D.description: The redundant park pawl position sensor B reads above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P271E.title: Transmission Performance
P271E.description: A general transmission performance fault. The transmission controller has detected behaviour outside acceptable bounds (slip, shift quality, ratio error) without a more specific cause.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P271F.title: Electronic Gear Shift - Position Not Learned
P271F.description: The shift-by-wire controller did not complete the position learning routine for the gear selector. Without learned end stops the controller cannot map selector positions to gear requests.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P28F4.title: Engine Disconnect Clutch Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P28F4.description: Voltage on the engine disconnect clutch pressure sensor signal line is above the expected window. Wire shorted to B+ or sensor open.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P28F5.title: Engine Disconnect Clutch Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P28F5.description: The engine disconnect clutch pressure sensor signal drops out or jumps intermittently. Loose connector or noisy ground reference.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P28F6.title: Engine Disconnect Clutch Actuator Circuit Intermittent
P28F6.description: The control circuit of the engine disconnect clutch actuator drops out intermittently. Loose connector or vibration-sensitive wiring.

causes.cause: Harness chafing intermittently shorts the wire
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P28F7.title: Exhaust Pressure Too High Bank 1
P28F7.description: The exhaust pressure measured on bank 1 exceeds the calibrated maximum. Common causes are clogged DPF, restricted exhaust path, or stuck exhaust brake/back-pressure valve.

causes.cause: DPF clogged with soot or ash

P28F8.title: Exhaust Pressure Too High Bank 2
P28F8.description: The exhaust pressure measured on bank 2 exceeds the calibrated maximum. Common causes are clogged DPF, restricted exhaust path, or stuck exhaust brake/back-pressure valve.

causes.cause: DPF clogged with soot or ash

P28F9.title: Exhaust Pressure Too Low Bank 1
P28F9.description: The exhaust pressure measured on bank 1 falls below the calibrated minimum. Common causes are leaks upstream of the sensor, missing DPF substrate, or sensor calibration drift.

P28FA.title: Exhaust Pressure Too Low Bank 2
P28FA.description: The exhaust pressure measured on bank 2 falls below the calibrated minimum. Common causes are leaks upstream of the sensor, missing DPF substrate, or sensor calibration drift.

P2A00.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2A00.description: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1: the signal is implausible or outside the valid range.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A01.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 2
P2A01.description: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 does not show the expected slow steady-state behaviour after the catalyst. Either the sensor is degraded or the catalyst itself behaves abnormally.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A02.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2A02.description: The optional third oxygen sensor on bank 1 (typically downstream of a second catalyst) returns implausible values during long-term monitoring.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A03.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2A03.description: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 reacts too slowly or shows insufficient signal swing during closed-loop fuel control.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A04.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 2
P2A04.description: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 shows abnormal behaviour during long-term plausibility evaluation. Often a sign of an aged sensor or weakened catalyst.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A05.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2A05.description: The third oxygen sensor on bank 2 (after a second catalyst stage on some vehicles) returns implausible values. Often related to sensor aging or mechanical exhaust leak upstream.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A06.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 4
P2A06.description: The fourth oxygen sensor on bank 1, where present, returns implausible values during long-term plausibility evaluation. Used on multi-stage aftertreatment systems.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A07.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 4
P2A07.description: The fourth oxygen sensor on bank 2 returns values outside the expected long-term performance window during plausibility checks.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A08.title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 3
P2A08.description: The ECM detects a negative voltage on the signal line of oxygen sensor 3 on bank 1. This is unusual for narrow-band sensors and often indicates a short to a negative reference, ground offset, or a wide-band sensor wired incorrectly.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to negative reference
Ground offset between sensor and ECM

P2A09.title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2A09.description: The ECM detects a negative voltage on the signal line of oxygen sensor 1 on bank 2. This is unusual for narrow-band sensors and often indicates a short to a negative reference, ground offset, or a wide-band sensor wired incorrectly.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to negative reference
Ground offset between sensor and ECM

P2A0A.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P2A0A.description: The ECM detects a generic fault on the secondary manifold absolute pressure sensor (MAP B). Air load estimation cannot be cross-checked.

P2A0B.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2A0B.description: The MAP B signal does not correlate with TPS, MAF, or RPM as expected. Vacuum leak, restricted port, or sensor drift.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2A0C.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P2A0C.description: Voltage on the MAP B signal line is below the expected window. Wire shorted to ground or sensor short.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2A0D.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P2A0D.description: Voltage on the MAP B signal line is above the expected window. Wire shorted to B+ or sensor open. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2A0E.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2A0E.description: The MAP B signal drops out or jumps intermittently. Loose connector or noisy ground reference. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2A0F.title: Fuel Supply Heater Performance
P2A0F.description: The fuel supply heater does not raise fuel temperature within the calibrated time window. Common in diesel and biofuel installations to prevent paraffin or fat crystallisation in cold weather.

P2A10.title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 2 Sensor 2
P2A10.description: The ECM detects a negative voltage on the signal line of oxygen sensor 2 on bank 2. This is unusual for narrow-band sensors and often indicates a short to a negative reference, ground offset, or a wide-band sensor wired incorrectly.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to negative reference
Ground offset between sensor and ECM

P2A11.title: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2A11.description: The ECM detects a negative voltage on the signal line of oxygen sensor 3 on bank 2. This is unusual for narrow-band sensors and often indicates a short to a negative reference, ground offset, or a wide-band sensor wired incorrectly.

causes.cause: Signal wire shorted to negative reference

causes.cause: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2A33.title: AFCM Power Relay Control Circuit Low
P2A33.description: Voltage on the AFCM power relay control line is below the expected window. Wire shorted to ground or coil short.

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2A34.title: AFCM Power Relay Control Circuit High
P2A34.description: Voltage on the AFCM power relay control line is above the expected window. Wire shorted to B+ or coil open.

P2A35.title: AFCM Power Relay Sense Circuit
P2A35.description: The AFCM detects a generic fault on the sense feedback line of its power relay. Relay state cannot be confirmed reliably.

P2A36.title: AFCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low

P2A37.title: AFCM Power Relay Sense Circuit High

Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2A3E.title: Alternative Fuel Delivery Error
P2A3E.description: The AFCM detects that alternative fuel delivery to the engine deviates from the commanded amount. Pump output, valve actuation, or injector flow does not match expectations.

P2A3F.title: Excessive Time to Enter Alternative Fuel Control
P2A3F.description: On bi-fuel vehicles, the AFCM cannot transition into alternative fuel control mode within the calibrated time window. Tank pressure low, vaporizer cold, or fuel quality limits the change-over.

causes.cause: Vaporizer not yet at operating temperature

P2A40.title: Alternative Fuel System - Injector Leakage to Rail Detected

causes.cause: Injector seal aged - external leak path

causes.cause: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2B91.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P2B91.description: The ECM detects a circuit high fault on the turbocharger/supercharger b temperature sensor. Reading cannot be used reliably for control.

Whistling or hissing sound from intake

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2B93.title: Wastegate Position Sensor A Exceeded Learning Limit
P2B93.description: The required adaptation offset for the wastegate position sensor A exceeds the calibrated learning window. Sensor or mechanism out of nominal range.

P2B94.title: Wastegate Position Sensor B Exceeded Learning Limit
P2B94.description: The required adaptation offset for the wastegate position sensor B exceeds the calibrated learning window. Sensor or mechanism out of nominal range.

P2B95.title: Cold Start Injection Pulse Performance
P2B95.description: During cold start, the ECM detects that the overall injection pulse performance does not match the calibrated cold-start strategy. Combustion stability is reduced during warm-up.

causes.cause: Injectors aged - flow drift across cylinders
Fuel rail pressure drifts during pulse

P2B96.title: Injection Pulse Performance
P2B96.description: The ECM detects that the overall injection pulse performance does not match the calibrated values. Combustion result deviates from expected fuelling behaviour.

causes.cause: Injectors aged - flow drift across cylinders
Fuel rail pressure drifts during pulse

P2B97.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P2B97.description: The required adaptation offset for the exhaust pressure control valve A position exceeds the calibrated learning window. Mechanical wear or sensor drift beyond compensation.

P2B98.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Supply Low
P2B98.description: The supply voltage to the exhaust pressure control valve A actuator is below the expected window. Fuse blown, supply wire shorted, or upstream regulator fault.

P2B99.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P2B99.description: The output driver for the exhaust pressure control valve A reports current or junction temperature above its protection threshold. Stalled actuator or short-circuit fault.

P2B9A.title: Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2B9A.description: The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) quality sensor signal drops out or jumps intermittently. Loose connector, dilution noise, or ground reference offset.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2B9B.title: Vehicle Conditions Incorrect for Particulate Matter Sensor Regeneration
P2B9B.description: The ECM detects that the vehicle is not operating in conditions suitable for the periodic PM sensor regeneration cycle. The sensor element cannot be cleaned and soot-mass measurement is paused.

causes.cause: Driving cycle too short for regen conditions

P2B9C.title: Coolant Pump A Stuck/Stalled
P2B9C.description: Coolant pump A reports a stuck/stalled condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

P2B9D.title: Coolant Pump A Supply Voltage Circuit
P2B9D.description: Coolant pump A reports a supply voltage circuit condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

P2B9E.title: Coolant Pump A Control Module Overtemperature
P2B9E.description: Coolant pump A reports a control module overtemperature condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

causes.cause: Ambient or under-bonnet temperature too high

P2B9F.title: Coolant Pump B Underspeed
P2B9F.description: Coolant pump B reports a underspeed condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

P2BA0.title: Coolant Pump C Underspeed
P2BA0.description: Coolant pump C reports a underspeed condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

P2BA1.title: Coolant Pump D Underspeed
P2BA1.description: Coolant pump D reports a underspeed condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

P2BA2.title: Engine Coolant Pump Stuck/Stalled
P2BA2.description: The engine coolant pump is mechanically stuck or has stalled. Coolant circulation through the engine is severely reduced or absent.

P2BA3.title: Starter/Generator Mechanical Performance
P2BA3.description: The hybrid control module detects that the integrated starter/generator does not deliver the expected mechanical torque or speed for the commanded operation. Belt slippage, bearing wear, or coupling fault.

P2BA4.title: Catalyst Feedgas Performance
P2BA4.description: The ECM detects that the exhaust gas composition reaching the catalyst (feedgas) deviates from the calibrated profile. Pre-cat O2 measurement and air-fuel control are inconsistent with engine operation.

causes.cause: Long-term fuel trim drifted out of nominal range

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2BA5.title: Particulate Filter Feedgas Performance
P2BA5.description: The ECM detects that the exhaust gas composition reaching the particulate filter (feedgas) deviates from the calibrated profile. Soot input rate cannot be modelled correctly, affecting regen scheduling.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2BA6.title: NOx Exceedance - SCR NOx Catalyst Performance
P2BA6.description: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to the SCR NOx catalyst. Conversion efficiency is degraded — aged substrate, sulphur poisoning, or thermal damage.

causes.cause: SCR catalyst substrate aged or contaminated
Thermal damage from prior over-temperature event

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2BA7.title: NOx Exceedence - Empty Reagent Tank
P2BA7.description: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to an empty reductant tank. SCR cannot dose AdBlue/DEF.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2BA8.title: NOx Exceedence - Interruption of Reagent Dosing Activity
P2BA8.description: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to interruption of reductant dosing. The injection valve, pump, or supply line is impaired.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2BA9.title: NOx Exceedence — Insufficient Reagent
P2BA9.description: The SCR system has detected that NOx emissions exceed the legal limit and the cause is traced to insufficient AdBlue/DEF dosing. Modern emission regulations require this fault to be reported separately so that operator-induced misuse (running an empty tank, diluting the fluid) is recorded.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2BAA.title: NOx Sensor Range/Performance (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P2BAA.description: The upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 returns values that are not plausible for the current operating point. NOx sensors are slow to warm up, sensitive to soot and water, and are a frequent failure on diesel SCR systems.

causes.cause: Sensor contaminated with soot or condensate
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2BAB.title: NOx Exceedence — Reagent System Performance
P2BAB.description: The SCR system has detected that NOx emissions exceed the legal limit and the cause is traced to a performance fault in the reagent dosing system — for example a slow dosing pump, a clogged injector, or a frozen line that is not yet caught by another DTC.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2BAC.title: NOx Exceedence - Insufficient Reagent Quality
P2BAC.description: The diesel exhaust aftertreatment system detects elevated NOx levels combined with abnormal reagent (AdBlue/DEF) consumption, indicating that the reagent quality is insufficient or contaminated. Many regions trigger driver inducement (limited restarts).
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2BAD.title: NOx Exceedence - Insufficient Reagent Consumption
P2BAD.description: The aftertreatment system detects elevated NOx emissions while reagent (AdBlue/DEF) consumption is below the expected level. Causes include clogged dosing injector, incorrect dosing rate or tampering.
symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2BAE.title: NOx Exceedence - EGR System
P2BAE.description: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to the EGR system. EGR flow is too low or absent under operating conditions where NOx reduction is required.

P2BAF.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2BAF.description: The heater sense feedback of NOx sensor 1 on bank 1 reports values that do not match expected operation. The sensor warm-up cycle does not behave as the diagnostic expects.

causes.cause: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2BB0.title: Alternative Fuel Consumption Too Low
P2BB0.description: The AFCM detects that alternative fuel consumption falls below the expected value for the active operating mode. Indicates injector clogging, leaks before injectors, or incorrect tank-fill correction.

P2BB1.title: Alternative Fuel Consumption Too High
P2BB1.description: The AFCM detects that alternative fuel consumption exceeds the expected value for the active operating mode. Indicates injector leakage, fuel pressure too high, or unmetered fuel loss.

P2BB2.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Empty
P2BB2.description: The AFCM detects that the alternative fuel tank is empty. Bi-fuel vehicles may switch to gasoline operation; mono-fuel vehicles cannot continue without refuel.

P2BB3.title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Performance
P2BB3.description: The ECM detects that the secondary fuel pump control circuit (typically used for high-load enrichment) does not respond as expected. Pump output, relay, or driver fault.
symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2BB4.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 4 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2BB4.description: The signal of engine coolant temperature sensor 4 drops out or jumps intermittently. Loose connector or noisy ground reference.

causes.cause: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P2BB5.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 5 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

P3464.description: The engine control module has detected a high voltage condition in the control circuit of the cylinder 8 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid. causes.cause: Solenoid or wiring shorted to power

P3465.title: Cylinder 8 Deactivation
P3465.description: The engine control module has detected a fault in the cylinder 8 deactivation system. Common in V8 engines with active fuel management — cylinder 8 cannot reliably switch state.

P3466.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 Open
P3466.description: The engine control module has detected an open hydraulic circuit in the cylinder deactivation system on bank 1. The system uses pressurized engine oil routed through dedicated lifters and oil control valves to collapse valves; an open circuit indicates loss of oil flow or a failed pressure switch.

causes.cause: Oil passage blocked or sludge buildup

P3467.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 Performance
P3467.description: The engine control module has detected a performance fault in the bank 1 hydraulic circuit used for cylinder deactivation. Oil pressure response or timing is outside the expected window during deactivation events, often caused by viscosity issues, internal leaks or worn lifters.

causes.cause: Incorrect oil viscosity or aged oil
Internal oil leak in deactivation circuit

P3468.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 Low
P3468.description: The engine control module has detected low oil pressure in the bank 1 hydraulic circuit responsible for cylinder deactivation. Below threshold pressure the lifters cannot collapse and the system disables further deactivation requests on bank 1.

P3469.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 High
P3469.description: The engine control module has detected an excessively high oil pressure or stuck-on signal in the bank 1 hydraulic circuit for cylinder deactivation. Either a stuck oil control valve, a blocked relief path, or a shorted pressure switch is reporting permanently high pressure.

P3470.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 2 Open
P3470.description: The engine control module has detected an open hydraulic circuit in the cylinder deactivation system on bank 2. Loss of oil flow, a failed oil pressure switch or a disconnected oil control valve prevents the system from deactivating cylinders on bank 2.

causes.cause: Oil passage blocked or sludge buildup

P3471.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 2 Performance
P3471.description: The engine control module has detected a performance fault in the bank 2 hydraulic circuit used for cylinder deactivation. Oil pressure response or actuation timing falls outside the expected window during deactivation events on bank 2, often caused by viscosity issues, internal leaks or worn switching lifters.

causes.cause: Incorrect oil viscosity or aged oil
Internal oil leak in deactivation circuit

P3472.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 2 Low
P3472.description: The engine control module has detected low oil pressure in the bank 2 hydraulic circuit responsible for cylinder deactivation. Below the calibrated threshold the switching lifters cannot collapse and cylinder deactivation on bank 2 is disabled until pressure recovers.

P3473.title: Cylinder 9 Deactivation
P3473.description: The engine control module has detected a fault in the cylinder 9 deactivation system. Found on V10/V12 engines with cylinder deactivation — cylinder 9 cannot reliably switch state.

P3474.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 2 High
P3474.description: The engine control module has detected an excessively high oil pressure or stuck-on signal in the bank 2 hydraulic circuit for cylinder deactivation. A stuck oil control valve, a blocked relief path or a shorted pressure switch is reporting permanently high pressure on bank 2.

P3475.title: Cylinder Deactivation Oil Pressure Switch Bank 1 Circuit
P3475.description: The engine control module has detected an electrical fault in the cylinder deactivation oil pressure switch circuit on bank 1. The switch confirms that hydraulic pressure has reached the level required to collapse the switching lifters; without a valid signal the system disables deactivation.

P3476.title: Cylinder Deactivation Oil Pressure Switch Bank 1 Performance
P3476.description: The engine control module has detected a rationality fault between commanded oil pressure and the bank 1 cylinder deactivation oil pressure switch state. The switch fails to change state at the expected pressure threshold during deactivation transitions.

causes.cause: Oil control valve slow to respond

P3477.title: Cylinder Deactivation Oil Pressure Switch Bank 2 Circuit
P3477.description: The engine control module has detected an electrical fault in the cylinder deactivation oil pressure switch circuit on bank 2. Without a valid signal the module cannot confirm that hydraulic pressure has reached the level needed to deactivate cylinders on bank 2.

P3478.title: Cylinder Deactivation Oil Pressure Switch Bank 2 Performance
P3478.description: The engine control module has detected a rationality fault between commanded oil pressure and the bank 2 cylinder deactivation oil pressure switch state. The switch fails to change state at the expected pressure threshold during deactivation transitions on bank 2.

causes.cause: Oil control valve slow to respond

P3479.title: Cylinder Deactivation Solenoid Bank 1 Control Circuit Open
P3479.description: The engine control module has detected an open circuit at the bank 1 cylinder deactivation solenoid. The solenoid routes oil pressure to the switching lifters; an open circuit prevents activation and the system disables deactivation requests on bank 1.

P3480.title: Cylinder Deactivation Solenoid Bank 2 Control Circuit Open
P3480.description: The engine control module has detected an open circuit at the bank 2 cylinder deactivation solenoid. The solenoid routes oil pressure to the switching lifters on bank 2; an open circuit prevents activation and the system disables deactivation requests on bank 2.

P3481.title: Cylinder 10 Deactivation

The receiving modules reject the data. Start authorisation may fail. Causes include a faulty sensor feeding the module, internal computation errors, a software or calibration mismatch after a repair, or bus interference corrupting the frames.

causes.cause: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptoms: Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
